artigo.texto: CATL remains the world’s largest electric vehicle battery supplier in 2026, ahead of BYD and LG Energy Solution. However, the competition extends beyond market share: battery prices, manufacturing efficiency, customer diversification and regional demand are determining which suppliers can grow profitably. Global battery installations reached 844.2 gigawatt-hours from January through August 2026, increasing 19.7 percent year on year. The figures cover batteries installed in registered battery-electric vehicles, plug-in hybrids and hybrid electric vehicles, rather than total battery production. For automakers, supplier selection connects vehicle affordability with dependable delivery, charging performance and long-term warranty support. CATL and BYD together supplied approximately 460.9 GWh, accounting for roughly 54.6 percent of installations. Seven Chinese suppliers held a combined 73.3 percent share. Growth varied sharply: CATL increased installations 25.2 percent, Gotion 47.1 percent, EVE 53.9 percent and REPT 126.3 percent. BYD grew 6.2 percent, while SK On declined 14.5 percent. These are eight-month results, not full-year rankings from Insight -SNE Research. CATL Combines Market Leadership With Financial Strength CATL’s 2025 annual results, released in March 2026, reported revenue of RMB 423.7 billion, up 17 percent, and net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 72.2 billion, up 42 percent. Lithium-ion battery sales reached 661 GWh, increasing 39 percent. These sales include applications beyond electric vehicles and therefore differ from SNE’s automotive installation figures. CATL reported 772 GWh of production capacity, with another 321 GWh under construction at year-end. Research and development spending reached RMB 22.1 billion, approximately 5.2 percent of revenue. The company also processed 210,000 tonnes of spent batteries and regenerated 24,000 tonnes of lithium salts. The combination of earnings, research spending and manufacturing scale gives CATL resources to develop products and expand internationally. Its challenge is to bring additional capacity online at a pace that matches commercially viable demand. BYD’s Integrated Model Creates a Different Advantage BYD combines battery manufacturing with vehicle production, allowing battery design and vehicle engineering to develop within the same group. Its Blade Battery uses lithium iron phosphate chemistry. LFP avoids nickel and cobalt in the cathode and is widely used where cost, durability and thermal stability are priorities. BYD’s structure can simplify coordination between vehicle platforms and battery supply. However, it also means battery deployment is closely linked to the performance of its own automotive business. For buyers comparing BYD with independent suppliers, the relevant questions extend beyond installation volumes. External supply availability, platform compatibility, commercial terms and production location determine whether a battery offering fits an automaker’s requirements. LG Energy Solution, Panasonic and SK On Face Different Demand Exposure LG Energy Solution and Panasonic recorded installation growth below the overall market, while SK On’s volumes contracted. These suppliers remain important because of their established vehicle programmes and manufacturing relationships. Their results illustrate how customer concentration and regional exposure can influence performance even when worldwide battery demand rises. The International Energy Agency notes that Tesla continues sourcing most of its EV batteries from established suppliers including Panasonic, LG Energy Solution and CATL, despite developing its own manufacturing capabilities. For suppliers, winning a vehicle programme creates an opportunity rather than a guaranteed production volume. Actual demand depends on vehicle sales, launch schedules and the customer’s decisions about battery sourcing. Battery Prices Show Why Chemistry Matters BloombergNEF’s 2025 battery price survey provides a cost benchmark for evaluating the market in 2026. Average lithium-ion pack prices fell 8 percent to $108 per kilowatt-hour. Battery-electric vehicle packs averaged $99/kWh, while chemistry averages across applications were $81/kWh for LFP and $128/kWh for nickel-manganese-cobalt batteries. Using those chemistry averages, an illustrative 60 kWh pack would cost approximately $4,860 with LFP or $7,680 with NMC—a difference of $2,820. This calculation is not a supplier quotation or a comparison of otherwise identical packs. China’s regional average was $84/kWh. North American and European prices were 44 percent and 56 percent higher, respectively, implying approximately $121/kWh and $131/kWh. Stationary-storage packs averaged $70/kWh, down 45 percent, demonstrating why automotive and storage battery prices should be compared separately. Lower Battery Costs Do Not Automatically Mean Cheaper Cars Battery purchasing costs influence vehicle economics, but retail prices also reflect manufacturing, electronics, distribution, taxes and financing. For an illustrative 75 kWh vehicle, a $10/kWh reduction in pack cost represents $750 in potential manufacturing savings. An automaker could use that saving to lower prices, improve margins or fund additional features. Likewise, a lower-priced chemistry is not automatically the best choice for every model. Energy density, pack size, charging behaviour and vehicle weight affect the final design. Suppliers that offer several suitable products can address more vehicle categories, while automakers must evaluate the complete battery system rather than the cell price alone. Manufacturing Capacity Exceeds 4 TWh The IEA Global EV Outlook 2026 battery analysis reports that global lithium-ion nameplate manufacturing capacity exceeded 4 terawatt-hours at the end of 2025, up approximately 30 percent. artigo.texto: Behind-the-Meter Power Offers Control, Flexibility and Speed for the AI Age Key Highlights - AI is driving data centers to rethink their relationship with power. - BESS helps data centers manage volatile AI compute loads and grid constraints. - UPS, BESS and on-site generation create a coordinated energy stack. - Virtual power plants can turn backup assets into strategic grid resources. - Energy-as-a-Service can reduce upfront costs for behind-the-meter infrastructure. For the last decade, the data center industry has been a quiet engine of the digital economy, but today, the explosive rise of AI is exacerbating power sourcing issues that must be solved to keep building at the speed of innovation. Electric Power Research Institute projects that data centers could consume as much as 17% of U.S. electricity by 2030, more than triple their current 4-5% share. This massive spike in demand is clashing directly with a severely constrained power grid. At the end of 2025, more than 2,060 GW of new generation and storage capacity was represented by projects actively seeking interconnection to the U.S. grid. In turn, data center operators are fundamentally rethinking their relationship with power, shifting from passive grid consumers to active, localized energy producers. Grid capacity is no longer the ceiling. Instead, the next chapter of digital infrastructure will be written behind the meter. Behind-the-meter (BTM) refers to energy assets located on the customer side of the utility connection, including battery systems, microgrids, generators, fuel cells, and distributed energy resources that can operate independently of grid constraints. The Role of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) While every data center developer face grid constraints, the industry’s two dominant business models are adopting distinctly different strategies to bypass the power bottleneck. Hyperscale Operators Hyperscale operators (tech giants like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft) utilize their massive balance sheets to secure gigawatt-scale capacity directly. Rather than acting as passive grid customers, hyperscalers are taking direct, active control of their energy supply chains. They negotiate custom, state-level tariffs directly with utilities, co-locate facilities next to large nuclear or baseload assets, and sign massive off-site Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs). Increasingly, hyperscalers are also deploying large-scale, on-site Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to bypass grid delays and accelerate their projects, or turning to behind-the-meter natural gas generation to provide additional power on-site. Colocation Providers In contrast, colocation providers lease space, power, and cooling to third-party tenants. Colos operate on a highly competitive, faster-to-market model where speed-to-revenue is the primary metric. Colocation facilities are geographically constrained, as their facilities must be located close to business hubs to minimize latency rather than simply next to remote power plants. Consequently, data center and colocation developers are increasingly integrating on-site, behind-the-meter energy solutions. In highly congested markets, BTM generation and battery storage can provide a path to power while developers wait for grid interconnection. In Virginia, for example, LS Power is pursuing a 300 MW data center project designed to receive power directly from its adjacent natural gas-fired Doswell power plant, creating a behind-the-meter supply arrangement that can help accelerate access to power. The New Coordinated Energy Stack: UPS + BESS + Generators Historically, a data center’s power architecture was passive, consisting of an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) to bridge 5-to-15 minutes of downtime and backup diesel generators to handle prolonged outages. AI has shattered this legacy design. Although many enterprise deployments still operate below 20 kW per rack, next-generation AI clusters are increasingly exceeding 100 kW per rack, with some designs targeting significantly higher densities. Furthermore, AI training runs create highly volatile, synchronized compute loads, causing electricity draw to spike and drop in massive, sub-second waves. To protect both sensitive computing equipment and the local grid from these fluctuations, operators are deploying a layered, grid-interactive energy stack: - UPS (Instant Protection): Positioned in series with the servers, the traditional UPS remains essential for providing millisecond-fast power conditioning and preventing data loss during transient voltage sags. - BESS (On-site Shock Absorber & Optimizer): Connected in parallel at the facility level, BESS acts as a real-time shock absorber. It smooths out volatile AI compute spikes, stores cost-effective off-peak power for use during peak hours, and participates in grid-balancing services. - On-site Generation (Long-Term Firm Power): Customer-sited generation, including natural gas microturbines, provides the ultimate firm baseload capacity, insulating the facility from grid failures for days or weeks. By layering these technologies, operators can stop treating their power systems like a pricey “insurance policy” that sits idle, and start using them as a smart, money-saving asset. By discharging on-site batteries during peak demand periods — a strategy known as peak shaving — operators can reduce the peak loads used to calculate demand charges, potentially lowering electricity costs significantly. Turning Backup Assets into Strategic Grid Partners Historically, backup diesel generators sat untouched, accumulating maintenance costs unless a blackout occurred. Today, utilities and data center operators are establishing mutually beneficial partnerships. Through Virtual Power Plants (VPPs), utilities can aggregate a data center’s distributed backup generators and BESS capacity into a single, software-controlled resource. artigo.texto: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has recently inaugurated two projects in Tamil Nadu. These projects are expected to support renewable energy integration ports and address growing demand for Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects in Tamil Nadu. One of the projects involves the development of port infrastructure across the country to help the shipping sector reach new heights. Tamil Nadu is expected to play an important role in this initiative. The central government has recently taken a significant decision In this direction with approximately Rs. 17,000 crore investment. The VOC Port in Thoothukudi is being developed into a mega container port and green energy hub. Once completed, the port will be able to accommodate even the ultra-large container vessels. This development is expected to help transform Tamil Nadu into a global hub for industry and transportation. BESS Project in Tamil Nadu Prime Minister Narendra Modi also laid the foundation stone for the 250 MW/500 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, on October 11, 2026. According to the tender, awarded to NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a subsidiary of NLC India Limited (NLCIL), last year, it would develop this project across Ottapidaram, Anuppankulam, and Kayathar. The systems are designed to support two full charging and discharging cycles daily, enabling them to manage peak power demand and improve energy availability during critical load periods. It will follow a Build-Own-Operate (BOO) model under which the company will receive financial assistance under the State component of the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme. Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) will procure the energy storage services from NIRL for a period of 12 years through a Battery Energy Storage Purchase Agreement (BESPA). About NLC India's 250 MW/500 MWh BESS Project The 500 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project was originally awarded to NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a subsidiary of NLC India Limited (NLCIL), following a tender issued by Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation Limited (TNGECL) in June 2025. It is the first large-scale energy storage initiative for NLCIL. The project involves the development of three standalone BESS units with a combined capacity of 250 MW/500 MWh. These units will be installed at three substations in Tamil Nadu—Ottapidaram, Anuppankulam, and Kayathar—each operating at 400/230/110 kV. The systems are designed to support two full charging and discharging cycles daily, enabling them to manage peak power demand and improve energy availability during critical load periods. The project will follow the Build-Own-Operate (BOO) model and was awarded through a tariff-based competitive bidding process. It will receive financial assistance under the state component of the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme. artigo.texto: A well-known local engineer said he's completely reimagined the concept of data centers — and he said it addresses just about every concern communities have expressed. Opposition to data centers has exploded almost as quickly as the industry itself. Channing Blackwell believes he's got the solution. Stream NBC4 newscasts for free right here, right now. “We're not putting off any pollution, we're not putting off any noise,” he said. Blackwell is a professional engineer, and whether or not you know his name, you know his work. His firm designed several monuments in D.C., including the National Museum of African American History and Culture. His father's company helped design the underground Metro system. When it came to looking at data centers, Blackwell said the solution was as easy as turning the problem upside down. “Once I put it underground, then I started really pushing on optimizing the building,” he said. He calls it “The Renaissance System.” Northern Virginia Northern Virginia news, events and updates “For 12 months, they've worked quietly fixated on three core principles: community security, environmental security, national security. That work gave birth to The Renaissance System,” a corporate video described the project. Buried below the ground, crowned by a berm adorned with solar panels, the subterranean data center concept would be powered by geothermal energy, relying on zero fossil fuel. At hyperscale, it would span 30 acres, cost less than half of the current hyperscale data center and be nearly as powerful as the largest data center currently operating in the U.S. — not to mention that Blackwell said it wouldn't need to plug into the electric grid. “People that are 20 miles down the road that are protesting the power lines — Are they really needed if you get rid of the above-ground data centers that are obsolete technology and go to something that we've designed?” he said. Just last week the U.S. Department of Energy released a report suggesting geothermal technology could solve one of the largest issues current data center design creates: heating and cooling. Blackwell explained that above ground, data centers struggle to keep the thermostat at a comfortable level for their servers, and it costs a lot of money to do it. Underground cooling comes naturally and requires zero community water. Blackwell said mother nature will work for us — all she requires is that we listen to her. “If you're sloppy with your design, she can't close it for you. But, if you're mindful, it's there,” he said. As Blackwell launches his Renaissance System, he's not the only game in town. Other companies around the country are working on similar projects. In fact, a company based in Texas just inked a deal with Google to provide geothermal energy to a data center out west. While the future of this technology has yet to be proven, one thing is certain: There are people hearing the concerns about the data center industry, and they are working on solutions. This Saturday, the Piedmont Environmental Council is hosting a march in Leesburg, calling for a statewide data center moratorium. News4 asked a council spokesperson about using geothermal energy to power data centers. The spokesperson was unfamiliar with the Renaissance System but said they hope it works.

artigo.texto: Diagnóstico de 90 dias vai mapear a infraestrutura do estado para disputar a instalação de empresas de tecnologia e data centers junto ao resto do Nordeste por Cynara Maíra Publicado em 12/10/2026, às 12h26 - Atualizado às 12h51 Estudo encomendado: Governo de Pernambuco e LIDE contrataram a Deloitte para fazer um raio-x da infraestrutura digital do estado em 90 dias. Financiamento privado: Os custos do levantamento são pagos pelas empresas Cavalcanti Petribu, Estratégica Engenharia e Dislub Equador. Secretarias envolvidas: Participam do projeto as pastas de Administração, Ciência e Tecnologia e Desenvolvimento Econômico. Objetivo: O documento vai apontar gargalos e orientar ações do governo para atrair empresas de tecnologia e investimentos privados. Lançamento: O encontro de apresentação ocorre nesta quarta-feira (14), às 10h30, na sede da Secti, no Bairro do Recife. O Governo de Pernambuco e o LIDE Pernambuco iniciam nesta semana a elaboração do Estudo Estratégico do Ecossistema de Infraestrutura Digital do estado. O levantamento, conduzido pela consultoria Deloitte com prazo de conclusão de 90 dias, vai traçar um diagnóstico técnico para orientar políticas públicas e atrair investimentos privados voltados à conectividade, inteligência artificial e centros de processamento de dados (Data Centers) no estado. A ideia é que o anúncio do início dos trabalhos ocorra nesta semana, na quarta-feira (14), como a primeira entrega formal da parceria entre o Governo do Estado e o Lide, após o início do acordo de cooperação técnica firmado em julho de 2026. A ideia é que o grupo de cooperação continue pelos próximos quatro anos. Na parte do Executivo, participarão as secretarias de Administração; Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação e a pasta de Desenvolvimento Econômico. No lado privado, bancarão os custos o Grupo Cavalcanti Petribu, a Estratégia Engenharia e o Grupo Dislub Equador. A partir das conclusões da Deloitte, a gestão estadual pretende definir prioridades para modernizar a rede, ampliar a conectividade e aumentar a competitividade econômica local. Quando o relatório for entregue, os dados ficarão disponíveis para consulta pública. A apresentação oficial do estudo acontece nesta quarta-feira (14), às 10h30, no auditório da Secti, no Bairro do Recife. O encontro reúne as titulares das secretarias envolvidas, lideranças do LIDE e dirigentes das empresas que patrocinam o projeto. O Lide Pernambuco é uma organização empresarial que reúne diversas empresas do estado que defendem o fortalecimento do ambiente de negócios e o desenvolvimento econômico do estado. Parte do acordo de cooperação técnica com o estado já previa o incentivo a projetos nas áreas de conectividade, data centers sustentáveis, atração de investimentos e desenvolvimento da economia digital no estado.

artigo.texto: Mercado global de coletores de calha parabólica: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Mercado global de coletores de calha parabólica deve se expandir até 2035, impulsionado pela demanda por armazenamento de energia térmica Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Coletores de Calha Parabólica, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de coletores de calha parabólica (PTC, na sigla em inglês) entra em uma fase de renovada importância estratégica, à medida que os sistemas de energia priorizam capacidade renovável despachável. Diferentemente dos sistemas fotovoltaicos, os coletores de calha parabólica integram armazenamento de energia térmica de custo competitivo, o que permite gerar eletricidade ou fornecer calor industrial além das horas de luz solar. Este relatório analisa o mercado de 2026 a 2035, abrangendo conjuntos completos de coletores, espelhos, tubos receptores, estruturas de suporte e sistemas de rastreamento. A análise identifica as usinas CSP de escala utilitária como o principal uso final, enquanto o calor de processo industrial, o aquecimento distrital, a dessalinização e a recuperação avançada de petróleo oferecem caminhos de diversificação. O cenário competitivo reúne empresas de engenharia consolidadas e fabricantes especializados de componentes. A dinâmica regional é moldada pela qualidade do recurso solar, pelo apoio de políticas públicas e pelas capacidades de fabricação locais. O cenário-base da previsão pressupõe continuidade moderada das políticas, queda dos custos tecnológicos e reconhecimento crescente do valor do armazenamento de longa duração. Os principais riscos incluem a concorrência de sistemas fotovoltaicos com baterias, atrasos no licenciamento e concentração da cadeia de suprimentos. O relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados para fabricantes, empreiteiras EPC, investidores e formuladores de políticas que atuam nesse mercado em evolução. O cenário-base para o mercado de coletores de calha parabólica de 2026 a 2035 prevê uma expansão moderada, porém constante, com taxa de crescimento anual composta de 4,2% em termos reais. Essa perspectiva se ancora na proposta de valor singular dos coletores de calha parabólica: a capacidade de armazenar energia térmica em escala, oferecendo eletricidade e calor despacháveis que complementam as fontes renováveis variáveis. O crescimento da demanda não repetirá o boom impulsionado por subsídios da década de 2010; será movido, isso sim, por projetos integrados de energia, configurações híbridas e mandatos de descarbonização industrial. As usinas CSP de escala utilitária continuarão sendo o maior segmento, mas sua participação diminuirá gradualmente à medida que as aplicações de calor de processo industrial e aquecimento distrital ganharem tração. Avanços tecnológicos, como receptores de maior temperatura e sistemas avançados de sais fundidos, aumentarão a eficiência e reduzirão o custo nivelado. Restrições na cadeia de suprimentos de componentes especializados, como tubos receptores evacuados, podem moderar o crescimento em determinados anos. Geograficamente, Oriente Médio e África, junto com a Ásia-Pacífico, responderão pela maior parte das novas adições de capacidade, apoiadas por planos nacionais de diversificação energética. América do Norte e Europa terão implantação seletiva, muitas vezes vinculada a projetos de pesquisa ou híbridos. O índice de mercado, com 2025 como ano-base em 100, deve alcançar 151 até 2035, refletindo o crescimento acumulado. Esse cenário-base pressupõe ausência de reversões políticas relevantes e queda gradual dos custos de capital, em linha com as curvas de aprendizado históricas. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores de Demanda - Crescimento da demanda por energia renovável despachável, impulsionado por requisitos de estabilidade da rede e pela integração de geração solar e eólica variável. - Adoção crescente de soluções de calor de processo industrial, à medida que os fabricantes buscam descarbonizar a produção de vapor em alta temperatura. - Políticas e incentivos governamentais de apoio à implantação de energia solar concentrada, incluindo leilões e créditos fiscais em regiões de cinturão solar. - Redução de custos na integração do armazenamento de energia térmica, ampliando a competitividade econômica dos sistemas de calha parabólica. - Expansão de projetos híbridos solar-gás e solar-dessalinização, sobretudo no Oriente Médio e no Norte da África. - Foco crescente no armazenamento de energia de longa duração para viabilizar o fornecimento renovável ininterrupto. Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Concorrência intensa de sistemas fotovoltaicos com armazenamento em baterias, que registraram rápida queda de custos e prazos de implantação mais curtos. - Altos custos de capital iniciais e longos prazos de desenvolvimento das usinas CSP de escala utilitária, o que desestimula parte dos investidores. - Disponibilidade limitada de componentes especializados, como tubos receptores evacuados, criando gargalos na cadeia de suprimentos. - Incerteza regulatória e mecanismos de apoio inconsistentes em mercados-chave, afetando os pipelines de projetos. - Consumo de água para resfriamento nas usinas CSP convencionais, uma restrição em regiões áridas com escassez hídrica. artigo.texto: Websites down and bots disabled: The unexpected consequences of bombing data centers The militaries of Ukraine, Russia and Iran have launched several waves of attacks on these facilities, causing billions of dollars in losses and, in some cases, the permanent destruction of data Ukraine has struck a major blow to Russia’s digital infrastructure. Since last Thursday, Ukrainian drones have carried out a series of attacks that destroyed three large data centers belonging to Yandex — known as “the Kremlin’s Google”— on the outskirts of Moscow. The Yandex Taxi ride-hailing app and the group’s payments service, Yandex Pay, have been temporarily taken offline. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy even said the bombings disabled Russian bots. This is not the first time a regular army has targeted data centers. According to repeated complaints by Kyiv, Moscow has been doing so since March. And before Russia, Iran did it as well. On February 28, after coming under attack from the U.S. and Israel in the bombings that marked the start of the war, Tehran used drones to destroy three commercial Amazon Web Services (AWS) data centers in the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. The attack disrupted regional cloud services and affected payment systems across the Persian Gulf. It also triggered a cascading effect that was felt across several AWS availability zones, including in various countries in the Americas and along the U.S. East Coast. The fact that Russia and Ukraine are destroying each other’s data infrastructure, and that Iran chose to strike these facilities as soon as the war began (there have also been reports of bombings in the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia), shows that data centers are increasingly in the crosshairs. “Data centers are secondary targets, right after the obvious military sites,” Matt McCrann, a former executive at counter-drone firm DroneShield with experience in the United States and the Middle East, told Forbes. It also illustrates another point in Iran’s case: in the modern era, not even a distance of 7,000 miles guarantees immunity from retaliation. “The attacks showed that physical distance from a conflict zone is no guarantee of insulation from the impacts of kinetic warfare,” says Tomáš Foltýn, an analyst at the cybersecurity company ESET. The Iranian strike on the three AWS data centers did more than disrupt services in the Middle East and elsewhere, including the United States, where platforms such as Snowflake, Anthropic’s Claude, and some financial applications experienced outages or degraded performance. The drones also permanently destroyed some of the data stored in those facilities, something that does not appear to have occurred in the case of the Russian data centers. The attack served as a reminder that so-called cloud computing is ultimately just a metaphor. Far from being ethereal, it relies on physical infrastructure. And when that infrastructure fails, everything can be lost. A new military target Data centers are the guts of the cloud: highly sophisticated facilities resembling industrial warehouses, packed with racks of servers, essentially computers as tall as wardrobes. These processors run software remotely, including streaming services, and store data such as files saved online. This infrastructure is essential to the functioning of online services, from email and word-processing applications to banking platforms. If data centers did not store files and run software remotely, all of that computing power and storage would have to reside on users’ devices themselves. Smartphones would be incapable of doing nearly as much as they do today, and we would likely have to carry portable hard drives wherever we went. In recent years, data centers have taken on a third role in addition to running software and storing data: training and operating artificial intelligence models, which requires equipping facilities with far more powerful microprocessors that also consume much more energy. That helps explain why academic Eliezer Yudkowsky, concerned that AI systems could one day rebel against humanity, has suggested humanity “be willing to destroy a rogue data center by airstrike” in countries that refuse to limit the computing power available to such systems. Because they are highly technology-intensive facilities that also require an uninterrupted power supply, data centers are among the most expensive pieces of infrastructure in existence. And that makes them an attractive target. “Attacking them makes a lot of sense from an Iranian military perspective. They are multibillion-dollar investments that emerged after Trump’s visit early in his term and are tied to other personal business interests of Trump and his family in the region,” says Colonel Ángel Gómez de Ágreda, author of Un mundo falaz. El nuevo orden global en la era de los algoritmos y la manipulación (A False World: The New Global Order in the Age of Algorithms and Manipulation). Gómez de Ágreda agrees that data centers are already among military targets. “One could also argue that data centers are legitimate [noncivil] targets, since they provide support to military operations,” he says. Permanent data loss Any company can rent server space from a cloud provider to store its data. AWS is the global market leader, with a 28% share, followed by Microsoft Azure (21%) and Google Cloud (14%), according to data from Synergy Research Group. Companies generally choose data centers located as close as possible to the markets they serve in order to reduce latency, the time it takes for data to travel from a device to a server and back. One of the keys to Netflix’s expansion, for example, was signing long-term agreements with AWS, allowing it to rely on the company’s global infrastructure so that its streaming service performed reliably in virtually every country. artigo.texto: Once upon a time in the high-stakes world of clean energy procurement, a project team sat around a conference table, staring at a massive, complex document: the Energy Storage Contract Alliance (ESCA) Model Supply and Purchase Agreement. To the untrained eye, a utility-scale battery contract looks like a dry maze of legal jargon.But to the lead developer and the chief technical officer, this wasn't just paper. It was the superhero blueprint that turned a chaotic market into an accessible, bulletproof project. This is the problem that is sought to be solved with a model BESS contract from ESCA. Buyers representing 40 GWh of utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) projects have launched the Energy Storage Contract Alliance (ESCA) and published an open model contract for buying utility-scale BESS. The contract is meant as a common reference for developers, EPCs, independent power producers, asset owners, and battery manufacturers and integrators. ESCA's twenty-two members are utilities, independent power producers, project developers and asset owners with projects worldwide, including Goldbeck Solar, Neoen, ILOS, Pacifico Energy and Eiffage. Anyone, buyer or supplier, can read the core contract free of charge. Members get the full agreement and its technical appendices. The market is growing fast. Global BESS shipments rose about 75% to around 420 GWh in 2025, and InfoLink Consulting expects around 600 GWh in 2026. Contract terms have not kept up. Many projects still start from a blank page or from one party's own template, and topics such as cell traceability, serial defects, inspection sampling and cybersecurity are handled unevenly. A common reference draft can cut drafting time and transaction costs for both sides and make offers easier to compare. A public baseline also lets suppliers respond to tenders against known requirements, and lets smaller developers negotiate on the same footing as large utilities. "Every BESS project works through the same technical and contractual questions, and most of the answers are not project-specific," said Arthur Claire, Secretary General of ESCA. "Those answers used to stay in each company's drawer. ESCA puts a complete baseline in the open, so any developer, utility or manufacturer can take it, use the parts that fit and ignore the rest." The model contract covers technical specifications, factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, warranties, payment and price-adjustment mechanisms, and cybersecurity. More than fifteen technical appendices set out requirements at system, rack, pack and cell level. The contract sets no prices, price levels or discounts. These remain entirely for each buyer and supplier to negotiate. Sinovoltaics, ESCA's technical secretariat, drafted the first version as a baseline for members to build on. Users can adopt it in full, in part or not at all, and can change any clause. Members can comment on each clause, and the Steering Committee decides on revisions. The Steering Committee includes MN8 Energy, Neoen, Fortum and Munich RE. "As the energy storage sector is witnessing increasingly large procurement processes that often focus on the lowest possible costs, this race-to-the-bottom approach may undercut vital contractual and procurement-related practices and threaten the viability of a BESS project," commented Naim El Chami, Battery Technical Expert at Neoen and a member of the ESCA Steering Committee. Here is how the ESCA model agreement turns confusing legal hurdles into pure peace of mind for energy buyers. For the full contract, see end of story. Act I: The Shield of Traceability and Quality In years past, buying a massive battery system meant placing an order and praying that the manufacturer didn’t swap out high-grade components for cheaper alternatives halfway through production. Enter Clause 4.3 (The Designated Cell) and Clause 4.5 (Traceability Requirements). The contract acts as a digital ledger that locks down the exact cell chemistry, model, and physical factory site down to the individual serial number. When the CTO's team wants to know where their hardware came from, they don’t get vague promises but a transparent, machine-readable as-built register linking every single container directly to its manufacturing batch. Even better, Clause 4.4 (Change Control) guarantees that the supplier can’t change so much as a line of firmware or a bracket on the enclosure without the buyer’s written blessing. For buyers, this turns what used to be a nerve-wracking "black box" into a crystal-clear glass house. Act II: The Gift of Total Data Visibility (Or, How Buyers Can Stop Worrying and Love the Telemetry) Fast forward to Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT). Normally, a buyer receives a summary PDF signed by the factory manager saying, "Trust us, it passed." Not under this agreement. Clause 5.1.8 and Clause 6.6 (Data Monitoring) hand the keys to the kingdom over to the buyer. The contract mandates 1-second interval raw data streams covering voltage, current, and temperature for every single cell during testing and operation. Through Clause 6.5 (Battery Analytics Solutions), independent software monitors the battery's health in real time. The contract explicitly states that the buyer owns all generated data, can access it without paying hidden subscription fees, and never has to rely on the vendor's cloud servers just to check if their asset is running safely. It makes world-class quality control as accessible and simple as checking a smartphone app. Act III: The Guarantee That Keeps on Giving (Or, The 15-Year Safety Net) As the project approaches commercial operation, the financial team usually asks the scariest question of all: "What happens five or ten years from now when these cells degrade or a component breaks?" This is where the ESCA agreement shows its true beauty through a stacked defense of buyer-friendly guarantees: - The Single Point of Responsibility (Clause 7.1.4): The seller can’t point fingers

artigo.texto: Resumo O Governo Federal trabalha para expandir o modelo de desenvolvimento de data centers implementado no Ceará para todos os estados da Região Nordeste. Siga o canal de Economia no WhatsApp para ficar bem informado A informação foi divulgada pelo ministro das Comunicações, Frederico Siqueira, no último sábado, dia 10, ressaltando o potencial do Nordeste para se consolidar como um hub digital de alcance global. Segundo o ministro, a Região reúne as condições centrais buscadas por investidores internacionais para a instalação de grandes centros de processamento de dados e inteligência artificial. O movimento apoia-se em três pilares estratégicos identificados no ecossistema cearense: Confira os assuntos econômicos no Ceará, no Brasil e no Mundo Estudos da Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV) citados pelo titular das Comunicações apontam que a implantação de um único data center focado em inteligência artificial no Complexo do Pecém tem potencial de mobilizar até R$ 25 bilhões em investimentos. O impacto econômico prevê a geração de 12,5 mil empregos durante a fase de construção e a criação de 1.860 postos de trabalho permanentes na operação do empreendimento. A iniciativa citada pelo ministério insere-se no contexto de investimentos de grande porte atracados no Ceará. O empreendimento em desenvolvimento no Pecém é o primeiro de um conjunto de cinco data centers autorizados a operar na Zona de Processamento de Exportação (ZPE) do Ceará. Acompanhe mais notícias de Economia no Linkedin do O POVO No total, o projeto global está avaliado em R$ 200 bilhões e tem como cliente final a gigante chinesa ByteDance, controladora do TikTok. Desenvolvido pela Omnia, o primeiro centro de dados contará, apenas em sua fase inicial, com uma capacidade instalada de processamento de 200 megawatts (MW). O volume é expressivo quando comparado ao cenário nacional atual: somados, todos os data centers em operação no Brasil possuem cerca de 700 MW de capacidade. Veja dicas rápidas sobre Educação Financeira no Dei Valor Assim, a entrada em operação do primeiro módulo no Pecém representará, sozinha, um incremento de 28,5% na infraestrutura de processamento de dados de todo o País. Já o projeto do data center da Voltalia no Pecém, em Caucaia, está com a licença prévia em análise pela Superintendência Estadual do Meio Ambiente (Semace) e priorizará a utilização de água de reúso. A informação foi divulgada pela Zona de Processamento de Exportação (ZPE) em agosto. Operado pela multinacional francesa, o empreendimento ocupará 62 hectares na região, o que equivale a 87 campos de futebol. O investimento total previsto é de R$ 181,7 bilhões em quatro anos, com uma geração de 2.300 empregos diretos na construção e 400 durante a operação. Além disso, conforme a ZPE, a estrutura exigirá expansão de usinas eólicas e solares. Demais informações, entretanto, não puderam ser divulgadas, devido ao “estrito cumprimento às normas de compliance e à legislação vigente”. “A ZPE Ceará esclarece que, em estrito cumprimento às normas de compliance e à legislação vigente, está legalmente impedida de divulgar dados comerciais, operacionais ou financeiros de empresas instaladas ou em processo de instalação na ZPE”, informou.

artigo.texto: Global law firm Dentons has advised PPF banka a.s. in connection with the financing of the construction and development of the 72 MW BESS Frasinet 1 battery energy storage system project in Romania. Dentons said this mandate highlights its capabilities in cross-border project finance and energy infrastructure, combining Czech and Romanian financing, security, real estate, and energy advice to support the development of battery energy storage capacity in Romania.

artigo.texto: Danville has added more than 100 housing units to its market since 2023, with over 200 more in construction. In Pittsylvania, a master-planned community will soon add more than 1,800 units to the county’s housing stock. It’s still not enough, local officials say. Danville and Pittsylvania County are experiencing unprecedented levels of growth, for which the housing market wasn’t prepared. Job creation in the region, which is driving the increase in demand for housing, has picked up rapidly in recent years, after decades of job losses tied to the declining tobacco and textile industries. Large facilities locating at industrial parks in the region are expected to create thousands of jobs in the coming years. The Berry Hill megasite, the largest industrial site in the state, will soon be home to lithium-ion battery separator manufacturer Microporous. Microporous has promised to create about 2,000 new jobs. And data center developer Stack Infrastructure is promising about 2,500 permanent jobs at an AI data center facility that is also expected to come to the Berry Hill site, though there has been no formal announcement. Close to 1,000 new housing units are needed to support the Microporous project alone, according to the Danville Housing Navigator. The workers will need places to live, said Linda Green, executive director of the Southern Virginia Regional Alliance, a regional economic development group. That’s why local development group Southside Investing is building a massive master-planned community development in Axton, nine miles from the megasite. Tony Salah, with Southside Investing, said the group “has been actively preparing to meet the housing demand of future jobs.” The 590-acre development, called Sugar Tree Living, will create more than 1,800 units across all housing types — single-family, apartments, townhomes and senior living. Salah joined other developers, along with real estate professionals, builders, bankers and economic development officials in Danville on Thursday for the fifth annual Southern Virginia Regional Housing Summit. At the event, Green said that housing demand in the region has increased even since 2022, when a study identified a pent-up demand for about 600 single-family homes and 700 apartment units in Danville. “Housing has been built, new projects have been announced and our economic development pipeline has changed substantially,” she said. “But the projections for tomorrow change even faster and more drastically.” Since the study was released, the city has built 112 rental units and 16 for-sale units, with 233 more units in construction. Despite this, the demand has continued to grow, according to a 2025 update to the study. Pent-up demand in the city now calls for nearly 4,000 rental units and 1,300 owned units, said Susan McCulloch, Danville’s director of housing and development. Housing is now seen as a key part of economic development, Green said. Companies always ask about housing when considering whether to locate in an area, she said. “They’re going to ask the housing question, and if you don’t have a solution for it, you can’t win the project,” Green said. “That’s why we increasingly view housing as workforce and economic development infrastructure. You no longer see a division between the departments.” Salah echoed this sentiment, calling the housing deficit “the overwhelming regional refrain of need.” The Pittsylvania County Board of Supervisors approved the Sugar Tree Living project in 2023, over a year before the Microporous announcement, anticipating that a major housing development would be needed to support eventual jobs at the megasite. On top of 1,800 housing units, the development will also offer amenities like healthcare, childcare, retail, dining, hospitality and recreation, and services like on-site fire and rescue. When it was approved, the master-planned community drew some pushback from residents about traffic, loss of agricultural land and the natural beauty of the county, and the possibility that the development could kickstart a chain of similar developments. Microporous locating at the megasite “validated our time and energy and dollars into this area,” Salah said in a 2024 interview after the company’s announcement. “We want to be the supply solution for a portion of the housing demand,” he said then. After Thursday’s housing summit, Salah added that Southside Investing is feeling “more and more confident that an abundant wave of well-paying, good jobs are closer than ever.” A second tenant at the megasite — and thousands of additional jobs — is on the horizon, with data center developer Stack Infrastructure planning to build an AI data center campus on nearly 3,000 acres at the site. A local performance agreement for the project outlines Stack’s promise of $1.3 billion in investment and more than 2,000 permanent jobs. “The housing implication is clear,” Green said. “We must prepare for both permanent employment growth and the workforce needed to construct and equip these growing facilities.” Information about the region’s housing needs, current projects and available sites can be found on the Danville Housing Navigator website.

Highlands West is expected to be built over Dauphin Highlands Golf Course at 650 South Harrisburg Street. Highlands East would be at 4951 Highland Street, according to preliminary plans from the developers. READ MORE | Dauphin County golf course will turn into data center after $45.6M sale The total of $120.3 million in contributions will be split between the following initiatives, the board said. - $38 million to build a joint police and fire headquarters and emergency operations center - $27 million in restricted long-term funding for roads, public works equipment, snow removal, facilities, parks, technology, capital reserves and debt and service stabilization. - $24 million for a second public safety facility, which would include a fire station, police substation, EMS support and a backup emergency operations center - $12 million to fund career firefighter positions, recruitment and retention, firefighter pension funding, and future police, public works and code enforcement staffing - $8 million for fire apparatus replacement - $4 million for operating-cost stabilization, including residential trash collection, assistance for seniors, veterans and residents in hardship, fee stabilization and taxpayer-impact mitigation - $3 million for a municipal training facility for fire, police and EMS training, emergency-response exercises and emergency-management preparedness - $3 million to replace patrol vehicles, make technology and communications upgrades and for equipment for criticial infrastructure protection. - $1 million for scholarships for township residents and training programs to support data center workforce readiness - $300,000 for solicitor, engineer and consulting fees The contributions will be paid in installments based on development milestones, the township said.

artigo.texto: Peugeot has revived the RCZ nameplate with the RCZ Vision concept car, showcasing the brand’s new design language for a coupé based on the STLA One platform, featuring a solid-state battery and a 1,000-volt electrical architecture. The RCZ Vision concept’s powertrain is claimed to output 500 hp and deliver up to 600 km of range with a claimed energy consumption figure of 11.5 kWh per 100 km, and its solid-state battery is said to to be able to be recharged from 10-80% in just 10 minutes, according to Peugeot. The RCZ Vision concept is Peugeot’s first expression of its “Feline Future” direction that will inform the design of future Peugeot models. According to Autocar, the RCZ Vision concept measures 4.65 m long, 1.35 m tall and 1.94 m wide, while its rolling stock is a set of forged aluminium wheels measuring 21 inches and 22 inches in diameter front and rear, respectively. Its cabin is designed to be a true four-seater, rather than the 2+2 configuration of its discontinued production namesake, and the RCZ Vision concept aims to accommodate two adults comfortably in the second row. The double-bubble roof of the previous RCZ has been rethought to optimise rear-seat headroom, while adding light to the cabin. Further maximising interior space is the RCZ Vision’s battery, which measures just 110 mm thick in order to retain a low floor and low-profile silhouette. Practicality and usability were priorities for the design team when designing the new RCZ Vision, as to maximise the likelihood of the car being adapted to production, said Peugeot design director Matthias Hossann. “This was an important part of my brief. I asked my team to make it look quite realistic in terms of proportion and size, in order to make this car more approachable. It’s not just designing a UFO or something which is highly futuristic,” Hossann told the publication. Inside, the cabin of the RCZ Vision concept is installed with the Hypersquare steering “wheel” that first featured on the Polygon concept, and the rectangular steering “wheel” will feature in the next-generation e-208. Displays in the RCZ Vision concept are transparent displays rather than traditional screens, which Peugeot says enables the driver to configure the information displayed, and the central display can even be completely switched off, where the transparent screen offers cleaner aesthetic. This setup of transparent displays complements the Hypersquare “wheel”, which offers access to main functions via the four rings close to hand, and therefore does not require the driver to move their hands from the steering control, says Peugeot. The RCZ Vision concept also serves to showcase the French manufacturer’s “X-by-wire” technologies including steer-by-wire, which means that it does not have a physical connection between the steering and the steered wheels. Peugeot says that steer-by-wire enables the use of variable ratio steering, such as to offer much quicker input at low vehicle speeds and reduced ratios for more stable steering when the vehicle is travelling at higher speeds. Also taking the by-wire approach is the braking system in the RCZ Vision, and the system is said to offer more precise braking modulation and seamless integration of regenerative braking. For ADAS, the RCZ Vision gets “Level 2++” automation, according to Peugeot.

artigo.texto: Key Capture Energy NY1 at Luther Forest in Saratoga County was the first utility-scale battery energy storage system in New York. It is located in Stillwater and broke ground in 2018. HUDSON— The Common Council’s legal committee recommended a six-month pause on battery energy storage systems in the city at a meeting Thursday. The move means the full council will vote on the proposal at its next meeting. The energy storage systems store power, typically from renewable sources, in rechargeable batteries for later use. Common Council President Margaret Morris said the moratorium recommendation began after developers reached out about building the facilities in Hudson. “Our code enforcement officer (Nick Fox) reached out to me, and he had had a couple of inquiries from, I think, two companies inquiring about what Hudson has in its code in relation to large-scale battery operations,” Morris said. One company is eyeing the site of the former Overhead Door garage building on Hudson Avenue, Morris said. Because Hudson has nothing in its code regarding the facilities, Fox suggested the council take some action. The council should be careful not to regulate an opportunity to bring revenue to the city, support the electrical grid, and help the environment, 3rd Ward Councilmember Jason Foster said. Morris countered that battery storage systems are mostly large-scale operations, not compatible with a two-square-mile city like Hudson, and compared them to artificial-intelligence data centers. Morris also cited the risk of large battery fires that can last for weeks, a concern that has led to moratoriums throughout the Twin Counties, including in neighboring Claverack. “There is benefit to these if they didn't catch on fire and didn't explode,” Foster said. “That is always possible. But they are balancing out the grid… I'm just trying to think about ways to help our budget and discuss it further rather than going straight to ixnay.” While the fire risk is concerning, the area does need to be developed, 4th Ward Councilmember Jennifer Belton said. “I would frankly rather see some other kind of small industry come in and do something in that same space,” Belton said. The Columbia Economic Development Corporation has made multiple attempts to get the current owners to sell the property, Morris said. With so much uncertainty, the smartest move would be to pass a moratorium on facilities while city lawmakers reach an agreement on next steps, Common Council attorney Ken Dow said. “If there's not a consensus about just prohibiting them or limiting places where they could go, I think it would be prudent to do a local law, instituting a moratorium for 3 to 6 months,” Dow said. “That way nothing gets in there that you regret. You can then figure out in more detail other places (for the facilities), learn more about these things, the size of them, put together something over the next few months and then modify the code.” Morris said Hudson would use moratoria from other municipalities to shape its moratorium. Foster also asked for an informational presentation on the battery energy storage systems.

artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia 13 de outubro de 2026, às 18:06 Na matéria publicada anteriormente, o nome por extenso do NIL foi grafado de forma errada. O correto é Nature Investment Lab. Também houve erro na grafia do Climate Ventures. Segue a versão corrigida: Apontada como um dos principais entraves para que projetos de reflorestamento e de Redução das Emissões por Desmatamento e Degradação Florestal (Redd+) consigam acessar linhas de financiamento, a modelagem dos contratos passará a ter um padrão, que está em desenvolvimento pelo Natural Investment Lab (NIL). A minuta desse contrato modelo foi apresentada publicamente durante a Semana do Clima que aconteceu recentemente em Nova York e, para elaborá-la, o NIL conversou com 25 importantes instituições. Entre elas, Itaú BBA, Regia Capital, Systemica, Petrobras e Regreen. No próximo passo, o rascunho do contrato modelo será colocado em audiência pública e deve ganhar destaque durante a COP31, que acontecerá entre os dias 9 e 20 de novembro na Turquia. A meta é concluir o trabalho até o final deste ano. O NIL aposta no processo de amadurecimento desse mercado, que já vem durando mais de 20 anos e que deverá elevar o carbono ao status de commodity, com possibilidade de ser negociado internacionalmente. “A ideia é preparar os desenvolvedores dos projetos de produção de carbono para que consigam lidar com todas as exigências com as quais vão se deparar quando tentarem acessar recursos”, explica Fabiana Philipi, gerente de projetos da Climate Venture, organização que lidera o NIL. Ela pondera, no entanto, que o documento de referência poderá ajudar os outros players desse mercado, como os compradores e financiadores do mercado de carbono. Segundo Philipi, as propostas de produção de carbono bem elaboradas têm forte demanda e o objetivo é ajudar desenvolvedores de todos os portes, desde empresas já consagradas como Re.Green e Mombak, até aquelas que estão dando os primeiros passos. As maiores compradoras dos créditos de carbono brasileiros, atualmente, são as big techs, principalmente a Microsoft. A minuta apresentada em Nova York refere-se a contratos offtake – compra mínima garantida – que são acordos jurídicos firmados entre comprador e vendedor de uma mercadoria, antes dela entrar em produção. O documento apresenta cláusulas referentes à estrutura comercial, como preço, pagamento e financiamento, garantias, recebíveis e financiadores, ciclo de vida dos créditos, entrega e titularidade, falha de entrega, entre outros. O NIL é um laboratório de investimentos criado a partir de uma iniciativa que reúne o Banco do Brasil, o Instituto Itaúsa, o Instituto Clima e Sociedade (iCS), o Banco Nacional do Desenvolvimento (BNDES) e a internacional Gfanz. O seu objetivo é atrair e estruturar financiamentos, além de promover inovação financeira, para ampliar a chamada economia de Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (SbN). artigo.texto: SPARTANBURG —A former cryptocurrency mining facility in the Tiger River Industrial Park is being converted into a data center. The company hopes it’s operational by the end of 2027. BV Power Alpha previously received a fee-in-lieu-of-tax agreement for its crypto mining facility that started up in 2022. The company, owned by Jerry Tang, is now called AIB Data Centers. In February, Tang abandoned efforts to build a new data center in the Tyger River Industrial Park after Spartanburg County Council declined to offer tax incentives in the wake of community criticism over the project. Since then, county council passed a data center moratorium that could prevent new data centers that have an IT electrical load of 65 megawatts or more. Council voted to include the caveat after lobbying from William Crawford, president of Pacolet Milliken, and Bryan Stone, president of Pacolet Milliken subsidiary Lockhart Power, who argued that small data centers create revenue that helps keep costs down for ratepayers. Pacolet Milliken developed the Tyger River Industrial Park and Lockhart supplies much of the power there. The new AIB data center will have an electrical load of only 50 megawatts, falling below that 65-megawatt threshold, according to the company. It will buy power from a utility instead of producing it, meaning it won’t create the type of air pollution that the NorthMark data center will generate. Company spokesperson Pierre DuBois said in an email that the planned data center would exist on the same land footprint as the bitcoin mining facility. “Essentially, the same equipment moves inside the walls, with other equipment added within those walls,” he added. DuBois also said the water use in the data center would be a fraction of what the crypto mining facility used. “Since the site began operating, it has used about 14,000 gallons a day,” said DuBois. “We estimate the data center will use about 165 gallons a day.” For comparison, the NorthMark data center projects to use more than 1 million gallons a day. In an email, DuBois said the new data center wouldn’t be a “hyperscale mega-project,” and that the company “offered to give up incentives awarded to the crypto mining facility in 2022, which would otherwise have carried over to the data center. The county accepted.” According to a news release, AIB has already signed a 12-year agreement with Dutch AI company Nebius. It includes two potential five-year renewal periods.

CATL, a Chinese battery technology company, supplies batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage applications, while SERES Group operates in the automotive sector through brands including AITO. Under the agreement, AITO will continue using CATL batteries across its vehicle lineup, following cumulative deliveries exceeding 1.2 million vehicles. The companies plan to accelerate Phase 2 of their Plant in Plant project at the SERES Super Factory, targeting 10–12 GWh of annual battery production capacity. Once both phases are completed, their combined annual production capacity is expected to exceed 20 GWh. The partnership also covers supercharging networks, battery lifecycle services and manufacturing coordination. CATL and SERES will additionally explore opportunities in Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia. artigo.texto: Mercado global de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica até 2035, impulsionado pela demanda de data centers e da indústria Resumo De acordo com o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica, o mercado entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, apoiada pela crescente demanda por medição de umidade precisa e durável em data centers, automação industrial, sistemas de climatização automotiva e equipamentos médicos. Diferentemente dos sensores capacitivos de polymer, os sensores de condutividade térmica oferecem medição direta da umidade absoluta, com histerese mínima e desempenho robusto em ambientes agressivos, o que os torna indispensáveis na fabricação de semiconductor, na produção farmacêutica e no controle avançado de HVAC. À medida que a digitalização e as exigências de eficiência energética se intensificam até 2035, espera-se que o mercado cresça a uma taxa composta anual estável, com o índice de mercado subindo de 100 em 2025 para um patamar significativamente mais alto em 2035. Este relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, segmentação, dinâmica da cadeia de suprimentos e estratégias competitivas, ajudando fabricantes, distribuidores e investidores a navegar por um cenário em evolução. Entre os principais fatores de crescimento estão a expansão de data centers de hiperescala, que exigem controle preciso de umidade para evitar condensação e descargas eletrostáticas, a adoção de regulamentações mais rigorosas de qualidade do ar interior e a integração de sensores de umidade em sistemas de gestão predial conectados à IoT. O ambiente competitivo é moldado por fabricantes de sensores consolidados e empresas de tecnologia especializadas, com foco em miniaturização, saída digital e redução de custos para adoção em massa. O cenário-base para o mercado de sensores de umidade por condutividade térmica entre 2026 e 2035 projeta crescimento robusto, com taxa composta de crescimento anual (CAGR) de 5,8% e índice de mercado atingindo 176 em 2035 (2025 = 100). Essa perspectiva se apoia na adoção acelerada de tecnologias de edificações inteligentes, nas quais os sensores de umidade são essenciais para otimizar o consumo de energia em HVAC e manter o conforto dos ocupantes. No ambiente industrial, o avanço da Indústria 4.0 e da manutenção preditiva impulsiona a demanda por sensores confiáveis e de longa vida útil, capazes de operar em condições extremas. O setor automotivo, em especial a fabricação de veículos elétricos, desponta como aplicação de alto crescimento para sensores de umidade no gerenciamento de baterias e no controle climático da cabine. Regionalmente, a Ásia-Pacífico deve permanecer como o maior e mais dinâmico mercado, sustentada pela fabricação de eletrônicos e pelo desenvolvimento de infraestrutura na China, no Japão e na Coreia do Sul. América do Norte e Europa registrarão demanda constante de reposição e modernização de sistemas existentes, enquanto América Latina e Oriente Médio e África oferecem oportunidades incrementais em monitoramento industrial e agrícola. Restrições na cadeia de suprimentos de componentes especializados e serviços de calibração podem representar desafios temporários, mas, no geral, o mercado está preparado para uma expansão consistente até 2035. No entanto, é preciso falar com franqueza técnica: o Redata, de forma isolada, não soluciona o gargalo da carga tributária sobre os equipamentos de tecnologia da informação (TI) utilizados nos data centers. O programa federal suspende a incidência de PIS/Cofins (Programa de Integração Social e Contribuição para o Financiamento da Seguridade Social) e IPI (Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados) é sobre uma lista de equipamentos de tecnologia da informação (TI). Trata-se de uma medida vital em um setor altamente intensivo em capital, no qual servidores e sistemas de armazenamento representam cerca de 70% dos investimentos. Contudo, uma verdade precisa ser dita: o principal peso tributário sobre os equipamentos continua sendo o ICMS (Imposto sobre Circulação de Mercadorias e Serviços). Enquanto o debate público se concentra na desoneração federal, o ICMS responde por dois terços do total da carga tributária. Isso significa que, embora o Redata antecipe um ambiente favorável, o ganho real de competitividade será limitado caso os estados não se unam a esse esforço por meio da aprovação do convênio no Conselho Nacional de Política Fazendária (Confaz), que permite a redução de até 90% do ICMS. A dinâmica é incontornável. Hoje, grandes operadores globais definem seus aportes comparando custos de implantação, matriz energética, segurança jurídica e incentivos tributários. Países disputam esses aportes, pois sabem que atraem inovação, geram empregos, estimulam outros setores e ampliam a capacidade digital de toda a economia. Nesse contexto, diferenças tributárias tornam-se decisivas. Quando um grupo internacional avalia instalar um data center na América Latina, o Brasil concorre com mercados que oferecem condições agressivas. Se o custo de equipamentos permanecer elevado pelo ICMS, perderemos competitividade num momento em que a demanda por infraestrutura digital cresce exponencialmente, impulsionada pela inteligência artificial e processamento em nuvem. Outro ponto que merece destaque é a inteligência estrutural do Redata. A política não se limita a benefícios tributários; ele estabelece mecanismos de habilitação para projetos de investimento e de coabilitação para empresas que fabricam ou comercializam os equipamentos. Esses instrumentos são essenciais, pois, sem eles, corre-se o risco de a desoneração não ser transferida para a economia. O objetivo do programa é assegurar que a redução tributária chegue ao investimento final e, posteriormente, ao consumidor de serviços digitais, ou seja, a verticalização dos benefícios para toda a cadeia. O sucesso do Redata não deve ser medido apenas pelos impostos reduzidos, mas pela capacidade sistêmica de diminuir o custo do processamento e armazenamento de dados. Quanto mais eficiente o processo, maior a competitividade das empresas que dependem da infraestrutura digital globalmente. Vale lembrar que o Brasil é contumaz importador de capacidade computacional, que em 2025 atingiu o deficit de US$ 7,9 bilhões. A implementação do programa precisa avançar. A regulamentação dos instrumentos de habilitação deve ocorrer com rapidez, objetividade e sem travas que desincentivem investimentos. Ao mesmo tempo, é indispensável construir uma agenda federativa com os Estados na estratégia nacional de atração de investimentos. A transformação digital tornou-se pilar do crescimento no século 21. Inteligência artificial, nuvem e economia de dados dependem de infraestrutura robusta. O Brasil possui vantagens, como matriz elétrica limpa e condição geopolítica estável. Mas essas virtudes não serão suficientes se o ambiente tributário onera os investimentos. O Redata é um passo decisivo. Contudo, seu potencial será plenamente alcançado apenas quando União e estados atuarem de forma coordenada. Sem a redução do ICMS, a política ficará incompleta. Com ela, o Brasil terá condições de se consolidar como polo global de infraestrutura, atraindo bilhões, gerando empregos e fortalecendo sua autonomia tecnológica. O desafio agora não é apenas celebrar a conquista. É garantir que ela produza todos os resultados que o país precisa para liderar a economia digital do futuro.

artigo.texto: - Gotion Power Morocco plans to begin commissioning its battery-production equipment during the week of 20 October. - The first phase of the Kenitra project represents approximately $1.3 billion in investment. - The factory will manufacture batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage, targeting African and international markets. - A separate partnership with Volkswagen’s PowerCo will produce battery materials in Morocco. Gotion Power Morocco announced on 12 October that equipment commissioning and startup would begin during the week of 20 October at its plant in Kenitra’s Atlantic Free Zone. The company says construction of the cell plant’s buildings and infrastructure is complete. The first phase is designed for 20 gigawatt-hours of annual production capacity, a planned figure rather than current output. The facility will manufacture lithium iron phosphate batteries, commonly known as LFP batteries, for customers in Morocco and elsewhere in Africa, alongside Europe, the Middle East and the United States. According to TelQuel, which reported the company’s statement issued on 12 October, commissioning will open the way to industrial cell production. Gotion Power Morocco chairman Khalid Qalam had previously indicated that sales of assembled batteries were expected before the end of the year. From investment plans to factory operations The announcement gives a more precise timetable for a project whose first production line had already been expected to start in October. Commissioning involves bringing equipment into operation and testing its performance before production can expand. It should not be confused with the factory immediately reaching its full annual capacity. Gotion’s own project information puts first-phase investment at approximately $1.3 billion and identifies a planned capacity of 20 GWh. The next commercial milestones will be consistent production, customer deliveries and the gradual increase in output. Volkswagen adds a European connection The factory’s progress comes as Gotion deepens its partnership with Volkswagen and the German carmaker’s battery subsidiary, PowerCo. On 28 September, the companies announced plans for joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia and Morocco to expand production of LFP battery cells and cathode materials. The proposed Kenitra joint venture will manufacture cathode material, a key battery component. Gotion will hold 51% and PowerCo 49%, with the partners managing the venture together. That materials project is separate from the cell-production equipment scheduled for commissioning this month. Volkswagen’s announcement did not establish an October startup date for the cathode facility. Morocco is attracting investment in both finished battery cells and the materials needed to manufacture them. Why Morocco matters to the supply chain Volkswagen says its partnership with Gotion is intended to diversify supplies and strengthen Europe’s battery industry. LFP technology offers relatively competitive costs, a long service life and durability, making it attractive for more affordable electric vehicles and energy-storage systems. The companies see expanding European demand as an opportunity for their production network. For Morocco, the investment provides an opportunity to move further into battery manufacturing while serving markets beyond its borders. The project has also attracted African development financing. The African Development Bank announced approval of a loan in July to support an integrated battery-manufacturing facility in Kenitra. Its financing documents describe an initial 10 GWh project, whereas Gotion’s broader first-phase description puts capacity at 20 GWh.

artigo.texto: Mercado global de criptografia por hardware: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Projeção do Mercado de Criptografia por Hardware até 2035: Crescimento Impulsionado pela Demanda de Data Centers e pela Conformidade Regulatória Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Criptografia por Hardware, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de criptografia por hardware entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, com horizonte de projeção até 2035. A criptografia por hardware, que se baseia em componentes físicos dedicados para executar funções criptográficas, oferece desempenho superior, menor latência e maior resistência à violação em comparação com alternativas baseadas em software. À medida que os volumes de dados aumentam e as ameaças cibernéticas se tornam mais sofisticadas, organizações de diversos setores priorizam uma proteção de dados robusta. Exigências regulatórias como GDPR, HIPAA e CCPA impulsionam a adoção, enquanto a proliferação da computação em nuvem e de borda cria novos vetores de demanda. O mercado abrange unidades de disco com autocrifragem, módulos de segurança de hardware, chips TPM, pen drives criptografados e outros hardwares especializados. Os principais setores de uso final incluem data centers, TI corporativa, governo, serviços financeiros e saúde. O cenário competitivo reúne fornecedores consolidados de semicondutores e armazenamento, além de empresas especializadas em segurança. Esta análise oferece uma visão orientada por dados da dinâmica de mercado, dos fatores de demanda e das considerações estratégicas para os participantes até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de criptografia por hardware prevê crescimento constante entre 2026 e 2035, sustentado por fatores estruturais de demanda. A frequência e a gravidade crescentes das violações de dados levam as organizações a adotar a criptografia baseada em hardware como camada fundamental de segurança. Os marcos regulatórios em todo o mundo estão mais rígidos, exigindo criptografia para dados sensíveis em repouso e em trânsito, o que impulsiona diretamente a demanda por soluções de hardware em conformidade. A expansão de data centers e da infraestrutura de nuvem, impulsionada pela transformação digital e por cargas de trabalho de IA, exige criptografia de alto desempenho que somente o hardware é capaz de oferecer. No segmento corporativo, a migração para arquiteturas de confiança zero e a necessidade de proteger ambientes de trabalho remoto são catalisadores adicionais. A adoção de dispositivos de armazenamento criptografados pelos consumidores também cresce, ainda que a partir de uma base menor. Entre os entraves estão os custos iniciais elevados, a complexidade de integração e a escassez de mão de obra qualificada. No entanto, a inovação contínua, como a integração da criptografia aos processadores principais e o desenvolvimento de criptografia pós-quântica, deve atenuar esses desafios. O índice de mercado deve alcançar 185 até 2035, refletindo uma trajetória robusta de expansão. Fatores de Demanda e Restrições Principais Fatores de Demanda - Violações de dados e ameaças cibernéticas crescentes impulsionam a demanda por criptografia de hardware resistente à violação - Exigências regulatórias rigorosas (GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA) que requerem criptografia para dados sensíveis - Proliferação de data centers e infraestrutura de nuvem que exige criptografia de alto desempenho - Adoção de arquiteturas de segurança de confiança zero e tendências de trabalho remoto - Crescimento da eletrônica de consumo com recursos de criptografia integrados - Avanços em algoritmos de criptografia e integração com arquiteturas de computação emergentes Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Custos iniciais elevados e complexidade de integração de soluções de criptografia por hardware - Escassez de mão de obra qualificada para implantação e gestão - Problemas de compatibilidade com sistemas legados e ambientes de TI diversificados - Concorrência de soluções de criptografia baseadas em software em segmentos sensíveis a custos Estrutura de Demanda por Setor de Uso Final Armazenamento em Data Centers (participação estimada: 30%) Os data centers são o maior setor de uso final da criptografia por hardware, impulsionados pelo crescimento exponencial das necessidades de armazenamento de dados e pela demanda por criptografia de alto desempenho e baixa latência. À medida que provedores de serviços em nuvem e empresas ampliam sua infraestrutura de armazenamento, cresce a implantação de unidades de disco com autocrifragem (SEDs) e módulos de segurança de hardware (HSMs) para garantir a proteção dos dados sem comprometer o desempenho. A migração para interfaces NVMe e PCIe acelera ainda mais a demanda por criptografia por hardware, pois essas tecnologias exigem offload criptográfico eficiente. A conformidade regulatória, como o GDPR e exigências específicas do setor, obriga os operadores de data centers a implementar criptografia para dados em repouso. Até 2035, espera-se que a adoção de SEDs se torne padrão no armazenamento corporativo, enquanto os HSMs terão demanda crescente para gestão de chaves e aceleração criptográfica. O avanço da computação de borda e do 5G também criará novos nós distribuídos de data centers que exigirão criptografia. Entre os indicadores do lado da demanda estão a capacidade de armazenamento embarcada, os gastos com infraestrutura de nuvem e o ritmo de construção de data centers.
