artigo.texto: Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) has published results in all three waves of the Global Battery Alliance (GBA) battery passport pilot, a record the Chinese battery maker says no rival has matched. The latest round covered cell producers with nearly 80% of global capacity, ahead of a full certification scheme due in early 2027. The pilot is building a shared method to track, measure and verify the environmental, social and governance (ESG) record of a battery over its life. CATL’s entry this year reported ESG data for every stage of supply, from mining and refining through materials, cells and packs. That breadth matters as passports move from trial to obligation. EU rules will require digital passports for electric vehicle batteries from February 2027, giving suppliers with verified upstream data an edge with European automakers. CATL joined at the GBA’s first proof of concept in January 2023, and in the second wave sought separate passports for its Shenxing and cell-to-pack batteries, with results checked by an independent auditor. It also says its core operations are carbon neutral and targets a carbon-neutral value chain by 2035. In a statement, Dennis Pan, Head of Sustainable Development at CATL, said: “The GBA Battery Passport pilot program provides an effective methodology for the industry to monitor, quantify and demonstrate ESG performance across the battery value chain. It helps the industry better prepare for future sustainability risks and challenges.” Source: CATL

artigo.texto: O mercado de carbono abre fontes adicionais de capital para empresas em transição para energias sustentáveis. O mercado de carbono pode gerar receita a partir da redução de emissões, ajudando as empresas a diversificar seus recursos de investimento e a reduzir a dependência de crédito bancário. No entanto, para que a valoração do carbono influencie as decisões de empréstimo, é necessário superar os obstáculos legais, de dados e de fluxo de caixa. No seminário "Política de Crédito e Mercado de Carbono: Desbloqueando Fluxos de Capital Verde", realizado em 14 de outubro, o Sr. Nguyen Ngoc Canh, Vice-Governador do Banco Central do Vietnã (SBV), afirmou que um mercado de carbono que funcione de forma eficiente ajudará a transformar os resultados da redução de emissões em valor econômico , criará recursos adicionais para as empresas e contribuirá para reduzir a pressão sobre o crédito bancário. Para cumprir seu compromisso de emissões líquidas zero até 2050, o Vietnã está acelerando o crescimento verde, a transição energética e a redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Esse processo exige investimentos significativos em inovação tecnológica, ajustes nos métodos de produção e melhoria da eficiência energética. Além do orçamento estatal, dos mercados de capitais e do crédito bancário, o mercado de carbono pode se tornar um canal para complementar esses recursos. Em 29 de janeiro de 2026, o Governo emitiu o Decreto nº 29/2026/ND-CP, que regulamenta o mercado interno de carbono. De acordo com as informações apresentadas na oficina, o mercado encontra-se atualmente em fase piloto, com mais de 511 milhões de toneladas de CO₂ equivalente em quotas de emissão alocadas a instalações dos três setores: energia térmica, siderurgia e cimento, durante o período de 2025-2026. A fase piloto se estenderá até o final de 2028, antes da transição para a operação obrigatória plena a partir de 2029. Segundo o vice-governador do Banco Estatal do Vietnã , Nguyen Ngoc Canh, o crédito verde e o mercado de carbono têm uma relação complementar. O crédito verde fornece capital para que as empresas invistam em tecnologia, desenvolvam produção verde e reduzam as emissões; o mercado de carbono cria um mecanismo para que esses resultados se tornem bens negociáveis. A receita proveniente do comércio de carbono, se estabelecida de forma consistente, pode sustentar o fluxo de caixa e melhorar a capacidade de pagamento de dívidas de uma empresa. A mensuração, o relato e a avaliação dos resultados da redução de emissões também fornecem informações adicionais para que as instituições de crédito avaliem a eficácia da utilização do capital e gerenciem os riscos dos empréstimos verdes. No final de junho de 2026, o saldo de crédito verde atingiu mais de 856 trilhões de VND, um aumento de 9,87% em comparação com o final de 2025. Durante o período de 2017 a 2025, a taxa média de crescimento foi superior a 20% ao ano. Os empréstimos pendentes concentram-se principalmente nos setores de agricultura , silvicultura, pesca e conservação da biodiversidade, representando mais de 31%; a energia verde representa quase 28%. Você também pode gostar Dadas as significativas necessidades de capital para a transformação verde, o desenvolvimento de um mercado de carbono contribuirá para a diversificação das fontes de financiamento, criando incentivos adicionais para que as empresas invistam em tecnologias limpas e reduzindo a dependência de empréstimos bancários. Na perspectiva dos bancos comerciais, a Dra. Nguyen Thi Thu Ha, Diretora da Escola de Formação de Quadros e Vice-Chefe do Comitê Diretivo de ESG do Agribank , acredita que incorporar o valor do carbono nas decisões de crédito exige determinar a confiabilidade dos resultados da redução de emissões e a capacidade de converter esse valor em fluxo de caixa real. A agricultura, a silvicultura e a economia circular têm um potencial significativo para reduzir as emissões, desde a produção de arroz e a pecuária até o tratamento de resíduos. Essas são também áreas em que o financiamento bancário pode ser vinculado a modelos de produção sustentáveis. No entanto, um projeto que atenda a critérios ambientais não gera automaticamente créditos de carbono; da mesma forma, possuir créditos de carbono não garante automaticamente a elegibilidade para empréstimos. Os bancos ainda precisam avaliar a viabilidade do plano de negócios e a capacidade de pagamento do projeto. Segundo a Sra. Ha, para que a valoração do carbono apoie as atividades de concessão de créditos, é necessário esclarecer a propriedade, os direitos de alienação e os benefícios decorrentes dos resultados da redução de emissões; e melhorar a qualidade do sistema de medição, reporte e avaliação. Quando os dados não são suficientemente confiáveis, os benefícios não são claros ou o mercado carece de um preço de referência estável, os bancos têm dificuldade em considerar a receita de carbono como uma fonte confiável de pagamento de dívidas. Os custos de levantamento, elaboração de relatórios e avaliações também podem se tornar uma barreira para cooperativas, pequenas empresas e áreas de produção dispersas. A padronização de dados, a redução dos custos de avaliação e a produção organizada ao longo da cadeia de valor ajudarão muitos projetos a acessar capital verde. Você também pode gostar Até o final de março de 2026, o saldo de crédito verde do Agribank atingiu quase 30 trilhões de VND. O banco está implementando programas de empréstimo para apoiar a agricultura limpa e de alta tecnologia, bem como a integração entre produção, processamento e consumo de arroz de alta qualidade e baixa emissão no Delta do Mekong. A Sra. Ha argumentou que é necessário aprimorar ainda mais o arcabouço legal relativo aos direitos aos créditos de carbono, desenvolver a infraestrutura de dados, reduzir os custos de avaliação e construir um mecanismo de compartilhamento de riscos para projetos em seus estágios iniciais. artigo.texto: A Finnish battery startup facing sustained accusations from industry rivals that its technology is overstated or outright fraudulent has released new independent test data showing its solid-state cells deliver more than their rated capacity at temperatures that would degrade or destroy a conventional lithium-ion battery. Donut Lab, which has previously claimed its cells can charge in minutes and offer high energy density, commissioned a second evaluation by VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, the country’s state-run research institute. The results, published by Donut Lab this week, focus specifically on thermal performance, examining how the battery behaves at 80°C and 100°C, temperatures at which standard lithium-ion cells begin to suffer serious performance loss and pose safety risks. Standard lithium-ion batteries are very sensitive to heat, with an upper operating temperature limit of typically around 60 to 70 degrees Celsius. High temperatures increase the risk of damage to battery cells and shorten their service life. High temperatures can also cause accelerated reactions inside the cell, and in the worst case, the risk of thermal runaway increases significantly. The Donut Battery does not use flammable liquid electrolytes, the component most responsible for thermal runaway in conventional cells. That difference in architecture is what VTT’s tests were designed to quantify under real thermal stress. The methodology was straightforward. Engineers placed the cell on an aluminium profile, secured a steel plate on top to apply light pressure and reduce hot spots, then measured capacity in stages at each temperature. At 176°F, the battery delivered about 110% of its rated capacity, showed better efficiency than at room temperature, and the cell showed no visible changes after the test. At 212°F, the battery used roughly 107% of its capacity and recharged back to 4.15 volts with the same capacity as at room temperature. Although the pouch lost vacuum at that temperature, the active materials remained fully functional. The efficiency gain at elevated temperatures is explained by basic electrochemistry. Heat reduces the internal resistance of a cell, which in turn reduces the voltage drop during discharge, allowing more of the stored energy to be extracted as usable output. In a liquid-electrolyte battery, that benefit is overwhelmed by accelerating degradation chemistry. In Donut Lab’s solid-state design, the degradation mechanism is largely absent, allowing the efficiency benefit to dominate instead. “The battery’s full capacity was utilised with excellent results at both 80 and 100 degrees Celsius, and it was possible to discharge it at a 1C discharge rate at 80 degrees and a 0.5C discharge rate at 100 degrees without any increase in temperature. The battery’s properties did not change even at 100 degrees, and it functioned normally when recharged, which demonstrates the convincing performance of the Donut Battery even in extremely hot conditions. This confirms that the battery is exceptional not only in terms of performance but also in terms of safety,” said Ville Piippo, CTO at Donut Lab. The results carry practical implications beyond the laboratory. Batteries that tolerate extreme heat without cooling system support could reduce the weight, complexity, and cost of thermal management in electric vehicles, particularly relevant for markets in desert climates where ambient temperatures routinely exceed the operating ceiling of conventional packs. Industrial applications including grid storage, aerospace, and military systems have similarly been constrained by the thermal sensitivity of existing battery chemistry. The tests also represent a deliberate shift in how Donut Lab is managing its public credibility. After bold claims generated skepticism rather than investment interest, the company is now building its case incrementally through third-party data published openly, letting the numbers do the work that press releases could not. For automakers in the US and companies focused on energy storage, having batteries that can handle extreme heat is absolutely essential. Batteries that can endure high temperatures not only lessen the strain on cooling systems but also enhance safety in sweltering regions like Arizona, Texas, and Nevada. Whether the technology proves durable at manufacturing scale remains the central unanswered question, but on the narrow question of what the cells do under extreme heat, the independent record now says they perform better than anything currently in mass production.

artigo.texto: Digital transformation from data: [Part 4] Building a digital platform for the carbon market Data on greenhouse gas emission quotas, carbon credits, and carbon market participants in Vietnam are managed centrally and uniformly on a single digital platform. The agriculture and environment sector is focusing on standardizing, connecting, and exploiting databases, innovating management methods, and serving the people and businesses. In response to the National Digital Transformation Day on October 10, 2026, with the theme "From architecture, platform, data to tangible results," the Agriculture and Environment newspaper is publishing a special feature titled "Digital Transformation from Data," clarifying the role of data in innovating management methods, improving operational efficiency, better utilizing resources, and serving the people and businesses. The shift towards data-driven governance. The Climate Change Department (Ministry of Agriculture and Environment) has developed and put into operation the National Registration System for Greenhouse Gas Emission Quotas and Carbon Credits. In June 2026, the system will begin operating in parallel with the domestic carbon exchange. This can be considered a significant step in the digital transformation of the agriculture and environment sector, contributing to the modernization of state management in responding to climate change and developing a carbon market in Vietnam. According to Mr. Nguyen Thanh Cong, Deputy Head of the Carbon Market Department (Climate Change Agency), the system helps transform management methods from traditional administrative processes to a digital environment. Through the system, data on greenhouse gas emission quotas, carbon credits, and market participants are managed centrally and uniformly on a digital platform. The data ensures accuracy, transparency, traceability, and control over historical fluctuations. In particular, the National Registration System is a crucial component of the digital infrastructure serving the operation of Vietnam's carbon market, playing a connecting role between state management and activities related to the custody, trading, and payment of greenhouse gas emission quotas and carbon credits. “The construction of this system not only meets the operational requirements of the domestic carbon market but also creates a foundation for gradually connecting and exchanging data with international cooperation mechanisms on carbon under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. This will support the achievement of greenhouse gas emission reduction targets, green transition, and Vietnam's commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050,” Mr. Nguyen Thanh Cong shared. The main functions of the system The national registration system serves to centrally and uniformly manage operations related to the registration, issuance of codes, tracking of ownership, transfer, and use of greenhouse gas emission quotas and carbon credits in accordance with the law . You may also like The Climate Change Department is providing training to organizations and businesses on participating in the carbon market. Photo: Trung Nguyen. First, the system facilitates the registration, setup, and management of electronic accounts for agencies and organizations participating in the carbon market. This includes managing account holder information, controlling transactions, and monitoring the balance of greenhouse gas emission quotas and carbon credits for each account. These activities are conducted electronically, simplifying the registration process, enhancing control capabilities, and improving the efficiency of transaction processing. For greenhouse gas emission quotas and carbon credits, the system registers and records information on allocated quotas and eligible carbon credits; assigns codes, manages the quantity, status, and history of changes of each carbon unit. Through centralized and unified management, the system allows for the tracking of greenhouse gas emission quotas and carbon credits throughout their existence and use. This ensures transparency, traceability, and reduces the risk of double recording and repeated use of a single carbon unit. The image illustrates the serial number of an organization/business's emission quota. Photo: VNEEC . In addition, the system supports operations related to depositing, withdrawing deposits, transferring ownership off-exchange, using carbon credits to offset emissions, paying, transferring, and borrowing greenhouse gas emission quotas as regulated. The system is connected and exchanges data with custody, trading, and payment systems to ensure synchronization between registration information and trading activities in the domestic carbon market. In addition to the aforementioned functions, the system also provides the ability to search, aggregate, statistically analyze, and report data on the registration and use of greenhouse gas emission quotas and carbon credits. These functions support state management agencies in monitoring market operations, verifying and cross-referencing information, and supervising the compliance of emitting facilities. The data also serves the planning and implementation of policies on greenhouse gas emission reduction and carbon market development in Vietnam. Step-by-step preparations for the official launch of the carbon market. The goal is to operate the system stably, safely, efficiently, and to meet the requirements of Vietnam's carbon market development in each stage. artigo.texto: SC Senate candidates clash over data center expansion in debate COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - During Sunday’s debate in South Carolina’s heated U.S. Senate race, data centers became a big point of contention for all three candidates. Republican Sen. Darline Graham, along with challengers Dr. Annie Andrews and Kasie Whitener, were asked Sunday if they supported data center moratoriums and if they’d support federal regulations. Andrews, the Democratic challenger, pushed Graham on her stance on data centers. “She [Graham] thinks we need to all get with the program and build data centers faster and faster,” said Andrews. “So why does ‘Data Center Darline’ think we need to do that? Because data center companies and AI companies have spent millions to prop up her campaign.” Graham fired back. “Since we’re name-calling here. obviously, you don’t know my stance on data centers. I’m concerned about data centers too, but let me be clear here: I think there needs to be community involvement when it comes to data centers,” the senator responded. Whitener, running as a Libertarian, said she feels local communities need to have a voice when it comes to building new data centers in their area. “It is a local issue,” Whitener said. At least six Midlands communities have voted to temporarily pause data center development, with others also doing so across the state. More South Carolinians are raising concerns about possible impacts of those data centers, including water consumption and higher energy bills. “These data centers are being built in communities’ backyards without any community input,” said Andrews. Andrews said her data center plan includes a two-year moratorium. Graham criticized the proposal, citing national security concerns and what she argued is a growing threat from China. “Under her Bernie Sanders plan, a two-year moratorium, that is dangerous to the national security of our country because in two years, China is going to be so far ahead, we’re going to be in so much trouble,” said Graham. Whitener doubled down on her stance. “Your community should be talking to one another and figuring out what’s best for you, and again you don’t need the government’s permission to do that,” Whitener said. Meanwhile, South Carolina state lawmakers are set to reassess statewide regulations on data centers when they return for the next legislative session in 2027. artigo.texto: Sign up for The Brief, The Texas Tribune’s daily newsletter that keeps readers up to speed on the most essential Texas news. This article is co-published with El Paso Matters and ProPublica as part of an initiative to report on local control of government. Sign up to receive ProPublica’s biggest stories as soon as they’re published. Last December, New Mexico officials celebrated publication of a plan to address climate change, designed to dramatically reduce the state’s greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. A few months later, just across the state line in Texas, El Paso city officials adopted their own such plan with a similar ambition. Each report cost millions of dollars to draft, but neither one took into account how the construction of data centers could upend climate goals in both places. Work is underway in Doña Ana County in southern New Mexico on one of the largest data center developments in the country: Project Jupiter, built by Austin-based Oracle. Twenty miles away in El Paso, construction is underway on another massive data center, this one built by Meta Platforms. A third, larger data center project is planned less than a 30-minute drive from the Meta site, on the Fort Bliss Army post in east El Paso. The data centers are “going to undo a lot of the very expensive and very meaningful work a lot of people are doing,” New Mexico state climatologist Dave DuBois told El Paso Matters. The sites are among a wave of data centers under construction across the country, driven by the rapidly escalating demand for artificial intelligence services like Claude and ChatGPT. Such projects have drawn intense scrutiny in recent months, as residents and elected officials have questioned their impact on communities’ water supplies, household electric bills and air quality. Texas alone has 596 data centers that are either in operation or planned across Texas as of early September, according to research by The Texas Tribune. But the projects located in this population center of 1.2 million, which encompasses El Paso and parts of southern New Mexico, are particularly notable because of their combined scope. When fully built out, the three data centers, each with its own power plant, will emit millions of tons of greenhouse gas emissions, equivalent to the planet-warming emissions released by more than two million cars in a year. They will also release air pollutants like particulate matter and nitrogen oxides, which directly affect local air quality and human health. The Meta and Project Jupiter data centers are expected to release these kinds of pollutants at relatively low levels, according to paperwork submitted to state regulators. But even a small increase in air pollution can still negatively impact communities close to and downwind of the data center sites, said Shaolei Ren, a professor of electrical and computer engineering at University of California, Riverside. “The health impacts can be significant for local communities,” Ren said. Because Project Jupiter, Meta and the Fort Bliss data centers are in two different states, and because there is no single federal regulation governing climate change or emissions, regulators have largely considered the projects’ impacts separately. “We’ve never had a national climate law passed by Congress,” said Ari Peskoe, director of the Electricity Law Initiative at Harvard Law School. “And so what we’ve had in this country are primarily state and local efforts.” The result is that officials in one state have little say over a project happening minutes away from them. Texas and New Mexico also take different approaches to dealing with climate change. New Mexico has codified greenhouse gas reduction targets into state law; Texas has not. New Mexico state Rep. Sarah Silva, a Democrat, represents the community of Chaparral, directly across the state line from Meta’s data center site in northeast El Paso. Her state has the power to regulate air quality and impose noise requirements, but only in New Mexico, not at a Texas construction site, even if it’s only a few hundred yards away. Likewise, residents living in west El Paso across the state line from Project Jupiter have no say in the project despite sharing an aquifer that crosses the state boundary. Emissions do not remain within the state where they originate, Silva said. “This is why we need federal regulation,” said Silva. “How do we knit something together that makes sense for our region when actually this is the job of the federal government?” Though they profess a desire to mitigate the impacts of climate change, local governments in El Paso and Doña Ana counties green-lit these projects in a part of the country seeing rapidly rising temperatures. The counties offered Meta and Project Jupiter tax incentives in exchange for corporate investment in their communities, job creation and, hopefully, the ability to attract more technology companies to the region. State officials have also provided incentives. More than a decade ago, Texas legislators approved a data center sales tax break, which exempts the facilities from paying sales tax on equipment they purchase, a decision that could now cost the state $3.2 billion in revenue over the next two years, according to The Texas Tribune. New Mexico lawmakers declined to advance a bill creating a similar tax break for data centers in 2021. But in 2025, they passed an unrelated law allowing large facilities such as Project Jupiter to generate their own electricity using natural gas. The law exempts these private power systems, known as microgrids, from renewable energy requirements, even as New Mexico requires electric utilities to source 50% of the power they sell from clean energy by 2030. The power plants that keep data centers running typically produce large amounts of emissions like carbon dioxide and methane that drive global climate change over time. artigo.texto: Modelos e plataformas de IA Celestica apresenta o switch de óptica coempacotada DS6005 para data centers de IA Adicione Unite.AI às suas fontes preferidas no Google A Celestica apresentou o DS6005, um switch para data centers totalmente refrigerado a líquido, que oferece capacidade de até 102,4 Tbps por meio de óptica coempacotada, em um comunicado da empresa datado de 12 de outubro de 2026. O sistema é baseado no chip de switch Tomahawk 6 – Davisson, da Broadcom, e a Celestica o está apresentando no OCP Global Summit 2026, em San Jose, realizado de 12 a 15 de outubro de 2026. A empresa, sediada em Toronto, descreveu o DS6005 como um sistema de comutação por óptica coempacotada (CPO), projetado para atender aos requisitos de densidade de largura de banda, consumo de energia, latência e alcance das redes de data centers de IA de próxima geração. A Celestica afirmou que o switch foi desenvolvido especificamente para redes de ampliação vertical e horizontal de IA e aprendizado de máquina, e que reduz o consumo de energia e a latência, além de melhorar a eficiência e a confiabilidade dos clusters de IA de próxima geração. Gavin Cato, vice-presidente sênior e gerente-geral de soluções de portfólio e engenharia de plataformas de IA da Celestica, afirmou que a infraestrutura de IA está impulsionando a demanda por largura de banda, enquanto o consumo de energia, o gerenciamento térmico, a latência e o alcance se tornam limitações cada vez mais importantes. “O DS6005 reúne óptica coempacotada, refrigeração líquida, módulos laser externos substituíveis em campo e gerenciamento de software compatível com CPO em uma plataforma compacta, projetada para ajudar os clientes a construir redes de IA escaláveis e eficientes em termos de energia”, disse Cato. Hardware e design do DS6005 O DS6005 posiciona seus mecanismos ópticos diretamente no encapsulamento do ASIC do switch, em vez de usar óptica plugável convencional no painel frontal. Segundo a Celestica, o design coempacotado tem como objetivo ajudar operadores de data centers a otimizar a densidade de largura de banda, reduzir a latência e melhorar a eficiência energética. A empresa informou que o equipamento conta com 64 portas de 1,6 TbE, que fornecem ao sistema capacidade de comutação de 102,4 Tbps, e que o gabinete de 1,5OU totalmente refrigerado a líquido, projetado para racks OCP ORv3, melhora a estabilidade térmica e a confiabilidade, ao mesmo tempo que aumenta a densidade geral do rack. O switch também é compatível com SONiC, o que, segundo a Celestica, permite acelerar a entrada em produção em uma arquitetura aberta e comprovada. A página do produto DS6005 lista uma CPU AMD Ryzen x86 ao lado do chip Broadcom TH6-Davisson. As 64 interconexões ópticas passam por 16x 4x conectores MMC-16, e o sistema também inclui uma porta 100GbE QSFP28, portas de console RJ45 e de gerenciamento GbE fora de banda, uma porta USB 3.0 Type A, uma porta USB-C de console e 16 interfaces ELSFP para módulos laser externos. O equipamento está em conformidade com a especificação de rack ORv3-HPR. Na página do produto, a Celestica afirmou que o switch reduz o consumo de energia dos links, oferece latência ultrabaixa e reduz a latência em comparação com a óptica com retimers. A página cita redes de ampliação vertical e horizontal de IA e aprendizado de máquina, computação de alto desempenho, modelos de IA de domínio para nuvens de fronteira e empresas e infraestrutura de nuvem em hiperescala como os tipos de implantação para os quais o sistema é otimizado. Silício Tomahawk 6 – Davisson da Broadcom A Broadcom anunciou, em 8 de outubro de 2025, que estava enviando o Tomahawk 6 – Davisson, seu switch Ethernet CPO de terceira geração, que descreveu como o primeiro do setor a oferecer capacidade de comutação habilitada por óptica de 102,4 Tbps. Para o dispositivo BCM78919, a Broadcom listou 16 mecanismos ópticos Davisson DR de 6,4 Tbps cada, largura de banda de 200 Gbps por link, módulos laser ELSFP substituíveis em campo e suporte a clusters de ampliação vertical com 512 XPUs, bem como a mais de 100.000 XPUs em redes de dois níveis, a 200 Gbps por link. Segundo a Broadcom, o chip está em conformidade com a norma IEEE 802.3 e é interoperável com os padrões 400G e 800G existentes. A Broadcom afirmou que o TH6-Davisson integra de forma heterogênea mecanismos ópticos baseados na tecnologia COUPE da TSMC com encapsulamento avançado de múltiplos chips no nível do substrato. A empresa relatou uma redução de 70% no consumo de energia das interconexões ópticas, um nível que descreveu como mais de 3,5 vezes inferior ao das soluções plugáveis tradicionais. Cato também fez uma declaração de apoio no comunicado de 2025, afirmando que a integração óptica, a eficiência energética e o desempenho do chip estavam alinhados à estratégia da Celestica para infraestrutura de IA e implantações de cargas de trabalho de próxima geração. Declarações de apoio e apresentação no Summit Manish Mehta, vice-presidente de marketing e operações da divisão Optical Systems da Broadcom, afirmou que transformar a óptica coempacotada de uma arquitetura avançada em um sistema pronto para produção exige colaboração nas áreas de silício, mecanismos ópticos, encapsulamento, design térmico, fabricação e integração de sistemas. Mehta disse que a engenharia de sistemas e a execução de plataformas da Celestica ajudaram a transformar a tecnologia da Broadcom em uma plataforma projetada para redes de IA de alta densidade. Sameh Boujelbene, vice-presidente de pesquisa do Dell’Oro Group, afirmou que as redes de IA estão deslocando o gargalo da computação para a infraestrutura física ao seu redor, na qual o consumo de energia, a densidade, o alcance e a complexidade da implantação são cada vez mais importantes. Boujelbene descreveu a óptica coempacotada como uma das principais soluções do setor para enfrentar esses desafios e afirmou que as abordagens plugável, próxima ao encapsulamento e coempacotada continuarão coexistindo à

artigo.texto: Energy Dome Opens Piacenza Plant to Expand CO2 Battery Production Energy Dome, an Italian company focused on long-duration energy storage, has launched a production facility in Piacenza, Italy, as part of a push to scale up manufacturing of its CO2 Battery technology for projects worldwide. The site will produce essential components, among them the sizable domes that form part of Energy Dome's carbon dioxide-based storage systems. According to the company, the first dome made completely in-house has been sent to India for the 20 MW/160 MWh Kudgi project alongside state-owned utility NTPC. Manufacturing is also proceeding for the 20 MW/200 MWh Columbia Energy Storage Project in Wisconsin, United States, together with Alliant Energy. The following component will go to a 23 MW/200 MWh project in Rhode, Ireland. Over the past year, Energy Dome put roughly EUR2 million, or about $2.2 million, into the Piacenza location to renovate the building, buy machinery and enhance electrical and network infrastructure. Across the next two years, it intends to lift total investment to around EUR6.5 million, with aims of tripling output capacity and growing the local staff from 30 employees to a range of 80 to 90 by 2028. Energy Dome stated that its technology depends on European manufacturing supply chains, such as steel and turbomachinery, instead of chains based outside Europe. The company says it operates on four continents, with over 2 GWh of projects either running or contracted, more than 3 GWh of authorized projects and a development pipeline above 30 GWh. Among its customers and partners are Google, Engie, Alliant Energy, NTPC, SEC and SRP. Energy Dome further pointed to Italy's National Integrated Energy and Climate Plan, grid operator Terna's identified requirement for 50 GWh of storage by 2030 and the new MACSE storage procurement mechanism as elements underpinning demand for energy storage. - 1. artigo.texto: A Yandex é a maior empresa de tecnologia da Rússia, oferecendo serviços como busca, transporte por aplicativo, comércio eletrônico, computação em nuvem e inteligência artificial (IA). Sua plataforma Yandex Cloud – especializada em poder computacional, armazenamento de dados e ferramentas de IA – é atualmente utilizada por mais de um terço das maiores empresas da Rússia. O ataque de 11 de outubro teve como alvo uma instalação da Yandex na região de Vladimir, a cerca de 180 km a nordeste de Moscou. Essa instalação também abriga o Galushkin, um dos três supercomputadores da empresa usados para o desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial. A Yandex anunciou no Telegram que o ataque danificou a infraestrutura do data center e forçou seu desligamento. “A infraestrutura do centro de dados da Yandex em Vladimir foi danificada por um ataque de drone, e as operações no local foram completamente suspensas. Vários serviços da Yandex estão atualmente inacessíveis aos usuários”, afirmou a empresa. Não houve relatos de vítimas no ataque mencionado. As equipes de resgate e os engenheiros da Yandex trabalharam para avaliar os danos e restabelecer o serviço. A empresa também recomendou que os clientes de serviços em nuvem ativem seus planos de contingência para responder a incidentes semelhantes. Segundo relatos da mídia, o ataque forçou a Yandex Cloud a entrar em modo de emergência; a interrupção do serviço afetou bancos, plataformas de comércio eletrônico, serviços de entrega, aplicativos de varejo, farmácias, academias e o site do Aeroporto Pulkovo em São Petersburgo. Em uma atualização posterior, o Yandex afirmou que o acesso a alguns de seus serviços – incluindo a assistente virtual de IA Alice, Busca, Mapas, Táxi e E-mail – estava sendo gradualmente restaurado. Este é o terceiro ataque contra instalações da Yandex em quatro dias. Anteriormente, o centro de dados da Yandex em Sasovo, região de Ryazan, foi severamente danificado em um ataque na noite de 7 de outubro, forçando seu desligamento. Outra instalação na região de Kaluga, a cerca de 150 km a sudoeste de Moscou, também foi danificada em um ataque com drone em 9 de outubro.

artigo.texto: Trinasolar Unveils 760 W Solar Modules and Battery Storage in Vietnam Trinasolar and Trina Storage unveiled their Vertex N G3 modules and Elementa 3 system in Ho Chi Minh City as data centres boost Vietnam's electricity demand. Trinasolar has unveiled its Vertex N G3 TOPCon 3.0 solar modules, with a power output of up to 760 W, along with Trina Storage's 6.25 MWh Elementa 3 battery energy storage system (BESS), at an event in Ho Chi Minh City. According to the group, the products expand its photovoltaic and storage offering in Vietnam, where industrial growth and artificial intelligence data centres are increasing electricity demand. The regional solar and battery market is also seeing smaller projects emerge, such as Audax's commissioning of the 4.12 MWp El Rebollo plant or Tavion's launch of battery parks in Bydgoszcz. Demand driven by data centres The International Energy Agency (IEA) projects global data centre electricity consumption to rise from approximately 485 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030. Vietnam's digital infrastructure strategy also calls for the development of artificial intelligence data centres and hyperscale data centres by 2030. Trinasolar says the Vertex N G3 and Elementa 3 address the generation and storage needs associated with this growth. The company points to greater use of solar electricity to supply these sites. Company TrinaSolar: company profile Vertex N G3 module features The Vertex N G3 is built on the manufacturer's TOPCon 3.0 cell technology and incorporates four technological upgrades. An "Ultra" cell platform increases power output and bifacial performance. Multi-cut and edge passivation technologies reduce current losses and improve shading and hot-spot performance, while ultra-high density packaging improves module efficiency and energy yield. The module has a bifaciality of 85% Â± 5%, which supports additional rear-side generation where site conditions allow. artigo.texto: 13/10/2026 A Câmara dos Deputados pode votar na tarde desta terça-feira, 13 de outubro, o requerimento de urgência do Projeto de Lei (PL) 3.716/2026, que altera o rateio dos custos da contratação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias (BESS). A proposta busca transferir aos consumidores o custeio atualmente atribuído aos geradores e tem o apoio de seis associações do setor elétrico, que defendem a mudança para garantir isonomia entre as tecnologias contratadas nos leilões de reserva de capacidade. Caso a urgência seja aprovada, o projeto poderá ser analisado diretamente pelo plenário, sem precisar concluir a tramitação nas comissões. O PL 3.716/2026 revoga um dispositivo da Lei 10.848/2004, incluído pela Lei 15.269/2025, que determina que os custos das contratações de reserva de capacidade com baterias sejam rateados exclusivamente entre os agentes de geração, conforme regulamentação da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). Em nota conjunta divulgada em 7 de outubro, seis associações do setor elétrico defenderam a aprovação urgente do projeto. As entidades argumentam que o modelo atual cria uma diferença de tratamento entre as baterias e outras tecnologias que prestam serviços de reserva de capacidade, cujos custos são distribuídos entre os usuários finais de energia elétrica. O posicionamento é assinado pela Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias (Abeeólica), Associação Brasileira dos Investidores em Autoprodução de Energia (Abiape), Associação Brasileira da Indústria do Hidrogênio Verde (Abihv), Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (Absae), Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (Absolar) e Associação Brasileira dos Produtores Independentes de Energia Elétrica (Apine). As entidades alertam que a atribuição dos custos exclusivamente aos geradores pode encarecer a energia elétrica para os consumidores e reduzir a competitividade da indústria brasileira. Modelo de custeio das baterias Na avaliação das associações, a reserva de capacidade tem como objetivo garantir a segurança do suprimento de energia elétrica, assegurando potência e flexibilidade para a operação confiável do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). Esses atributos podem ser fornecidos por diferentes tecnologias, que, segundo as entidades, devem receber tratamento equivalente. Atualmente, os custos da reserva de capacidade são distribuídos entre os usuários finais, conforme os parâmetros legais previstos no artigo 3º-A da Lei nº 10.848/2004. No entanto, os sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias recebem tratamento diferente, com os custos atribuídos exclusivamente aos geradores, conforme determinou a Lei n° 15.269/2025. Para as entidades, essa regra cria um descompasso entre a natureza sistêmica do serviço prestado, a distribuição de seus benefícios e a responsabilidade pelo pagamento dos custos. Baterias podem gerar economia de R$ 1,6 bilhão por ano As associações argumentam que os sistemas de armazenamento de energia, inclusive os baseados em baterias, podem contribuir para reduzir outros encargos pagos pelos consumidores ao otimizar a operação do parque gerador. Como exemplo, a nota cita um estudo da Volt Robotics segundo o qual os sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias podem reduzir a variação do Preço de Liquidação das Diferenças (PLD) e o acionamento de usinas termelétricas, gerando uma economia superior a R$ 1,6 bilhão por ano para os consumidores. O documento também destaca que atribuir legalmente os custos aos geradores não impede que eles sejam repassados aos consumidores finais. No mercado regulado, as entidades mencionam o reconhecimento, pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel), da inclusão integral e automática desses custos nas tarifas de energia. No mercado livre, o impacto pode ocorrer por meio de renegociações ou reajustes de preços. Já na autoprodução de energia, os custos podem ser incorporados aos preços de bens e serviços, afetando a competitividade da indústria brasileira. As associações acrescentam que o pagamento do encargo pelo segmento de geração pode elevar os custos para os consumidores devido ao repasse dos valores, acrescidos de tributos e despesas administrativas. Data centers e hidrogênio verde entram no debate A nota também relaciona a expansão da eletrificação da economia à necessidade de discutir a responsabilidade pelo custeio da reserva de capacidade. Segundo as entidades, novas cargas, como veículos elétricos, data centers e projetos industriais eletrointensivos, incluindo parques produtores de hidrogênio verde, influenciam a demanda máxima de energia e o déficit de capacidade do sistema. Na avaliação das associações, esses consumidores também podem contribuir para reduzir o déficit de capacidade caso recebam sinais econômicos adequados para ajustar sua demanda. Por isso, as entidades defendem que as baterias sejam tratadas em igualdade com as demais soluções de capacidade, considerando os atributos de potência e flexibilidade. O objetivo, segundo a nota, é permitir a contratação da tecnologia mais eficiente para cada cenário e reduzir os custos finais com transparência. Fonte: MegaWhat

artigo.texto: Energia hidroelétrica. A “arma-secreta” portuguesa para armazenamento Como podemos tirar maior proveito dos recursos naturais em Portugal para aumentar a capacidade de armazenamento da nossa rede elétrica? A transição energética depende do armazenamento e esta realidade tornou-se mais evidente nos últimos anos. Hoje, as redes modernas e de maior eletrificação, como as redes portuguesa e ibérica, enfrentam desafios relacionados com a interoperabilidade, a flexibilidade, maiores consumos energéticos e maior complexidade dos sistemas, que exigem soluções inovadoras. Estas soluções podem também residir no armazenamento. O conceito de armazenamento de energia abrange diferentes tecnologias, algumas mais maduras e outras mais inovadoras, sistemas híbridos e controlos digitais que nos permitem deslocar a procura e a oferta de energia e controlá-las de acordo com as necessidades. Um dos tipos de armazenamento, complexo em termos de maturidade, aplicação histórica e efeitos na rede, é a energia hidroelétrica e a bombagem. “Energia hidroelétrica” não é a primeira palavra que se associaria ao armazenamento. Quanto à produção, a energia hidroelétrica é a tecnologia de produção de energia renovável mais difundida e madura, fornecendo um sexto da eletricidade global atual, mais do que todas as outras fontes renováveis combinadas, de acordo com a IEA. Esta disponibilidade e maturidade resultaram também no desenvolvimento do seu verdadeiro potencial para o armazenamento de energia: a bombagem hídrica, ou Pumped-Storage Hydropower. Esta tecnologia de bombagem hídrica representou, em 2020, 95% de toda a capacidade de armazenamento de energia instalada a nível global (International Hydropower Association, 2023). A União Europeia reconheceu a importância das tecnologias de armazenamento por bombagem para a mitigação das alterações climáticas e para o futuro dos sistemas energéticos, no relatório “Hydropower and pumped storage hydropower in the EU” (Joint Research Centre, 2025). Em Portugal, é evidente a predominância da energia hidroelétrica como fonte de energia, com uma contribuição no mix energético de 30%. A Estratégia Nacional de Armazenamento de Energia, recentemente lançada, visa atingir 10,5 GW total de armazenamento de energia em 2040, incluindo baterias e bombagem. Portugal dispõe atualmente de uma capacidade de de 3,6 gigawatts (GW) apenas em sistemas hidroelétricos de armazenamento por bombagem, que o governo pretende quase duplicar para 5,6 GW em 2040, confirmando o protagonismo que deve ser atribuído a esta tecnologia em termos de potencial de armazenamento e mecanismos de proteção da rede. Atualmente, Portugal já dispõe de várias centrais hidroelétricas com bombagem que contribuem para a rede nacional. As centrais de Alqueva, Alto Lindoso, Frades II e, mais recentemente, o complexo de Gouvães, no Tâmega, não só trouxeram mais energia limpa para a rede, como também estão a contribuir significativamente para o seu equilíbrio e para o aumento da utilização de outras energias renováveis. Só o complexo hidroelétrico do Tâmega contribuiu para aumentar a capacidade de armazenamento da rede portuguesa em mais de 40 milhões de kWh, o equivalente ao consumo de energia de 11 milhões de pessoas durante 24 horas (Iberdrola, 2026). A barragem de Alqueva acrescenta mais 10 GWh de capacidade de armazenamento ao sistema. Esta barragem participou no projeto de inovação XFLEX Hydro, financiado pela UE, no âmbito do qual se testaram soluções operacionais inovadoras. Este projeto permitiu uma melhor compreensão das capacidades das centrais hidroelétricas nacionais para proporcionar flexibilidade energética à rede portuguesa, comprovando que são capazes de prestar serviços como inércia sintética e aumentando as suas capacidades para fornecer outros serviços de frequência, serviços de Black Start e Controlo de Tensão. Todos estes serviços são cruciais em redes dominadas por energias renováveis, uma vez que permitem equilibrar a rede de forma a prevenir eventos como o Apagão na Península Ibérica de 2025. A utilização de sistemas de armazenamento por bombagem permite assim proteger a integridade da rede. A utilização das tecnologias de armazenamento com hidroelétricas em benefício da rede já não está limitada pelos desenvolvimentos tecnológicos, dependendo sim de mudanças políticas e regulamentares. É agora necessário analisar a regulamentação das redes em toda a Europa e em Portugal e eliminar as barreiras regulamentares existentes. As mesmas barreiras regulatórias aplicam-se à falta de remuneração de serviços de sistema específicos ou a criação de mercados que garantam a prestação de serviços auxiliares a custos mais baixos, o que incentivaria o investimento em novos sistemas de armazenamento flexíveis. Ao mesmo tempo, existe um grande número de centrais hidrelétricas envelhecidas que não estão a atingir o seu pleno potencial. A participação em projetos de inovação e o aumento dos recursos do meio académico para implementar novas tecnologias podem trazer benefícios para a modernização do portfólio energético. Através de estratégias nacionais como a portuguesa, é possível observar como a energia hidroelétrica e, em particular, as soluções de armazenamento por bombagem, têm tido e continuarão a ter um papel fundamental na eletrificação, flexibilização e modernização das redes. Tendo em conta os recursos naturais a que o país tem acesso, faz todo o sentido recorrer a eles e utilizá-los de forma respeitosa, de modo a permitir o objetivo global de mitigar as alterações climáticas e proteger esses próprios recursos naturais. Nota: Esta é uma coluna fruto da parceria entre a Women in ESG Portugal e o Mulheres na Energia (Associação Portuguesa da Energia) para o ECO. Por meio deste canal pretendemos trazer conteúdos ligados ao ESG e Energia de forma descomplicada para a sociedade, na voz de mulheres, de gerações diferentes, que detêm expertise técnica na área. artigo.texto: Projeto da Mombak prevê restaurar 7,2 mil hectares e gerar créditos de carbono; operação anterior eleva a R$ 360 milhões o financiamento do banco à empresa restauração de áreas degradadas na Amazônia é uma necessidade ambiental, mas, quando uma operação privada destinada a recuperar florestas também abre caminho para a geração e comercialização de créditos de carbono, o dinheiro público exige uma conta completa: quanto custa, quais resultados entrega e quem fica com os ganhos econômicos. O Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) aprovou financiamento de R$ 200 milhões para a Mombak, empresa especializada em projetos de remoção de carbono. O empreendimento prevê restaurar 7,2 mil hectares, principalmente no Pará, com investimento total estimado em R$ 457 milhões e prazo de financiamento de 25 anos. Segundo o banco, o projeto poderá remover mais de 4,7 milhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono equivalente ao longo de 50 anos, com potencial de gerar até 4,7 milhões de créditos de remoção de carbono. Esses ativos poderão ser negociados no mercado voluntário e, futuramente, em mercados regulados. A operação foi anunciada pelo BNDES em 21 de setembro. O financiamento representa aproximadamente 44% do investimento previsto. Em uma conta direta, equivale a cerca de R$ 27,8 mil por hectare em recursos financiados pelo banco. Considerado o investimento total, o custo projetado chega a R$ 63,5 mil por hectare. Os números, isoladamente, não demonstram desperdício nem irregularidade. A restauração florestal envolve preparo do solo, aquisição de sementes e mudas, plantio, manejo, manutenção e monitoramento. O que eles justificam é uma pergunta objetiva sobre as condições financeiras e os resultados esperados de uma operação dessa dimensão. O projeto não se limita à recomposição da vegetação nativa. A captura de carbono prevista poderá dar origem a créditos comercializáveis, criando uma fonte potencial de receita para o empreendimento. É um modelo econômico que pode contribuir para a recuperação de áreas degradadas e para o enfrentamento das mudanças climáticas. Mas a combinação de financiamento público de longo prazo com receitas futuras provenientes de ativos ambientais também exige transparência sobre a distribuição dos riscos e dos benefícios. Quais são os juros e as demais condições contratuais do financiamento? Que garantias foram exigidas? Quem será titular dos créditos gerados e como se dará sua comercialização? Se a captura de carbono ficar abaixo das projeções ou os preços dos créditos caírem, quem absorverá os prejuízos? São questões que não pressupõem qualquer irregularidade. Constituem, porém, parte necessária da avaliação de um empreendimento apoiado por uma política pública. O financiamento de R$ 200 milhões não é o primeiro concedido pelo BNDES à Mombak. Em agosto de 2024, o banco anunciou uma operação de R$ 160 milhões para projetos de restauração de 13 mil hectares na Amazônia. Naquela primeira operação, os recursos foram divididos entre R$ 80 milhões do Fundo Clima e R$ 80 milhões da linha BNDES Finem. Portanto, não se deve confundir o valor total do financiamento com a parcela proveniente especificamente do Fundo Clima. Com a nova operação, os financiamentos aprovados para a empresa somam R$ 360 milhões, enquanto os dois projetos preveem recuperar aproximadamente 20,2 mil hectares. Segundo o BNDES, até junho de 2026, 9,4 mil hectares do primeiro empreendimento já haviam sido implantados. O dado permite avançar na apuração. Quais resultados ambientais já podem ser medidos? Quanto foi efetivamente desembolsado e qual é o cronograma dos recursos restantes? Que indicadores de sobrevivência das árvores, recuperação da biodiversidade e remoção de carbono estão sendo utilizados para avaliar o projeto anterior? E de que maneira esses resultados foram considerados na aprovação do novo financiamento? A previsão divulgada pelo banco é de até 440 empregos diretos e 65 indiretos durante a implantação do novo projeto. Depois dessa fase, a estimativa é manter aproximadamente 50 postos de trabalho, entre diretos e indiretos. A diferença entre o emprego temporário e o permanente não invalida o empreendimento. Projetos de restauração podem produzir benefícios ambientais duradouros sem depender de uma grande estrutura permanente de pessoal. Ainda assim, é pertinente conhecer a parcela dos investimentos que permanecerá na economia paraense, a participação de fornecedores locais e as oportunidades abertas aos moradores das áreas abrangidas. A recuperação da floresta pode gerar benefícios muito além da captura de carbono, mas esses resultados precisam ser identificados e acompanhados. Também importa saber onde estão as áreas contempladas, quais são as condições dos contratos com os proprietários e como serão monitorados os resultados ambientais ao longo das décadas previstas para a operação. A Amazônia precisa de floresta em pé. Precisa igualmente de ciência, saneamento, infraestrutura, regularização fundiária, fiscalização, bioeconomia e geração de renda para quem vive no território. O desafio é impedir que a valorização econômica do carbono se descole dos interesses ambientais e sociais da região que o produz. Restaurar florestas com financiamento público pode ser uma política acertada. Mas o resultado não deve ser medido apenas pelo número de hectares recuperados ou de toneladas de CO₂ que se espera retirar da atmosfera. É preciso saber quanto custará a recuperação, quais benefícios serão comprovados, como os riscos serão distribuídos e quem ficará com a receita gerada pelos créditos de carbono. •Os rumores chegaram ao fim no sábado, 10. A prefeita de Marituba, Patrícia Alencar (foto), anunciou nas redes sociais que está grávida de uma menina, fruto do relacionamento com o prefeito de Mãe do Rio, Bruno Rabelo. Agora é esperar a chegada da pequena - e desejar saúde à futura mamãe e à bebê. •Deputados que andavam de olho na área da saúde do Estado podem tirar o cavalinho da chuva.

artigo.texto: The government is building an international carbon market that companies can use not only to trade voluntary greenhouse gas reduction credits but also to meet regulatory requirements, including national emissions targets. To that end, it will split the credit issuance system into two categories and begin full-scale operation of the Global Verified Carbon Market (GVCM) next year. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance and Economy Lee Hyoung-il discussed the detailed implementation plan for the GVCM at a ministerial meeting on international economic affairs on the 12th. The GVCM is designed to spur trading in greenhouse gas reduction credits, whose credibility has been questioned because of a lack of internationally standardized criteria. The government fleshed out the operating framework based on a roadmap announced in December last year. Credits will first be divided into two types depending on whether the host country of a project has approved their transfer. Credits approved for transfer, designated "GVCM A," can be used to meet an investing country's nationally determined contribution (NDC) or to comply with regulations in the international aviation sector. Credits without such approval, designated "GVCM NA," will be used for companies' voluntary environmental activities. Their scope of use can be expanded if the host country grants approval later. The government will also review linking the credits to the domestic emissions trading scheme and the greenhouse gas target management system if certain conditions are met. In line with that shift, the market's previous name, the Global Voluntary Carbon Market, has been changed, with "Voluntary" replaced by "Verified." To improve the credibility of transactions, key information such as project operators and reduction volumes will be recorded on a blockchain. The government plans to build the trading platform using the Korea Exchange (KRX) and to consider issuing credits in the form of digital assets in the future. The government will secure participating countries this year and form an issuing body next year to flesh out the project. It will also discuss converting credits generated by greenhouse gas reduction projects of the World Bank (WB) and the Green Climate Fund (GCF) into GVCM credits. The meeting also reaffirmed existing plans, including the creation of a 3 trillion won ($2.1 billion) overseas construction fund, follow-up negotiations on the South Korea-China free trade agreement (FTA), and an industrial complex in India dedicated to Korean companies. Lee said exports have maintained solid momentum, noting that the current account posted a surplus of $46.11 billion in August. He cited trade issues with the U.S., supply chain instability and the possibility of adjustments in artificial intelligence (AI) investment as external risks. "The government will respond to external uncertainties without wavering as one economic team and create new growth opportunities," Lee said.

artigo.texto: "BUMDs need to start identifying carbon units or activities that can be properly maintained and developed as a basis to drive regional revenue," Jumhur told reporters in Jakarta on Tuesday. He made the statement after delivering his opening remarks at a technical briefing for regional leaders on Carbon Pricing Implementation and Climate-Resilient Low-Carbon Development. Jumhur said that regional enterprises can turn carbon trading into a reliable revenue source while maintaining strict land management standards, ensuring that regional carbon potential remains well-preserved in the process. He then pointed to mangrove restoration as an example, noting that mangroves can absorb around 3,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent per hectare annually. Based on an estimated carbon offset rate of US$50 to US$60 per ton, the carbon value from a hectare of mangroves could reach around US$150,000. Beyond local revenue potential, Jumhur stressed that regional governments must ensure the financial benefits of carbon trading reach local communities, in line with the central government's expectations. According to Jumhur, the need to build local capacity around carbon pricing governance is also important, so that regional leaders can accurately understand carbon market mechanisms and opportunities. Clear communication between central and local governments is essential, he added, to ensure that carbon market development yields maximum benefits for the public. He expressed hope that, with BUMD involvement, regional environmental potential can be developed into economic activities that boost local revenue while benefiting communities. artigo.texto: China's AI chip crunch is pushing some of its biggest tech groups to look abroad for compute power, and Southeast Asia is quietly becoming one of the beneficiaries. This pressure cooker of demand, capex and export rules is creating fresh attention on regional data center and cloud infrastructure stocks that could either ride a multiyear buildout or struggle to keep up. This article walks through 3 stocks exposed to that theme and what their AI data center story might mean for your portfolio. The 3 stocks in this article are just a starting sample, and the full screen surfaced 54 more companies with equally compelling narratives that are not covered here. Overview: Insight Enterprises helps enterprises design, buy, and run multicloud, data center, AI, security, and workplace technology across global markets. artigo.texto: Unlocking the Green Story Behind Containment Sealed containment material delivers real, measurable carbon savings in data centers—so why isn't anyone reporting it? October 14, 2026 The growth of AI-driven power and cooling demands is putting data center operators under much harsher scrutiny when it comes to environmental impact. Sustainability mandates mean more questions are being asked of operators’ carbon footprints, PUE gradings, and long-term net-zero commitments. While ambitious green roadmaps, solar power purchase agreements, and liquid cooling systems all check the carbon-reduction box, one of the simplest sustainability wins is already happening in many data halls. Yet the material used to seal and fully enclose either horizontal or vertical containment, a product already installed and doing its job, barely gets mentioned. A Sealed Story, Left Untold Hot aisle and cold aisle containment is standard practice in modern data centers. The containment roof panel for cold aisle containment and vertical panel for hot aisle containment, and the material used, is often treated as a minor detail within a much larger cooling strategy. There is often one detail that goes unaddressed: openings above the cold aisle containment due to a lack of roof system, and openings above the hot aisle due to containment not going up to the plenum ceiling, and it's been driving up cooling costs since the day the facility opened. It's not an oversight or a design flaw. It's a direct byproduct of adhering to fire code. Sprinkler heads are engineered for the widest possible dispersal pattern to maximize coverage in a fire event and fully sealing or enclosing the top of the cold aisle with a roof system or with vertical panels above the hot aisle and up to the plenum ceiling can take the facility out of compliance with the fire code. That leaves facility operators with two options: - To leave the roof system off of cold aisle containment or to leave at least 24” of containment off the top of the vertical hot aisle containment up to the plenum ceiling, preserving the sprinkler's coverage pattern at the cost of a fully sealed containment system; or - Install sprinkler heads in every single aisle, which solves the dispersal problem but comes with a catch — a layout that made sense at commissioning rarely stays fixed for the life of the facility, and a sprinkler system built around a specific aisle plan doesn't adapt easily when that plan changes. Most facilities take the first option. It's simpler, cheaper, and satisfies fire code, but it also means that either the cold or hot aisle containment system is not fully sealed and contained, allowing the hot air to rise, drift across the gap, and mix back into the cold aisle. This design undoes some of the benefits that the containment system just performed, and the HVAC system compensates by working even harder. This is a constant, low-grade condition and rarely gets flagged as an issue. Instead, it shows up as elevated energy costs and lower cooling efficiency, spread across the operational life of the facility in a way that's easy to normalize and tough to trace back to its origin. However, closing the openings outright isn't as simple as adding a horizontal roof or vertical panels for the physical containment seal. Doing that just reintroduces the original problem of fire code compliance. If the suppression system can't detect a fire fast enough because the containment is fully sealed, it becomes a real hazard. Why DAB Panels Are the Overlooked Asset DAB panels solve a problem that has limited containment for years. Traditional roof panels can obstruct sprinkler coverage, force relocation of sprinkler heads, or get rejected outright by the local Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ). DAB panels are currently the only approved product that seals the horizontal gap over the cold aisle without triggering those concerns. The same is true with hot aisle vertical panels up to the plenum ceiling. DAB panels that are made from an EPA-certified, plant-based cellulose composite provide a continuous seal across the top of a contained aisle. Cooling equipment runs closer to design conditions instead of continuously compensating for leaked airflow, and panels can be easily cut, configured and fitted on-site around cable trays, pipes, and other overhead obstructions, ideal for both new builds and retrofits. Paired with a purpose-built passive airflow flap, a small mechanism fitted with a melting fuse plug, DAB panels keep the containment seal closed and intact under normal operating conditions, letting the HVAC system run at full efficiency. If a fire starts and aisle temperature rises, the fuse plugs melt, the flap opens, and hot air is immediately released upward for cold aisle containment and outward for hot aisle containment to the sprinkler activation system. The sprinklers dissolve the DAB panels within 30 seconds, removing the risk of any falling-object hazard that might restrict egress, so response time stays fast and AHJs stay satisfied. This is a design that fire protection engineers have reviewed and signed off on directly. A fully sealed cold or hot aisle, paired with airflow flaps where needed, meets fire code requirements without compromising fire suppression response times. Why the Disconnect Exists DAB panels are being adopted because they solve a fire-safety-versus-efficiency conflict that had nothing to do with ESG reporting. They weren't adopted because someone was chasing a carbon number. That's why the sustainability benefit has gone unclaimed. It's a side effect of a sound engineering decision. Containment sealing is typically a facilities and procurement decision, evaluated on cooling performance, installation cost, and code compliance, not on its contribution to a corporate carbon disclosure. artigo.texto: Residents and local officials in Kenosha County are pushing back on a utility-scale standalone battery project being proposed in the town of Wheatland. Robin Energy Storage, a subsidiary of Danish investment firm Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, filed an application with state regulators late last month seeking approval for a 200-megawatt battery energy storage system, or BESS. While Kenosha County is already home to the Paris Solar and Battery Park, this storage project wouldn’t be charged up by a specific generation resource. Instead, it would draw power from the grid at periods of low demand and discharge that energy back onto the grid at times of high demand. Understanding Wisconsin, Together. WPR’s “Wisconsin Today” newsletter keeps you connected to the state you love without feeling overwhelmed. No paywall. No agenda. No corporate filter. “It’s not connected to a data center, a solar farm, wind turbines or anything — it’s connected to the overall grid, and it just provides stability,” said Scott McPherson, a spokesperson for Robin Energy Storage. “It can provide energy when it’s needed under peak demands. It would be storing energy when there’s excess capacity.” While the company argues the project could help boost reliability for Wisconsin’s energy grid, residents have raised potential safety concerns as well as concerns about the loss of rural character in the community. Wheatland Town Board Supervisor Kyle Madsen said the town’s planning commission voted against the proposal before the developer filed its application with the state Public Service Commission. He said he’s against the battery project because he feels there are too many unknowns. “We’re not against making progress or anything like that,” Madsen said. “It’s just, what’s the best fit for our town? And we do not believe, at this point in time, that these standalone battery storage facilities should move forward within our town.” County leaders say developer is trying ‘sidestep’ locals At the county level, officials have framed the company’s application with the PSC as an effort to “sidestep” a countywide moratorium on battery energy storage systems. Kenosha County Executive Samantha Kerkman said the county established zoning requirements for battery storage systems in 2024 after learning of a potential battery storage proposal. The county passed an initial moratorium while it was working on those regulations. This May, the county passed another moratorium, citing “potential health and safety issues” and “changes in technology and circumstances” around battery systems. Kerkman said she believes counties have a role to play when it comes to regulating utility-scale battery projects. “The Public Service Commission does have the right to regulate BESS systems that are attached to large-scale solar projects,” she said. “I believe state statute does give them that authority. But for the standalone BESS systems, there’s no statutes with regards to the PSC’s authority to regulate those.” Under state law, electric generation facilities with a capacity of 100 megawatts or more generally require siting approval from the state Public Service Commission rather than local governments. That applies to natural gas power plants and large-scale solar and wind projects. PSC staff believe a standalone battery project of 100 megawatts or more would generally be subject to the same requirement, but it will ultimately be up to the commission itself to review the facts and make a determination, according to an agency spokesperson. “The Commission carefully reviews all applications it receives and will render a decision in accordance with the applicable law and Commission’s authority,” the spokesperson said via email. McPherson, the spokesperson for Robin Energy Storage, said the company was not trying to sidestep local governments. He said they filed their application after the PSC released new rules this year giving developers more clarity in applying for standalone battery projects at the state level. “We were working at the local level all the way. The state came up with their rules. Now we’re going to the state,” he said. “Pretty cut and dried.” Safety concerns fuel debate Aside from disagreements over regulatory authority, Kerkman said the county’s experience with the existing storage facility in Paris has raised concerns about another battery proposal in the county. She said maintenance alarms have been going off “on a very regular basis” at the battery facility in Paris since around May, requiring first responders to show up to make sure it’s just a maintenance alarm. We Energies is the majority owner of the Paris battery project. Spokesperson Brendan Conway said in an email that the utility is working with first responders to address “alarm notification issues” at the Paris site. He said the company appreciates “their partnership as we resolve the matter.” Conway said the batteries in Paris are “providing energy to the grid regularly, including supporting customers during periods of peak electricity demand.” While standalone battery proposals are relatively new in Wisconsin, Ciaran Gallagher, energy and air manager at the nonprofit Clean Wisconsin, said the technology is the same as the technology used in the battery systems paired with solar farms. She said that risks of fires or explosions tied to utility-scale battery storage have generally decreased as the technology has become more widely adopted. “There have been some fires at batteries in the United States, but that risk is pretty low, especially as the technology has developed and the fire safety measures around it have developed,” Gallagher said. “I think all energy systems come with some element of risk.” A new report from the national nonprofit Electric Power Research Institute shows the failure rate for BESS systems dropped by 98 percent from 2018 to 2025. artigo.texto: The domestic carbon market, which began operating on June 29, marks an important step in Vietnam's green transition while highlighting the need for stronger financial mechanisms to support its development, he said at a workshop on credit policy and carbon markets in Hanoi on October 14. The event was organised by VIR in coordination with the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) at VIR's headquarters. “If the carbon exchange is the market’s infrastructure, credit policy, the banking system and capital markets are the driving forces behind the green transition,” Hoanh said. Credit policy plays a leading role in directing financial resources towards emissions reduction, helping businesses and individuals invest in greener activities and linking sustainable development objectives with the flow of capital throughout the economy. The green transition ultimately requires tangible investments in cleaner technologies, energy efficiency, changes to production processes, low-emission agriculture, forest protection and development, waste treatment, renewable energy and more sustainable supply chains. "To bring these projects to fruition, Vietnam needs a financial system capable of identifying, pricing, allocating and managing green capital," said Hoanh. Vietnam’s carbon market framework was established under the 2020 Law on Environmental Protection and subsequently developed through a series of legal documents. The latest regulations include Decree No.29/2026/ND-CP on the domestic carbon exchange and Decree No.112/2026/ND-CP on international exchanges of greenhouse gas emission reduction outcomes and carbon credits. Vietnam has also gained experience in monetising verified emissions reductions on international markets. In 2024, the country received its first $51.5 million payment from the World Bank for 10.3 million tonnes of verified emission reductions under the North Central Region Emission Reductions Programme. The launch of allowance trading on 29 June 2026 introduced a new way of recognising the economic value of emissions reductions. However, the establishment of a trading platform alone will not ensure the market's long-term success. "A sustainable carbon market also requires liquidity, reliable data, verification mechanisms, confidence among buyers and sellers, and a strong financial ecosystem to support market participants," Hoanh said. He highlighted several questions that policymakers, financial institutions and businesses need to address, including how to remove regulatory and financial bottlenecks, channel green capital towards the right projects, and enable banks to assess both the opportunities and risks associated with green investments. Businesses must also be able to demonstrate the effectiveness of their transition efforts and access bank lending along with medium- and long-term financing from capital markets. Meanwhile, carbon value needs to become an increasingly reliable factor in financial decision-making. These challenges were among the reasons VIR organised the workshop, bringing together policymakers, banks, businesses, experts and other stakeholders to exchange views and identify practical solutions. "The carbon market would create a new economic driver when businesses could see the financial benefits of emissions reductions, banks and capital market institutions could manage green capital effectively, investors could identify value, and producers received commensurate benefits," said Hoanh. He expressed his hope that discussions at the workshop would lead to concrete policy proposals, practical cooperation initiatives, and models that could be implemented in practice. The event forms part of broader efforts to connect Vietnam’s carbon market development with credit policy and capital mobilisation, helping ensure that the country’s green transition is supported by the financial resources needed to deliver measurable results. The workshop featured presentations by the SBV, the Asian Development Bank, and Agribank, followed by a discussion with representatives from regulatory authorities, capital markets, banks, businesses, and consulting organisations. Key topics included expanding green capital flows, improving businesses' access to finance, developing the carbon market, and strengthening the links between emissions reduction value and financial decision-making.

artigo.texto: For many years, the price of both solid state drives (SSDs) and hard drives (HDDs) were decreasing in price. About a year ago, I bought a 5TB HDD for backing up my desktop and paid $130 through Amazon. Today, that same drive is $230. People throughout the tech industry have seen the doubling of pricing across the board when it comes to computer storage. And, like so many things in the world today, you can blame AI. While so many are protesting the creation of massive data centers around the country with worries over higher electricity bills and environmental concerns, a slightly more niche issue has emerged thanks to AI’s need for computing power. Hard drives, for portable external ones to replacements for your PC, are going way up in price as data center companies swallow up as much storage as they can get their hands on. The surge in demand has rippled across the technology industry and hit the hard drive market particularly severely, which is ironic considering speculation over the last decade was that the need for hardware like this would slowly disappear with a shift into the cloud. But, data centers have rapidly changed the math when it comes to storage. And hard drive prices aren’t alone. Since early 2025, the price of RAM, once a fairly inexpensive upgrade that has been declining in price for decades, is now through the roof. What cost less than $100 in some cases to upgrade in early 2025 now runs three to four times that, what the industry has dubbed RAMageddon. Some of this might feel like much ado about nothing in the grander scheme of AI’s potential risks to the world and humanity itself, but if you need to make what used to be a pretty easy and cheap upgrade to your computer or storage, suddenly like gas, eggs and virtually everything else, you are going to pay more. And, there really is no clear sign that things will slow down, No doubt manufacturers will begin to stabilize pricing as they produce more tech, but no one would blame them if they didn’t. AI’s rise is still a huge gamble and many people in the technology world have predicted that data centers may eventually be replaced by smaller and cheaper tech options. For now, it just means more money out of your pocket thanks to AI.
