artigo.texto: Marco Rubio warns the Ukraine… Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan signed a… India’s annual battery storage installations are set to nearly double every year by the 2032 fiscal year, as the renewable energy boom drives increased investment in battery energy storage systems (BESS), a new report by Nuvama has shown. Total BESS capacity installations in India are expected to jump to 302 gigawatt-hours (GWh) in 2032, up from just 6.3 GWh at present, suggesting a compound annual growth rate of 91% during the period, analysts at Nuvama wrote in the report carried by Indian media. India’s Central Electricity Authority estimates BESS installations would reach 236 GWh by FY32, lower than the estimates of Nuvama analysts, and 1,840 GWh by 2047. As India’s renewable energy capacity soars, the country will need increased battery storage installations to support the growth and allow greater grid flexibility, the India Energy Storage Alliance (IESA) said last month. According to discussions at the IESA Chennai Connect 2026, India will require about 888 GWh of energy storage capacity by 2035-36 to meet rising electricity demand and support reliable integration of renewable power. “Energy storage will be one of the defining technologies of India’s energy transition,” said Ashok Jhunjhunwala, Institute Professor at IIT Madras. “Renewable energy must stay at the forefront, but it needs to be supported by storage to build a stronger, more reliable, and increasingly affordable power system.” India has realized it needs to scale up its battery storage installations significantly to proceed with the rapid growth of renewable energy sources. India’s authorities plan to introduce, from July 1, 2027, a regulation requiring developers of solar and wind energy projects to have battery storage installed at the sites in a bid to better manage the renewable energy output and reduce curtailments. Despite a major solar and wind installations boom in recent years, India has been struggling to fully utilize the capacities because output has often been curtailed due to the lack of battery storage. artigo.texto: - Saudi Arabia can deliver electricity to AI data centers faster than the US, leveraging its advanced infrastructure and clear expansion plans, according to Siemens Energy CEO Christian Bruch. - The rapid speed of power delivery is crucial for competing in the AI industry, with even a six-month difference in data center launch impacting development significantly. - Saudi Arabia's strategic infrastructure planning includes clear targets through 2030, facilitating easier project implementation compared to other countries. - Siemens Energy is investing $150 million to expand its Dammam facility, which will include a new transformer factory and create 130 to 150 jobs. - Siemens Energy aims to establish local manufacturing capabilities to bolster energy security and reduce reliance on international supply chains. - The company plans to make Dammam a regional hub for power system repairs and local talent development, further enhancing its operational capabilities by 2030. JEDDAH: Saudi Arabia can supply electricity to AI data centers faster than the US, giving it an edge in attracting computing investments through its advanced power infrastructure and clear plans to expand generation capacity, Siemens Energy CEO Christian Bruch has said. Speaking to Mohammed Fathi of Asharq Bloomberg at the company’s Dammam facility, Bruch said the speed of power delivery has become a key factor in competing for AI projects. He added that advancing or delaying a data center’s launch by six months can make a significant difference as artificial intelligence and superintelligence technologies develop rapidly. Asked whether the Kingdom could supply electricity to data centers faster than the US, Bruch said: “Yes, I think so.” He noted that Saudi Arabia had made significant progress in developing its power infrastructure in recent years and had a clear, coordinated plan for adding new generation capacity. This comes as the company invests around $150 million to expand its Dammam facility, adding 60,000 sq. meters and establishing a factory for large power transformers. The expansion is also expected to create around 130 to 150 additional jobs, as the company seeks to strengthen local manufacturing, serve Saudi demand and export to international markets. Saudi Arabia’s planning and execution advantage Bruch described Saudi Arabia as “a model for strategic infrastructure planning,” saying its clear targets through 2030 and defined electricity generation requirements help suppliers plan and deliver projects in phases, making the process more straightforward than in other countries. He said the Kingdom could also supply electricity to data centers at “highly competitive” costs, enhancing its appeal to companies seeking locations for their investments. Data center operators would find Saudi Arabia a suitable location for their projects, he added, noting that the US “will not always remain the only destination.” Asked about discussions with Humain, Bruch did not disclose any specific agreements but said he expected further announcements on larger-scale, higher-capacity data center computing projects in Saudi Arabia. He added that Siemens Energy’s role is to supply equipment, while other entities would handle operations. Major transformer factory planned for Dammam The Dammam expansion marks another step in Siemens Energy’s industrial development in the Kingdom. The company began with a gas turbine factory, later added compressors for the oil and gas sector, and opened a facility for electrical switchgear used in the power grid last year, according to Bruch. He noted that the new transformer factory would be one of the company’s key manufacturing facilities in this field globally, with production capacity sufficient to serve both the Saudi market and international markets. He added that a further expansion phase could be implemented in the future if business develops in line with the company’s expectations. Bruch did not specify the plant’s annual production capacity but said it would manufacture large power transformers for high-voltage networks, including Saudi Arabia’s main 380-kilovolt transmission grid. He further said: “What we need is clarity on the stability of the environment — in other words, is there sustained demand? Is there a long-term strategy? And that is what I see in Saudi Arabia today.” The investment builds on Siemens Energy’s major contracts in the Kingdom. In June 2024, the company announced a deal worth around $1.5 billion to supply key technologies for the Taiba 2 and Qassim 2 gas-fired power plants, alongside a 25-year maintenance agreement. Each plant is planned to have a capacity of approximately 2,000 megawatts and will use HL-class gas turbines, steam turbines and generators. In March 2025, Siemens Energy announced a further $1.6 billion contract to supply key technologies for the Rumah 2 and Al-Nairyah 2 power plants, with a combined capacity of 3.6 gigawatts. The deal includes 25-year maintenance agreements. At the time, the company said key components for the plants would be manufactured at its Dammam facility. The plants were scheduled to begin connecting to the grid in simple-cycle mode in 2027, before transitioning to full combined-cycle operation the following year, according to the timeline announced at the time. Saudi capacity allocation amid global demand Bruch said Siemens Energy was in talks over new gas-fired power projects in Saudi Arabia and was reserving production capacity for the Kingdom, despite strong global demand partly driven by the expansion of data centers. The CEO added that Siemens Energy’s turbine sales pipeline currently extends through 2032, but rescheduling production and balancing the mix of turbine types and sizes could create opportunities to allocate additional capacity to certain projects. artigo.texto: West Bengal has issued a tender for the installation, testing and commissioning of a 50 MW (AC) solar power plant and a 10 MW/40 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) at Jungle Sundari Karmanagari-II in Purulia district. The project includes 12 years of operation and maintenance (O&M). It has sought bids till November 17, 2026 As part of the tender requirements, the developers must submit three sets of the draft Detailed Design Drawings and Reports, along with editable soft copies on a compact disc (CD), for approval. The draft must include a master plan and all documents required under the scope of work. The contractor must submit the draft Detailed Design Drawings and Reports within 21 days of the issuance of the Letter of Award (LoA). As the solar PV power plant will be grid connected type, grid outage will be considered as 12 hours as (6 am to 6 pm) for calculating NMGG. No relaxation in NMGG will be considered for any other losses occurred in the syste Following approval, six sets of the finalized Detailed Design Drawings and Reports, along with editable soft copies on a CD, must be submitted to the Chief Engineer, Solar Power Generation Department (SPGD), West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (WBSEDCL). Scope of Work Under the scope of work, the contractor is responsible for the design, engineering, procurement, supply, installation, construction, testing and commissioning of the project, along with 12 years of O&M. The project is located at Jungle Sundari Karmanagari-II, Raghunathpur Block-II, Mouza Raibandh-42, in Purulia district, West Bengal. The O&M scope includes deploying a supervisor and adequate skilled personnel with the appropriate voltage-grade electrical workmanship licences to ensure round-the-clock plant operations. The contractor must also deploy adequate security personnel, comprising a minimum of one armed security guard and three security personnel in each of the three shifts. Additionally, the contractor must submit three sets of comprehensive user manuals and two sets of Operation and Maintenance format books suitable for use over 144 months. The maintenance scope includes the supply of spare parts and the replacement of all damaged equipment and accessories with new components within the annual maintenance charges. The downtime of the solar PV system and BESS must not exceed 72 hours which is equivilant to three days. The entire project, including the finalization of Detailed Design Drawings and Reports, site execution, trial runs, performance ratio (PR) testing of the solar PV plant and performance guarantee (PGT) testing of the BESS plant, must be completed within 550 days from the date of commencement.

artigo.texto: Estados vivem onda de regulação para receber data centers Levantamento mostra que projetos apresentados nas Assembleias Legislativas pularam de 4 para 16, sendo que metade deles cria restrições A expansão dos investimentos em data centers no Brasil começa a provocar uma reação regulatória nos Estados, com propostas que vão da concessão de incentivos locais a novas exigências sobre uso de água, licenciamento ambiental e transparência. Dos 16 projetos apresentados nas assembleias estaduais em 2026, oito criam restrições ou ônus aos empreendimentos. As propostas favoráveis eram maioria no ano passado, segundo levantamento da Innova Assuntos Públicos obtido com exclusividade pelo Valor. O estudo mapeou 20 projetos de lei e de lei complementar sobre data centers em 11 assembleias legislativas entre 2025 e outubro de 2026. Em todo o ano de 2025 foram registradas quatro iniciativas, valor que saltou para 16 no acumulado deste ano até outubro. Dos 20 projetos, nove são restritivos, sete favoráveis, dois misturam incentivos e exigências e dois são considerados neutros. O estudo associa a reação aos data centers ao aumento da insatisfação popular com a expansão deles nos Estados Unidos e à mobilização de movimentos sociais locais. O avanço de investimentos ou anúncios nos Estados, possivelmente aliado a estratégias consideradas insuficientes de comunicação com a população local, também é apontado como um dos fatores que ajudam a explicar o crescimento dessas propostas. Para a Innova, a onda regulatória significa que o debate sobre o tema tem ganhado força, diz a Innova. Os projetos favoráveis estão mais avançados: são os únicos que já viraram lei. Ceará e Goiás já aprovaram normas voltadas à atração dos empreendimentos. No Ceará, a lei aprovada em julho de 2026 criou licenciamento escalonado por porte e potencial poluidor, além de prever cessão de áreas públicas e desoneração de ICMS. Como o ICMS será extinto em 2033, concessões nesses sentido são temporárias. Em Goiás, a legislação combina incentivos, zonas prioritárias e licenciamento simplificado, com preferência pelo biometano como fonte de energia, ponto que pode desfavorecer outros suprimentos renováveis. “O levantamento mostra que a regulação dos data centers está chegando aos Estados e em ritmo acelerado. Isso não significa que essas propostas vão ser aprovadas amanhã, mas mostra que a sociedade e os parlamentos estaduais estão olhando para esses empreendimentos com muito mais atenção do que há um ano”, diz Fernanda Arbex, autora do estudo e sócia da Innova. Segundo ela, o que mais chama atenção é a velocidade com que o debate se espalha. “Textos apresentados em um Estado reaparecem quase iguais em outro, e parte das regras está sendo decidida fora das assembleias, em conselhos ambientais. Para quem investe, acompanhar esse processo de perto passou a fazer parte do planejamento estratégico, tanto quanto a conexão à rede ou o licenciamento.” Ela alerta ainda que as empresas que se adiantarem e entrarem cedo nesses debates, com dados e diálogo com as comunidades locais, terão mais chances de contribuir para a construção de regras previsíveis, em vez de apenas reagir a elas depois. O movimento ocorre ao mesmo tempo em que o governo federal avançou com o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata), que concede benefícios tributários em troca de contrapartidas para estimular a instalação de data centers no país. Nos Estados, os nove projetos restritivos ainda estão em comissões, mas são mais incisivos, com previsão de vedações, multas, tetos de potência e plebiscitos. Os favoráveis costumam ser autorizativos ou estabelecer diretrizes gerais, com incentivos tributários e simplificações. Os projetos restritivos ocorrem no Ceará, Minas Gerais, Pará, Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Sul e São Paulo e se concentram principalmente em água, licenciamento e transparência. A energia aparece de forma indireta, sobretudo como condição para a concessão de incentivos. No licenciamento, o caso mais restritivo identificado pelo estudo está no Rio Grande do Sul. Uma proposta exige estudo prévio de impacto ambiental para cargas acima de 2 Megawatts (MW) e limita a soma dos grandes consumidores a 50% da potência média do Estado. O texto também prevê plebiscito para empreendimentos a partir de 20% dessa potência, gatilho estimado em cerca de 700 MW. Em Minas Gerais, outra proposta busca restringir os procedimentos simplificados de licenciamento e prevê consulta prévia a comunidades tradicionais. Já o uso de água é a frente em que esse movimento aparece de forma mais disseminada. Os cinco projetos centrados no tema impõem alguma restrição, embora com diferentes graus de exigência. Em São Paulo, duas propostas determinam o uso exclusivo de água de reúso, inclusive por data centers em operação, e preveem multa mensal de R$ 50 mil e paralisação em caso de reincidência. As exigências também alcançam a transparência. No Pará, um projeto prevê a criação de um painel público com indicadores de desempenho hídrico e energético dos data centers. No Ceará, outra proposta estabelece diretrizes de transparência e de inclusão das comunidades nos benefícios associados aos empreendimentos. “São exigências de menor custo, que tendem a se espalhar”, avalia a consultoria. Em energia, a atuação dos Estados ocorre principalmente por meio de condições indiretas. No Rio de Janeiro, uma proposta condiciona incentivos ao uso de energia limpa com geração própria, exigência que pode conflitar com contratos de energia renovável no mercado livre. No Ceará, um projeto trata da sustentabilidade energética nas Zonas de Processamento de Exportação (ZPEs). Além dos projetos de lei, o levantamento identificou dois atos de conselhos ambientais e 22 requerimentos e indicações apresentados em assembleias estaduais, dos quais 17 em 2026. artigo.texto: New Delhi [India], October 12 (ANI): India and the European Union have agreed to strengthen technical cooperation on carbon markets, including carbon pricing mechanisms and monitoring systems, as both sides discussed the implementation of the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), the Ministry of Power said on Monday. The discussions took place during a bilateral meeting between Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary in the Ministry of Power, and Gerassimos Thomas, Director-General for Taxation and Customs Union at the European Commission, in New Delhi. The two sides expressed willingness to continue technical engagement on the recognition of carbon pricing mechanisms, monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) systems, and capacity building. They also agreed to facilitate continued dialogue on carbon markets, CBAM-related methodologies and other areas of mutual interest. During the meeting, Agarwal highlighted India’s progress under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), including the notification of emission intensity reduction targets for 490 industrial units and the development of the domestic carbon market. The discussions come as India continues to develop its framework for carbon trading and emission reduction, with cooperation on carbon pricing and verification systems emerging as an important area of engagement with the European Union. Agarwal also highlighted India’s progress in expanding non-fossil energy capacity. Non-fossil sources account for 308 gigawatts (GW) of India’s total installed electricity generation capacity of 558 GW, according to the ministry. The European Union side appreciated India’s progress in developing its carbon market and shared updates on the implementation of CBAM. The mechanism was among the key subjects discussed during the meeting, alongside opportunities to improve technical understanding and cooperation between the two sides. Both sides agreed to continue engagement on methodologies related to the mechanism and on systems for monitoring, reporting and verifying emissions. The meeting underlines the importance of continued dialogue between India and the European Union on carbon market development, emissions accounting and capacity building, as both sides seek to strengthen cooperation in these areas. The Ministry of Power said the discussions focused on India’s carbon market development, the EU’s CBAM and opportunities for enhanced technical cooperation. (ANI) (This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. Punjab Kesari assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

artigo.texto: Leader Energy Group Berhad has commenced construction of its 100 MW/400 MWh grid-scale Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Pajam, Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia, marking a significant step in the company’s expansion into utility-scale energy storage infrastructure. The project is being developed under Malaysia’s Battery Energy Storage System bidding programme (MyBeST) and is scheduled for commissioning in 2027. The project is being implemented through Leader Energy Storage Sdn. Bhd., a subsidiary of Leader Energy, and is designed to enhance grid flexibility across Peninsular Malaysia. Once operational, the facility is expected to support renewable energy integration, improve electricity supply-demand management and contribute to greater grid stability as Malaysia expands its clean energy capacity. The development builds on Leader Energy’s experience in battery storage technology through its 1.45 MWh sodium-sulfur (NAS®) BESS pilot project at the Leader Solar Energy II (LSE II) solar facility in Bukit Selambau, Kedah. The pilot system is integrated with a 20 MWac grid-connected solar photovoltaic plant and demonstrates the potential of energy storage to capture surplus solar electricity and discharge it when required, improving renewable energy utilisation. The pilot project has also received industry recognition, winning the Renewable Energy Enabler Technology award under the Special Submission category at the Malaysia National Energy Awards 2025. Additionally, it was selected as a finalist in the Energy Storage category at the Enlit Asia Power & Energy Awards 2026. Commenting on the development, Dato’ Sean H’ng, Executive Deputy Chairman and Group Chief Executive Officer of Leader Energy, highlighted that the company’s experience with solar-integrated battery storage has provided valuable operational insights. He stated that the Pajam project represents the next phase of Leader Energy’s expansion into grid-scale storage while supporting Malaysia’s broader energy transition objectives. He further emphasised the growing importance of battery energy storage systems in managing electricity supply and demand as renewable energy penetration increases. According to the company, storage infrastructure will play an essential role in maintaining grid reliability while enabling greater integration of variable renewable energy sources. Malaysia’s MyBeST programme, administered by the Energy Commission (Suruhanjaya Tenaga), comprises four grid-connected battery energy storage projects, each with a capacity of 100 MW/400 MWh. Together, the projects represent a combined capacity of 400 MW/1,600 MWh, with commissioning scheduled for 2027. The programme forms part of Malaysia’s broader strategy to strengthen electricity system flexibility, reduce dependence on fossil fuel-based peaking power plants and improve long-term power system efficiency. It also supports the country’s National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), which targets 70% renewable energy capacity by 2050. For Leader Energy, the groundbreaking represents another milestone in its strategy to develop an integrated renewable energy infrastructure platform combining clean power generation, battery storage and electricity transmission capabilities. With more than three decades of experience in the power sector, Leader Energy develops, constructs, owns and operates renewable energy generation, energy storage and power transmission assets across Asia. The company’s latest investment in grid-scale battery storage is expected to strengthen its participation in Malaysia’s evolving electricity market while supporting the region’s transition towards a more reliable and lower-carbon energy system. artigo.texto: Gil Torquato, Abranet: É difícil pensar na regulamentação do Redata ainda este ano Para o presidente da Abranet, a renovação do Congresso Nacional e a própria eleição presidencial deve provocar um delay. "É ruim, mas é o momento que estamos vivendo". Ele também defendeu o adiamento da Reforma Tributária. O presidente da Associação Brasileira de Internet (Abranet), Gil Torquato, defendeu ao participar de um painel na Futurecom 2026 que a regulação da Inteligência Artificial tem de ser “o mais cirúrgica possível e cobrir setores específicos para não inibir a inovação”. Segundo ele, quanto menos regulação será melhor para a IA, uma vez que é necessário estimular e não inibir o mercado. Em entrevista, Gil Torquato disse que as regulamentações têm de dar respaldo e segurança jurídica para assegurar os investimentos. Sinalizou ainda que uma agência para IA tem de ajudar nas diretrizes, mas não teria de ter uma visão punitiva. Gil Torquato é descrente da possibilidade de o Marco Legal de IA ser aprovado ainda este ano. “Houve uma renovação do Congresso e o tema tem de ser mais discutido”, pontuou. O presidente da Abranet falou também sobre o Redata. Ele também acha difícil ter a regulamentação ainda este ano – ela está com o poder executivo – diante das eleições presidenciais. “O Redata é muito importante, gostaria que saísse, mas acho que teremos um delay”, admite. E ao ser questionado sobre a Reforma Tributária, Gil Torquato lembrou que as empresas não estão preparadas e o próprio governo está atrasado. Ele defendeu o adiamento da vigência do novo regime. “É um tema sensível. Afeta todas as empresas e é preciso rediscutir as alíquotas”. artigo.texto: Richardson Electronics is also expanding its La Fox manufacturing operations Richardson Electronics and ComEd have announced plans to install a 5-megawatt-hour (MWh) battery energy storage system at Richardson Electronics’ manufacturing facility in La Fox, Illinois, US. The companies describe the project as a research and development demonstration and claim it will be the largest commercial battery energy storage system in Illinois. The project is supported by Illinois’ Reimagining Energy and Vehicles (REV Illinois) programme and ComEd’s customer interconnection process. ComEd, a subsidiary of Exelon Corporation, will provide engineering studies and site preparation assistance for the installation. Richardson Electronics is also expanding its La Fox manufacturing operations to increase production of commercial battery energy storage systems (BESS). Through a partnership with Gotion Illinois, the company currently offers commercial storage systems in 211-kilowatt-hour (kWh), 422-kWh, and 760-kWh configurations. According to Greg Peloquin, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Richardson Electronics’ Power & Microwave Technologies and Green Energy Solutions groups, the company’s energy storage solutions are intended to help customers manage energy consumption more efficiently while improving grid reliability and resilience. The initiative aligns with Illinois’ Clean and Reliable Grid Affordability Act, which includes battery storage as part of efforts to address projected electricity supply shortfalls. ComEd’s Distributed Generation Rebate Program also supports battery storage adoption. The programme, which has recently reached a $350 million milestone, offers eligible customers rebates of up to $300 per kWh of storage capacity for qualifying battery installations.

artigo.texto: Governo Federal quer replicar modelo de data centers do Ceará em todo o Nordeste Ministro das Comunicações destaca energia renovável, infraestrutura de cabos e incentivos do Pecém como pilares para atrair investimentos globais 09:19 | Out. 13, 2026 O Governo Federal trabalha para expandir o modelo de desenvolvimento de data centers implementado no Ceará para todos os estados da Região Nordeste. Siga o canal de Economia no WhatsApp para ficar bem informado A informação foi divulgada pelo ministro das Comunicações, Frederico Siqueira, no último sábado, dia 10, ressaltando o potencial do Nordeste para se consolidar como um hub digital de alcance global. Segundo o ministro, a Região reúne as condições centrais buscadas por investidores internacionais para a instalação de grandes centros de processamento de dados e inteligência artificial. O movimento apoia-se em três pilares estratégicos identificados no ecossistema cearense: - Abundância de energia renovável (eólica e solar) - Alta conectividade garantida pela rede de cabos submarinos ancorados em Fortaleza - Segurança jurídica proporcionada pelo Regime Especial de Tributação para a Infraestrutura de Processamento de Dados (Redata). Confira os assuntos econômicos no Ceará, no Brasil e no Mundo Estudos da Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV) citados pelo titular das Comunicações apontam que a implantação de um único data center focado em inteligência artificial no Complexo do Pecém tem potencial de mobilizar até R$ 25 bilhões em investimentos. O impacto econômico prevê a geração de 12,5 mil empregos durante a fase de construção e a criação de 1.860 postos de trabalho permanentes na operação do empreendimento. Projeto do Pecém vai elevar capacidade nacional de dados em 28,5% A iniciativa citada pelo ministério insere-se no contexto de investimentos de grande porte atracados no Ceará. O empreendimento em desenvolvimento no Pecém é o primeiro de um conjunto de cinco data centers autorizados a operar na Zona de Processamento de Exportação (ZPE) do Ceará. Acompanhe mais notícias de Economia no Linkedin do O POVO No total, o projeto global está avaliado em R$ 200 bilhões e tem como cliente final a gigante chinesa ByteDance, controladora do TikTok. Desenvolvido pela Omnia, o primeiro centro de dados contará, apenas em sua fase inicial, com uma capacidade instalada de processamento de 200 megawatts (MW). O volume é expressivo quando comparado ao cenário nacional atual: somados, todos os data centers em operação no Brasil possuem cerca de 700 MW de capacidade. Veja dicas rápidas sobre Educação Financeira no Dei Valor Assim, a entrada em operação do primeiro módulo no Pecém representará, sozinha, um incremento de 28,5% na infraestrutura de processamento de dados de todo o País.

artigo.texto: Economia e Negócios: PE quer liderar a rota dos Data Centers no país Com localização geográfica estratégica e energia limpa, acordo de cooperação entre o governo estadual e o LIDE Pernambuco busca atrair BigTechs Clique aqui e escute a matéria A economia atual tem nos dados o seu combustível vital, impulsionando o avanço contínuo da inteligência artificial, do e-commerce e da computação em nuvem. Para que essas tecnologias continuem se expandindo, exige-se uma infraestrutura física extremamente robusta. Nesse cenário, o estado de Pernambuco dispõe de uma janela de oportunidade decisiva para se consolidar como líder nacional na atração de data centers e na conexão de cabos submarinos. As vantagens comparativas: posição geográfica estratégica e energia renovável Para atrair os maiores players globais do setor, Pernambuco reúne diferenciais competitivos claros: - Localização geográfica estratégica: Por representar o caminho mais curto do Brasil para a Europa e para a África, o estado é o ponto ideal para ancorar cabos intercontinentais de fibra ótica. - Matriz energética limpa: O forte potencial do Nordeste na geração de energia solar e eólica funciona como o principal atrativo para as BigTechs, que necessitam de grande oferta de eletricidade renovável para abastecer suas instalações e cumprir metas rigorosas de descarbonização. Acordo de cooperação técnica: estruturação e atração de investimentos privados Transformar esse potencial bruto em desenvolvimento real exige planejamento técnico e articulação. Por isso, o Governo do Estado de Pernambuco assinou um acordo de cooperação técnica com o LIDE Pernambuco para elaborar um estudo estratégico do ecossistema de infraestrutura digital. Esse diagnóstico qualificado servirá de base para subsidiar a atração de investimentos privados e posicionar o estado como referência em inovação. A iniciativa conta com a participação ativa de secretarias estaduais estratégicas, como as de Administração, Ciência, Tecnologia e Desenvolvimento Econômico. A ação conjunta entre o poder público e a iniciativa privada sinaliza ao mercado global que a infraestrutura digital é prioridade, garantindo que Pernambuco aproveite a transição tecnológica para gerar empregos de excelência na economia de dados. artigo.texto: A $750 million investment agreement for industrial development and a potential data center at New River Valley Commerce Park is off, at least for now, after a company did not finalize the contract. The 475-acre site in Pulaski County was scheduled to exchange ownership on Oct. 5, between multi-government representative Virginia’s First Regional Industrial Facility Authority and developer New River Valley LLC, according to the proposed agreement. “Right now as it stands, the contract has expired with the company,” said Michael Solomon, the authority’s executive director. “They had until the 5th to close, and they didn’t.” Solomon said Friday he did not know the reason or reasons for the company’s decision. The initial amount the developer was set to pay was approximately $1.6 million, with $580,000 already in escrow as a deposit. The remaining amount was due at closing, according to Solomon. The authority is likely to get the money that remains in escrow based on the contract, he said. Over 10 years, the developer would have been required to invest at least $750 million in industrial projects such as manufacturing and a data center. No end user for a data center development had been identified, Solomon said. The authority, which owns and manages the commerce park, was created in 1998 through a partnership between 11 member governments — the counties of Bland, Craig, Giles, Montgomery, Pulaski, and Roanoke, the cities of Radford and Roanoke, and the towns of Dublin, Pearisburg and Pulaski. In the efforts to boost economic activity, each member would receive proportional tax revenue from industry development at the site based on the amount of previous investment — host Pulaski County would receive the most. As Cardinal News previously reported, the county was expected to receive $15 million in 2025 from the state’s general funds, appropriated by the General Assembly to go toward utility infrastructure development at the park. That figure was later reduced to $7.5 million, which remains untouched and has carried over into this year’s budget, Solomon said. No new developer has been identified, Solomon said, and the authority continues to assess what other options are available. Cardinal News reached out to New River Valley LLC for comment and did not receive a response last week. The authority will hold a public meeting to discuss data centers in general at the New River Valley Fairgrounds at 5581 Fair Grounds Circle in Dublin from 6 to 8 p.m. Thursday. Christopher Lloyd, senior vice president and director for infrastructure and economic development at McGuireWoods Consulting, is scheduled to speak at the forum. Live questions will not be taken during the meeting and should be presubmitted to executivedirector@nrvcommerpark.org, according to the online event page.

artigo.texto: MAHOMET – Several Mahomet residents are calling on the village to ban future non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) after officials ended talks with a data center developer last week. Officials were collaborating with Clean Cloud Energy, a data center developer based on the East Coast, for a plan to build a data center in the village. Those discussions ended after they faced backlash from the community. At Tuesday night’s meeting, several residents said the village was not transparent with the community about these discussions. “When was the right time for CCE? After the ‘i’s’ had been dotted and the ‘t’s’ crossed and the final product presented before the planning and zoning and village board meeting?” Mahomet resident Laurie Scott said. “That is not community engagement. It’s community bulldozing.” President Jason Tompkins confirmed the village administrator did sign a village-wide NDA covering staff and elected officials, which he was aware of. But he said the preliminary discussions that village staff were having would have been the same with or without an NDA. “The NDA was not our idea,” he said, “but I think going forward it should be a discussion we have to have.” Trustee Bruce Colravy said he wants to propose legislation to ban village staff from signing NDAs. Some Champaign County Board members have similarly brought up that idea. “I would also like — there are some people who don’t believe that the talks have actually ended,” he said, “So I’d like a draft resolution to institute a moratorium on data centers that matches Champaign County.” Champaign County currently has a one-year pause on data center development. However, it does not apply to projects inside city or village limits, like the proposal in Mahomet. “This represents such a small piece of the distrust that’s been built,” Colravy said, “and I think that we should do some things to try to repair that.”

artigo.texto: Changan and CATL to collaborate on 1,500 km solid state cells, establish 75 GWh battery lines Chinese automaker Changan has officially announced plans to deepen its partnership with battery giant CATL. The two firms have committed to expanding joint battery production capacity to 75 GWh and collaborating on solid-state batteries (SSBs) and sodium-ion cells. Like its previous statements on its in-house SSBs, Changan announced an interactive platform owned by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. The automaker also expressed commitment to prospective industries, including humanoid robots and China’s “low-altitude economy”. More cells with CATL Changan and CATL are not new partners in China’s automotive sector, having established a joint venture (JV), CATL-Changan (时代长安, Times Changan), earlier in 2023. The JV supplies cells to Changan’s in-house NEV brands, including Avatr, Deepal, and Nevo. Libattery.net, a Chinese battery industry outlet, reports that CATL-Changan is on track to reach 50 GWh of battery production capacity, a plan Changan revealed at an investor relations event in May 2025. The announcement means CATL-Changan will receive an additional 25 GWh of capacity and new production lines. The JV plans to establish a 700,000-square-meter facility and invest 5 billion yuan (~750 million USD) in the expansion. According to Changan, the new facility will integrate the “latest generation of CATL battery tech” and supply cells to the automaker’s NEV brands. It’s planned to start operations in 2027 and meet the 25 GWh goal in three years. It will be situated in a high-tech zone between Chongqing City and Sichuan Province. The automaker expects the expansion to bring in annual revenue of 10 billion yuan (~1.5 billion USD), create 2,500 jobs, and generate 300 million yuan (~45 million USD) in tax revenue for the local community. More on Changan’s SSBs Changan has joined the race for SSBs in China, announcing its Golden Bell (Jinzhongzhao) cells in November 2023. The automaker says it’s aiming for an energy density of 400 Wh/kg and claims it will be 70% safer than rivals because it uses “AI remote diagnosis technology”. It also claims the new Golden Bell cells will help EVs reach ranges over 1,500 km and says cell degradation won’t be noticeable for at least 600,000 km. Cell life will exceed 5,000 cycles, and Golden Bell packs will support 6C charging, enabling a 30-80% charge in 9 minutes. The automaker has also reiterated its development schedule for the Golden Bell cells, aiming for vehicle road tests in 2026 and ramping up to commercial production in 2027. Source: libattery.net

artigo.texto: India aims to shift from primarily using and importing battery technologies to researching, developing, and manufacturing its own batteries. Experts see this initiative as a way to meet future energy needs more independently and affordably. Experts say scientists have been studying lithium-ion batteries for decades and that now India should expedite the development of newer battery technologies and transition them from laboratories to manufacturing facilities. “With nearly 60 years of lithium-ion research behind us, this is the perfect time to accelerate the development and industrialisation of next-generation battery chemistries,” said Aninda J. Bhattacharyya, a Professor and J.C. Bose National Fellow at the Indian Institute of Science, ahead of the Battery Show India, organised by Informa Markets. Bhattacharyya emphasised that while lithium-ion batteries will continue to play a vital role, India should also explore other types of batteries that utilise materials readily available within the country. India currently relies on imports for some critical battery materials and technologies. “Sodium-ion batteries are particularly promising due to the abundance of sodium, which has a lower reliance on critical minerals and potential cost advantages,” added Bhattacharyya. Experts gathered at the Battery Show India in Bengaluru for a media roundtable in anticipation of the fourth edition of the show, scheduled for October 22–24, 2026, at India Expo Mart in Greater Noida. The roundtable took place amid the government's recent approval of a Rs 50,000 crore incentive scheme for 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) deployment, part of a larger Rs 1.86 lakh crore program to strengthen renewable energy and transmission infrastructure. “So far, approximately 9 GW of storage capacity has been installed, while the potential stands at around 236 GW, creating significant opportunities for manufacturing, investment, employment, and domestic supply chains,” said Ramesh Shivanna, Director of the Federation of Karnataka Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FKCCI). The Central Electricity Authority has projected a requirement of 236 GWh of BESS by 2031–32. The government's recent approval for deploying 50 GWh of BESS under the Green Energy Corridor highlights the scale and urgency of this opportunity. “As storage becomes a foundational element of India’s power infrastructure, the focus will need to broaden across battery technologies, manufacturing, grid integration, power management, safety, and digital intelligence,” said Rajneesh Khattar, Senior Group Director at Informa Markets, India. Experts concluded that India's energy storage ambitions (requiring around 300 GWh) necessitate self-reliance across the entire battery value chain. The inconsistency of other renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind, further highlights this need.

artigo.texto: WASHINGTON COUNTY, Va. (WJHL) — Tuesday night, the Washington County, Virginia, Board of Supervisors adopted zoning language that restricts where a battery energy storage facility can go. Battery energy storage facilities are a tool that saves extra energy for use at a later time. The ordinance specifically applies to Tier 2 facilities, which are commonly used in data centers. “This is more what, you know, a layman would say, utility-scale battery storage,” Stephen Richardson, the Washington County, VA, planning commission coordinator, told the board of supervisors during Tuesday night’s meeting. “And so all of that would be permitted by special exemption.” The ordinance specifies that energy storage projects would only be allowed in manufacturing zones. “So you want to be as close to either a substation or, as you say, a high-powered line that they can get onto,” Richardson told the board. “And as you all know, right now, there’s so many restrictions on anybody adding anything to the grid.” The ordinance also halts projects that start without approval. “This is not by right, even though it’s an M-1 and M-2,” Saul Hernandez, a member of the board of supervisors, said during the meeting. “It would require a special exception vote, which we all know we would have to vote in the affirmative have to take an additional vote. So this is not by right.” Board chair Dwayne Ball said the ordinance looks out for Washington County taxpayers’ pockets. “You don’t want to be too far away because the farther away you are, the more it costs,” Ball said. “So I think it’ll be very limited to M-1 and M-2 for that reason also.” The ordinance was unanimously approved. The new zoning language will take effect immediately.

artigo.texto: DOVER, Del. - Dover City Council voted unanimously Monday night to pass an 18-month moratorium on new data center applications, as officials raise concerns about the potential impact on the city’s infrastructure and electric rates. The pause will give the city time to study whether its municipal infrastructure could support future data center development and establish regulations before considering applications. Councilman David Anderson, who co-sponsored the ordinance, said officials need more information about the potential costs before moving forward. "How can we properly allocate cost if we don't have the numbers yet?" Anderson said. "That's why we need a moratorium, a pause to understand what the cost would even be, so that the residents and the other businesses don't unfairly bear that burden." Councilwoman Donyale Hall also expressed concerns about the potential impact on ratepayers, particularly those already struggling to afford basic necessities. "For some it's a choice between paying a utility bill and buying food, groceries or medication," Hall said. "And that's just an unfortunate circumstance that we find ourselves in." Hall said she is sensitive to proposals that could result in additional costs for residents and wants the city to determine whether its infrastructure could accommodate data centers before allowing development to move forward. "Let's put forward something that places a pause on this until we can figure out if our small municipal infrastructure would be able to even entertain the possibility of one of these things coming into our local area," Hall said. Hall called it a way to give the city time to assess its options. The issue has also drawn concern from residents. State leaders recently held a town hall in Dover focused on data centers, giving community members an opportunity to ask questions and share concerns about energy demand, water use and who would ultimately bear the costs. Rashawn Chapman, who has lived in Dover for several years, said he opposes data center development in Delaware. "The frequency that they put in is harmful for us. It's harmful for the planet. It's harmful for the animals," Chapman said. Chapman also questioned whether an 18-month pause would be enough time to address the potential impacts. "They should not allow those data centers to be built in Delaware," he said. "Delaware is small. It's not big like New York or Texas." Dover has not yet received a formal data center application, but council members say companies have expressed interest in the area.

artigo.texto: Um novo sistema de baterias, o primeiro do seu tipo no país, será instalado no Acre para garantir a estabilidade da rede elétrica. A novidade, recomendada pela EPE, usa tecnologia avançada que ajuda a rede a se equilibrar sozinha, prevenindo apagões enquanto novas linhas de transmissão são construídas. A mudança marca uma nova era para a segurança do fornecimento de energia no Brasil. Durante muito tempo, os sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias (BESS) foram associados principalmente à redução de custos com energia, à gestão da demanda e à integração de fontes renováveis. No entanto, uma importante mudança começa a ganhar força no planejamento do setor elétrico brasileiro: o armazenamento deixa de ser apenas uma ferramenta para consumidores e passa a desempenhar um papel estratégico na própria infraestrutura de transmissão de energia. Essa transformação ficou evidente com a recente recomendação da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) para a implantação de um sistema de armazenamento de 100 MW / 200 MWh em Cruzeiro do Sul, no Acre. Previsto para ser contratado no Leilão de Transmissão nº 01/2027, o empreendimento será o primeiro sistema de armazenamento por baterias incorporado diretamente ao segmento de transmissão do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). - O projeto no Acre será o primeiro sistema de baterias integrado à rede de transmissão nacional. - A capacidade instalada é de 100 MW, com armazenamento de 200 MWh. - A tecnologia 'grid-forming' permite que as baterias estabilizem a rede sozinhas. - A solução complementa a construção de novas linhas de 230 kV na região. - O modelo visa aumentar a segurança e evitar apagões em regiões remotas. O primeiro marco para a rede de transmissão nacional Mais do que um projeto pioneiro, trata-se de uma mudança de paradigma. Tradicionalmente, quando surgiam problemas relacionados à confiabilidade do fornecimento, a resposta era ampliar a infraestrutura física do sistema elétrico por meio da construção de novas linhas de transmissão e subestações. Essas obras continuam sendo fundamentais, mas nem sempre oferecem a velocidade necessária para responder às necessidades do sistema ou representam a solução mais eficiente para desafios específicos. É justamente nesse contexto que o armazenamento por baterias ganha protagonismo. No caso do Acre, a solução proposta utiliza tecnologia grid-forming, que permite ao sistema não apenas armazenar energia, mas também atuar ativamente na estabilidade elétrica da rede. Diferentemente dos inversores convencionais, que dependem da rede para operar, os conversores grid-forming conseguem estabelecer referências de tensão e frequência, oferecendo suporte imediato em situações de contingência. Tecnologia que estabiliza a rede instantaneamente Na prática, isso significa que o sistema poderá responder quase instantaneamente a falhas na transmissão, reduzindo riscos de interrupções no fornecimento e aumentando a confiabilidade da operação. Essa capacidade torna-se especialmente importante em regiões como Cruzeiro do Sul e Feijó. Embora ambas já estejam conectadas ao Sistema Interligado Nacional, a infraestrutura ainda apresenta limitações de redundância. Em determinadas situações, a indisponibilidade de um componente da rede pode comprometer o abastecimento. O armazenamento, nesse cenário, funciona como uma camada adicional de segurança operacional enquanto os reforços estruturais da transmissão são implantados. O aspecto mais interessante dessa estratégia é que ela demonstra que o armazenamento não substitui a expansão da rede, mas a complementa. O planejamento elaborado pela EPE prevê, paralelamente ao BESS, a construção de novos circuitos em 230 kV para reforçar a conexão entre Rio Branco, Feijó e Cruzeiro do Sul. Segurança operacional e novas oportunidades de investimento Ou seja, a transmissão continua evoluindo, enquanto o armazenamento oferece flexibilidade, rapidez de resposta e suporte operacional durante a transição. Essa combinação representa uma tendência observada em diversos mercados internacionais. À medida que os sistemas elétricos se tornam mais complexos, com maior participação de fontes renováveis e crescente eletrificação da economia, soluções capazes de aumentar a estabilidade e a flexibilidade da rede passam a ser cada vez mais relevantes. No Brasil, esse movimento também abre espaço para novas oportunidades de investimento e inovação. O armazenamento por baterias já demonstra resultados importantes em aplicações industriais e comerciais, reduzindo custos com demanda contratada, aumentando a previsibilidade energética e proporcionando maior autonomia para empresas. Agora, sua incorporação ao planejamento da transmissão amplia significativamente o potencial de utilização da tecnologia. Para o mercado, isso representa o amadurecimento de uma solução que tende a assumir funções cada vez mais diversas dentro do setor elétrico. Acreditamos que iniciativas como a prevista para o Acre demonstram que o armazenamento deixa de ocupar um papel complementar para tornar-se um elemento estratégico da modernização do sistema elétrico brasileiro. Estamos diante de uma mudança importante. O BESS passa a ser reconhecido não apenas como uma solução de eficiência energética, mas também como uma ferramenta essencial para aumentar a confiabilidade da transmissão, ampliar a resiliência da rede e preparar o Brasil para os desafios da transição energética das próximas décadas.

artigo.texto: The AI Data Center Reckoning: Why Infrastructure Must Earn Its Social License Something fundamental is breaking in the data center world, and it's not just a technical problem. It's becoming a social and political one. October 13, 2026 The AI Data Center Reckoning: Why Infrastructure Must Earn Its Social License Something fundamental is breaking in the data center world, and it's not just a technical problem. It's becoming a social and political one. For decades, data centers operated quietly in the background of modern life. They were infrastructure in the truest sense: essential, reliable, and largely invisible. Communities welcomed them as economic engines that brought jobs and tax revenue without the noise, traffic, or pollution of traditional industry. Then AI arrived and changed everything. AI data centers consume vastly more power, not incrementally more, but orders of magnitude more. They can draw enormous volumes of water for cooling. They require utility infrastructure upgrades that strain local grids. And they're proliferating at a pace that's catching regulators, utilities, and communities off guard. The result is something the industry hasn't faced before: organized resistance. Local and national governments are imposing moratoriums. Utility commissions are questioning grid capacity. Environmental groups are raising alarms about water consumption and carbon emissions. Data centers are losing their social license to operate, and the industry needs solutions that address the root causes, not just the symptoms. Why Social License Demands Converged Architecture The social license crisis stems from a fundamental inefficiency in how data center infrastructure has traditionally been designed. Power, backup systems, and cooling are engineered independently and assembled only during construction. This siloed approach creates cascading inefficiencies that communities can see and feel. Power passes through multiple conversion stages, losing energy as heat at each step. Cooling systems respond slowly to load changes because they lack real-time visibility into compute demand. Energy storage sits idle until a utility outage occurs, providing no benefit during normal operation. The cumulative result is facilities that consume more power, use more water, and place greater strain on local infrastructure than necessary. When a community faces rising electricity rates or water restrictions while a data center down the road operates inefficiently, the backlash is predictable and justified. Incremental improvements won't solve this. The industry needs a fundamental rethinking of infrastructure design, and converged architecture provides a framework for doing exactly that. The Four-in-One Solution Converged architecture integrates power distribution, energy storage, and thermal management as a unified platform from the outset. Midea, working with Clou Electronics, has developed a four-in-one solution that demonstrates how this integration addresses the social license challenge directly. The system combines four critical components into a single coordinated architecture: - Power Supply Integration - Rather than treating power distribution as a separate system, the converged platform minimizes conversion stages, reducing energy loss and waste heat generation from the start. - Active Energy Storage - Instead of backup batteries that sit idle, the system uses energy storage to actively buffer demand spikes in real time. This reduces peak load on the grid, smoothing the facility's impact on local utility infrastructure and making it a better grid citizen. - Magnetic Levitation Cold Source - Traditional chillers rely on mechanical bearings that create friction and consume parasitic energy. Magnetic levitation technology eliminates physical contact in rotating components, using magnetic fields for suspension. This cuts energy consumption in the cooling plant itself while extending equipment life and reducing maintenance requirements. - Liquid-Cooled CDU - The liquid cooling distribution unit (CDU) is designed for higher-temperature operation and near-closed-loop water usage. By integrating with the magnetic levitation cold source and coordinating with real-time compute activity, the system dramatically reduces water consumption compared to conventional evaporative cooling approaches. The key differentiator is integration. These components aren't simply installed in the same facility; they're designed to work together from the ground up. The control systems coordinate across power, storage, and cooling. The thermal interfaces optimize heat transfer. The power buffering responds to actual compute demand, not ambient temperature changes. Magnetic CDU: The Efficiency Foundation As data centers face increasing demands from high-density computing and AI workloads, traditional cooling systems struggle to keep pace. Midea's Magnetic CDU offers a transformative approach to thermal management, combining exceptional energy efficiency with operational simplicity and reduced space requirements. The Magnetic CDU delivers outstanding energy performance that directly impacts operational costs. With a Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.1 or lower, facilities can achieve substantial reductions in electricity consumption compared to conventional cooling systems. The unit's intelligent free cooling capabilities maximize the use of ambient conditions, further reducing energy costs while maintaining optimal operating temperatures for all equipment types. Designed for versatility, the system adapts to diverse cooling requirements with adjustable water temperatures, supporting everything from traditional servers to the latest high-performance computing chips. The unit seamlessly switches between cooling modes in seconds, ensuring stable temperatures even during sudden load changes—critical for preventing equipment stress and maintaining uptime. artigo.texto: More data centers headed to San Antonio. City Council will vote on data center regulations SAN ANTONIO - Tx — The debate over data centers popping up here in San Antonio and all throughout Texas has prompted calls of regulation from city leaders and the community. Tonight District 6 Councilman Ric Galvan hosted a town hall meeting to hear from the community before city council votes on two proposals to regulate data centers. Proposal 1 will automatically permit new data centers as long as they are within certain zoning districts that are at least 500 feet away from residential homes, schools, daycares, assisted living facilities, and hospitals. Proposal 1 would not require a vote from city council; however, Proposal 2 would require a city council vote. Proposal 2 would also give the community an opportunity to make public comments before the data center would be approved. Public commenters at Tuesday’s town hall meeting voiced their concerns. “After hearing what everyone said today it sounds like Proposal 2 needs to be implemented. We have three hospitals in this area. What’s going to happen to the ICU when the electricity goes out, and their generators are not enough?” Councilman Galvan says he is also advocating for data centers to only be allowed to use recycled water. The District 6 Councilman says he supports Proposal 2. “I think primarily what we should be looking towards is that every data center that comes to San Antonio goes before City Council for a full vote.” City Council will vote on the two proposals on Oct. 29.

artigo.texto: No Chile, a ENGIE inaugurou 160 contêineres de baterias em infraestrutura reservada à expansão térmica. O BESS Lile custou US$ 174 milhões, armazena 802 MWh e pode atender o equivalente a mais de 84 mil casas por até cinco horas. O que estava reservado para ampliar a geração térmica de um complexo industrial no norte do Chile agora abriga uma bateria de escala incomum: 160 contêineres, 40 equipamentos de suporte e capacidade de armazenar 802 MWh de eletricidade. A ENGIE Chile colocou o BESS Lile em operação comercial em Mejillones, na região de Antofagasta, após investir US$ 174 milhões. O empreendimento tem 142 MW de potência e pode devolver eletricidade ao sistema chileno por até cinco horas. Segundo a empresa, isso equivale ao consumo de mais de 84 mil residências durante esse intervalo. A autorização para operar comercialmente foi concedida pelo Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional em 25 de setembro de 2026; a companhia anunciou a conclusão da primeira etapa da reconversão do complexo em 8 de outubro. Um espaço planejado para aumentar a geração térmica recebeu 160 contêineres de baterias O BESS Lile reutiliza a subestação de interconexão, vias internas e áreas de um complexo que havia sido preparado para expansão de geração térmica. São instalações que já tinham acesso ao sistema elétrico, originalmente previstas para uma ampliação da geração a carvão. A antiga estrutura passou a ter outra finalidade sem que todo o complexo térmico fosse convertido de uma só vez. - Pesquisadores da USP usaram simulações de física quântica para investigar 22 espécies químicas e combater falhas em baterias de sódio que prometem formar camada protetora contra dendritos que reduzem a vida útil - Grécia inaugura parque de baterias de € 50 milhões e 200 MWh em Tessalônica, com armazenamento diário equivalente à recarga de 3 mil carros elétricos e reforço à rede elétrica - Peru conecta mais de 136 mil painéis solares no deserto de Nasca e forma complexo de 403,52 MW com dois parques eólicos, unindo sol e vento na mesma região de Ica - Estudo com 88 mil unidades consumidoras de energia solar por assinatura registrou inadimplência média de 17% e alerta para riscos da abertura do mercado livre no Brasil As baterias ficam distribuídas em 160 contêineres, acompanhados por 40 conjuntos elétricos de apoio. O parque funciona como sistema independente de armazenamento, conhecido como stand-alone: recebe eletricidade da rede e pode reinjetá-la quando o operador necessita. Ao contrário de uma usina, o equipamento não gera eletricidade: guarda a energia recebida e a devolve em horários determinados pela operação da rede. São 142 MW de potência, 802 MWh guardados e autonomia de até cinco horas A capacidade final divulgada em 2026 superou a previsão de 140 MW apresentada pela empresa um ano antes. Os 142 MW indicam a potência que o parque pode entregar ou receber. Os 802 MWh representam a quantidade de energia que seus módulos podem guardar. A relação entre potência e capacidade define por quanto tempo as baterias podem fornecer eletricidade. A empresa usa uma referência residencial para traduzir essa capacidade: eletricidade equivalente ao consumo de mais de 84 mil casas durante até cinco horas de fornecimento. Quando há muita produção solar durante o dia, baterias conectadas à rede podem absorver parte dessa energia e devolvê-la após o pôr do sol, quando a geração fotovoltaica diminui. Como o BESS Lile está conectado diretamente à rede, sua carga e descarga dependem da operação do sistema, e não de um parque solar exclusivo no local. O carvão começou a sair de Mejillones no fim de 2025, mas a transformação continua A mudança não começou com os contêineres. Depois de quase três décadas de operação, a ENGIE desligou em 31 de dezembro de 2025 as unidades a carvão CTM1 e CTM2, que tinham juntas 334 MW de capacidade instalada, segundo o relatório anual da companhia. O plano de descarbonização ainda prevê outros equipamentos e retiradas de unidades no mesmo conjunto industrial. Outra unidade da região, a Infraestrutura Energética Mejillones (IEM), está em processo de adaptação para funcionar com gás natural. Em outubro de 2026, a empresa dizia que essa instalação ainda aguardava a entrada em operação comercial após a conversão. A empresa mantém no plano de transformação o futuro encerramento de operações a carvão nas unidades Central Termoeléctrica Andina (CTA) e Central Termoeléctrica Hornitos (CTH). Potência de baterias no Chile saiu de 1,2 GW para 3,2 GW ao longo de 2025 O novo parque entra em uma rede que está mudando rapidamente. Um levantamento do Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional, divulgado em abril, mostrou que a potência de armazenamento em baterias no Chile passou de aproximadamente 1,2 GW para 3,2 GW ao longo de 2025. O mesmo relatório apontou participação conjunta recorde de 46,2% da geração solar e eólica em dezembro de 2025. O órgão também identificou gargalos e atrasos na infraestrutura de transmissão e apontou a necessidade de atualizar regras de operação e remuneração diante do crescimento das baterias. Antes de Lile, a ENGIE colocou mais 251 MW de baterias em operação em agosto Em 28 de agosto de 2026, a companhia informou a entrada em operação comercial de outros dois projetos: BESS Libélula, na região de Santiago, e BESS Los Loros, em Atacama. Juntos, eles adicionaram 251 MW de potência de armazenamento ao sistema chileno, com US$ 283 milhões investidos nessa parte dos empreendimentos. O BESS Libélula dispõe de 203 MW e 1.034 MWh, com 208 contêineres, e integra um projeto que também inclui geração solar. O Los Loros reúne 48 MW e 275,23 MWh junto a uma usina fotovoltaica existente. Lile é diferente: opera como armazenamento independente, dentro de um complexo de origem térmica. Com o início das operações em Mejillones, a ENGIE contabiliza cinco sistemas de baterias que começaram a operar comercialmente em 2026 e informa ter alcançado 803 MW de capacidade instalada nessa tecnologia no Chile. artigo.texto: CATL expands Seres battery capacity: what it means for Contemporary Amperex Technology stock Published on 10/13/2026 at 09:01 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS - CATL agreed with Seres on October 11, 2026, to expand dedicated battery capacity to more than 20 GWh annually. - The October 11 agreement adds 10 to 12 GWh of annual pack capacity at Seres' Chongqing plant. - Second-quarter 2026 revenue reached CNY 147.8 billion, while net income was CNY 22.5 billion. - The Shenzhen quote was CNY 288.71 on October 13, 2026, 1.24 percent above the 52-week low. Contemporary Amperex Technology stock was quoted at CNY 288.71 on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on October 13, 2026 at 2:45 p.m. CST, as CATL expanded its battery partnership with Seres. The October 11 agreement adds 10 to 12 gigawatt-hours of annual pack capacity and takes dedicated capacity at Seres' Chongqing plant above 20 gigawatt-hours, according to East Asia Brief on October 11, 2026. What 20 GWh means for CATL The Seres project places CATL battery assembly directly inside the vehicle plant. The expansion adds 10 to 12 GWh of annual pack capacity, while the agreement gives CATL a five-year supply framework running through August 2027, East Asia Brief reported. The operating model also locks CATL into Seres' Aito vehicle range, whose cumulative deliveries equipped with CATL batteries have exceeded 1.2 million units, according to the same October 11 report. For CATL, the value is production visibility rather than a disclosed order amount because the companies did not publish construction costs or a commissioning date. Recent results show scale CATL reported CNY 147.8 billion of revenue and CNY 22.5 billion of net income for the second quarter of 2026. Revenue rose 57 percent from CNY 94.2 billion in the second quarter of 2025, while net income increased 37 percent from CNY 16.5 billion, according to Simply Wall St. The comparison also shows the pressure behind the capacity push: second-quarter profit growth trailed revenue growth by 20 percentage points. Simply Wall St reported that the second-quarter profit margin was 15 percent, down from 18 percent a year earlier, while earnings per share exceeded analyst expectations by 2.1 percent. Three dated operating milestones On July 25, 2026, CATL reported second-quarter revenue of CNY 147.8 billion and net income of CNY 22.5 billion. On September 22, 2026, its Debrecen factory began trial production after the company had produced 537,000 battery modules at the site. On October 11, 2026, the Seres agreement lifted the Chongqing plant's planned dedicated capacity above 20 GWh, with each event covered by Simply Wall St and East Asia Brief. Next results come into view CATL's board is scheduled to meet on October 20, 2026, to consider third-quarter results for the nine months ended September 30, according to Futubull. The company is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on October 21, 2026, according to Simply Wall St. Stock stays near its yearly low The Shenzhen quote of CNY 288.71 on October 13, 2026 stood 1.24 percent above the 52-week low of CNY 285.17 and 38.33 percent below the 52-week high of CNY 468.75. CATL's market capitalization was CNY 1.3 trillion on that date, giving the Seres expansion a market setting defined by scale and a wide distance from the yearly high. The continuously updated company information is available through the Market report Shanghai Composite. artigo.texto: Mercado global de memória não volátil: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de memória não volátil até 2035: demanda de data centers e do setor automotivo impulsionará o crescimento Resumo De acordo com o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Memória Não Volátil, o setor entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de memória não volátil (NVM) é um pilar fundamental da economia digital, pois garante a persistência de dados em dispositivos e infraestruturas. Em 2026, o setor já amadureceu para além da eletrônica de consumo e se tornou indispensável em armazenamento corporativo, infraestrutura de nuvem, sistemas automotivos e IoT industrial. A transição da arquitetura NAND planar para a 3D NAND sustentou a Lei de Moore e viabilizou armazenamento em escala de terabytes, enquanto tecnologias emergentes, como a memória de classe de armazenamento, borram as fronteiras entre memória e armazenamento. Este relatório traz uma análise abrangente do estado atual do mercado e projeta sua trajetória até 2035. O cenário é moldado pela demanda transformadora de setores centrados em dados, pela inovação tecnológica e pela interação entre a dinâmica das cadeias de suprimento e fatores geopolíticos. Entre os principais vetores de demanda estão o crescimento exponencial da criação de dados, a proliferação de cargas de trabalho de IA e aprendizado de máquina, a eletrificação e a automação de veículos e a expansão dos dispositivos de IoT. O mercado, porém, também enfrenta restrições, como a alta intensidade de capital, a ciclicidade e a concentração da cadeia de suprimentos. A análise disseca essas dinâmicas técnicas e comerciais e oferece uma visão clara das forças que moldam produção, demanda, preços e estratégias competitivas. Insights estratégicos são essenciais para fabricantes de memória, OEMs, investidores e formuladores de políticas que atuam nesse mercado intensivo em capital e estrategicamente sensível. O cenário-base para o mercado global de memória não volátil entre 2026 e 2035 prevê crescimento robusto, impulsionado pela demanda estrutural por armazenamento e processamento de dados. A expectativa é de expansão a uma taxa de crescimento anual composta (CAGR) de 7,2%, alcançando um índice de mercado de 200 em 2035 (2025=100). Esse crescimento se apoia no aumento incessante da geração de dados, na migração para computação em nuvem e de borda e na proliferação de aplicações de IA e aprendizado de máquina que exigem memória de alta velocidade e alta capacidade. No segmento de data centers, os SSDs corporativos vêm substituindo os HDDs, impulsionados pela necessidade de acesso mais rápido e menor latência. O setor automotivo desponta como um importante motor de crescimento, com sistemas avançados de assistência ao motorista (ADAS), entretenimento a bordo e direção autônoma exigindo grandes volumes de NVM para armazenamento de código e registro de dados. A eletrônica de consumo, incluindo smartphones e PCs, continua a demandar capacidades de armazenamento maiores, enquanto os dispositivos de IoT se multiplicam e exigem NVM embarcada de baixo consumo. Do lado da oferta, o setor é marcado por alta intensidade de capital e uma base de produção concentrada, sobretudo na Ásia-Pacífico. Avanços tecnológicos, como a transição para 3D NAND com mais camadas e a comercialização de tipos emergentes de NVM, como MRAM e PCM, moldarão o cenário competitivo. O mercado, no entanto, não está livre de desafios. Ciclicidade, tensões geopolíticas e possíveis rupturas na cadeia de suprimentos representam riscos. O cenário-base pressupõe que não haverá grandes recessões globais e que o ritmo de adoção tecnológica será constante. Também considera que as políticas comerciais permanecerão relativamente estáveis, permitindo o fluxo contínuo de componentes e produtos acabados. Nessas condições, o mercado está preparado para expansão sustentada, com o valor migrando para soluções de maior densidade e desempenho. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores de Demanda - Crescimento exponencial da criação global de dados e necessidade de infraestrutura de armazenamento eficiente. - Proliferação de cargas de trabalho de IA e aprendizado de máquina, que exigem memória de alta largura de banda e baixa latência. - Eletrificação e automação automotiva, com sistemas ADAS e de entretenimento a bordo demandando NVM de grau automotivo. - Expansão de dispositivos de IoT e computação de borda, impulsionando a demanda por NVM embarcada de baixo consumo. - Migração de HDDs para SSDs em data centers e dispositivos de consumo, elevando a demanda por NAND flash. - Implantação do 5G e aumento da capacidade de armazenamento em smartphones, ampliando o conteúdo de NAND e NOR flash por dispositivo. Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Alta intensidade de capital e ciclicidade do mercado de memória semicondutora. - Tensões geopolíticas e restrições comerciais que afetam cadeias de suprimento e acesso à tecnologia. - Concentração da produção em poucas regiões, expondo o mercado a desastres naturais e rupturas logísticas. - Desafios tecnológicos para escalar a 3D NAND além das contagens atuais de camadas e para comercializar tipos emergentes de NVM. - Volatilidade de preços decorrente de desequilíbrios entre oferta e demanda e de ajustes de estoque. artigo.texto: SINEXCEL Completes Power Conversion System Shipment for 100 MW/400 MWh Chile Battery Storage Project SINEXCEL has completed the shipment of all power conversion systems for a 100 MW/400 MWh battery energy storage project in Chile, according to a company press release. The Shenzhen-listed firm said the delivery covers the full order of StellaON 1250K units for RelyEZ Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd. The project is a four-hour system located in the Atacama region. It is designed to charge when demand is lower and discharge during peak periods, a pattern intended to support grid flexibility and project returns. Delivery Timing and Project Execution SINEXCEL stated that it completed the full power conversion system order on schedule. The company said this helps RelyEZ Energy protect the timetable for transport, installation, commissioning, and grid connection. According to the release, large-scale overseas projects depend on production, inspection, and shipment schedules staying closely aligned with on-site construction. Coordinated delivery is described as reducing uncertainty and helping local teams plan subsequent stages, since delays in a single batch can narrow the construction window for a project of this scale. Equipment Specifications for Atacama Conditions The StellaON 1250K power conversion system is built for environments that can include high temperatures, dust, and sand. SINEXCEL reported a maximum efficiency of 99% and a rated-power efficiency of 98.5% for the unit. The system supports operation from minus 40 degrees Celsius to 60 degrees Celsius, maintains full power output at 55 degrees Celsius, and carries an IP65 protection rating. The company said maintaining rated output in high temperatures can reduce power derating and the need for additional capacity, while higher conversion efficiency limits energy losses across repeated charge-discharge cycles. Service Network and Company Scale Following shipment, the Chilean project moves into on-site installation and commissioning. SINEXCEL said it has a dedicated after-sales team in Latin America and seven service centres across the Americas. Technical requests can receive a response within 30 minutes, backed by round-the-clock support and a seven-day spare-parts guarantee. SINEXCEL reported that it has deployed more than 17 GW of energy storage capacity across over 5,000 projects and works with more than 600 partners in more than 60 countries and regions. The company said it will continue to expand its local operations across Latin America and provide customers with support throughout the project lifecycle. Founded in 2007, SINEXCEL describes itself as a pioneer in energy storage, electric vehicle charging, and power quality solutions. Its disclosed deployments include 17 GW of installed storage, 200,000 electric vehicle DC chargers, and nearly 20 million amperes of active harmonic filters. - 1.
