artigo.texto: - Category - Defense Tech Three Yandex Data Centers Hit in Four Days—Now All of Its Supercomputers May Be Down A series of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian data centers may have knocked all three of Yandex’s supercomputers offline, potentially taking out half of the six largest supercomputing systems operating in Russia, Russian technology outlet T-Invariant reported on October 11. The first strike came overnight on October 8 against Yandex’s Sasovo data center in Russia’s Ryazan region. The facility, operating since 2014, hosts two of the company’s three supercomputers—Chervonenkis, with a peak performance of 29.42 petaflops, and Lyapunov, rated at 20.03 petaflops. We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field. Chervonenkis is Yandex’s most powerful machine and had been Russia’s strongest newly built supercomputer of the past 15 years. When it entered service in 2021, it ranked 19th in the global TOP500 list. It has since fallen into the second hundred as sanctions and limited access to advanced hardware made infrastructure upgrades increasingly difficult. A second strike followed on October 9 against Yandex’s data center in Kaluga, located in the Grabtsevo industrial park. Yandex describes the site as its largest data center and one of the biggest such facilities in Russia. Two days later, on October 11, another strike hit the company’s Vladimir data center, home to its third supercomputer, Galushkin, which has a peak performance of 20.64 petaflops. According to T-Invariant, all three Yandex supercomputers are now out of service. Experts interviewed by the outlet said the attacks may have caused enormous damage to Russia’s high-performance computing infrastructure, particularly because the facilities were built long before physical protection against drone strikes became a serious consideration. “Yandex built its centers and supercomputers in peacetime and for peacetime. All development focused on normal human life; nobody imagined drones would hit the roof. Earthquakes and other natural disasters are not expected in the Ryazan and Vladimir regions, so nobody thought about investing in physical protection for the buildings,” one supercomputing expert told the outlet. Yandex built the systems primarily to train neural networks and handle large-scale machine-learning workloads. All three rely on AMD EPYC processors and NVIDIA A100 accelerators connected through high-speed InfiniBand networking—hardware that Russian companies have found increasingly difficult to obtain in large quantities. One expert argued that restoring systems of this scale could prove far more difficult than simply repairing a damaged building. “It will not be possible to restore supercomputers of this level. And it is not even about the availability of money. The main problem is not even sanctions, but the shortage of chips and other components: there is a huge queue for them around the world. However, the costs of gray and black imports are also very high,” the specialist said. T-Invariant noted that Russia’s remaining major supercomputing capacity is concentrated around Moscow. Sberbank’s Christofari and Christofari Neo are located in Skolkovo, an area considered relatively well protected by air defenses, while MTS operates its GROM supercomputer in Lytkarino. Yandex also maintains other data centers in Mytishchi and Ivanteyevka in the Moscow region. Previously, Russia’s internet segment suffered widespread outages hours after a retaliatory Ukrainian drone strike hit a Yandex data center in the Ryazan region. Discuss this article:

artigo.texto: Recently, the "Hydrogen Wind Series portable hydrogen power generation equipment" independently developed by Guangdong Huachen Hydrogen Energy Co., Ltd. is about to be officially released. As the first product in this series, the world's first 200W portable hydrogen power generation equipmentwas officially released at the "Five New" power equipment technology exhibition and new-type power system equipment upgrade technology conference during the 28th China (Shenzhen) International Hi-Tech Fair. Innovative hybrid energy architecture addresses mobile energy storage endurance pain points In scenarios such as emergency rescue, power repair, communication support, field operations, and outdoor mobile power consumption, energy supply is often constrained by multiple factors including fixed power grid coverage, equipment endurance, refueling efficiency, and transportation conditions. Especially in long-duration continuous operation environments, traditional mobile energy storage equipment mainly relies on increasing battery capacity to improve endurance, but the resulting increases in weight, volume, and charging time can also affect equipment mobility and usage efficiency. To address these needs, the Hydrogen Wind Series portable hydrogen power generation equipment is designed around the concept of "continuous power generation," using coordinated operation of multiple energy systems to build a mobile energy solution suitable for off-grid scenarios. The product adopts ahybrid energy architecture in which aluminum-based energy storage materials, hydrogen fuel cells, and lithium batteries work in coordination. Among them, aluminum-based energy storage materials handle energy storage functions, hydrogen fuel cells are responsible for energy conversion, and lithium batteries respond to equipment start-stop, instantaneous loads, and power fluctuations, achieving coordinated operation across energy storage, power generation conversion, and stable output. At the same time, the product adopts a modular refueling approach, enabling rapid refueling by replacing aluminum-based energy storage materials, and can flexibly configure energy reserves according to different mission durations and actual load requirements, enhancing continuous power generation capability while maintaining equipment portability. First 200W product released, covering diverse civilian and professional scenarios As the first product in the Hydrogen Wind Series, the world's first 200W portable hydrogen power generation equipment is primarily aimed at mobile application scenarios with high requirements for equipment portability, continuous power supply capability, and refueling flexibility. In the civilian sector, the product can serve outdoor travel, mobile office work, drone power supply, and other needs; in professional application fields, it can be further extended to emergency support, power and communication operations, and field operations, providing new power generation solutions for mobile electricity use in different environments. Starting with the 200W product, Guangdong Huachen Hydrogen Energy will continue to improve the Hydrogen Wind Series product lineup around different power levels and application needs, gradually forming a portable hydrogen power generation equipment portfolio covering multiple types of scenarios. Engineering validation continues to advance, safety assurance system refined Moving from laboratory technology to end-use products, engineering validation is a critical step in promoting product application. Currently, Hydrogen Wind Series products have undergone testing and validation around application scenarios such as emergency rescue, power repair, communication support, and field operations, with continuous optimization of system stability, safety, and environmental adaptability in complex environments. In terms of safety assurance, the product is equipped with an intelligent monitoring system that provides real-time monitoring of key parameters such as system operating status, temperature, and pressure, and enhances system operational reliability through multiple safety protection mechanisms. At the same time, to meet the demands of outdoor and complex environment applications, the product features targeted designs for wide-temperature-range operation, wind and sand resistance, and dust protection. Guangdong Huachen Hydrogen Energy Co., Ltd. is a hydrogen energy end-user industrialisation platform wholly established by Zhongyun Intelligent Technology (Guangzhou) Co., Ltd., primarily focused on high-end hydrogen energy end-use equipment R&D, scenario-based solutions, and industrialisation applications. The launch of the "Hydrogen Wind Series" portable hydrogen power generation equipment represents an important step for the company in advancing scenario-based, productised, and industrialised applications of hydrogen energy technology.

artigo.texto: CHARLOTTE, N.C., Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Magnera today announced it has entered into a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) with the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Army Research Laboratory to evaluate and advance next-generation battery separator technologies, supporting evolving energy requirements across defense, critical infrastructure, and commercial applications. The collaboration will leverage Magnera's OmniSep™ platform, an advanced separator technology engineered to enhance battery performance, safety, and reliability in demanding operating environments. Designed with high ionic conductivity, superior electrolyte wettability, and enhanced thermal stability1, OmniSep™ supports the power, efficiency, and safety requirements of next-generation battery systems. The initiative aligns with the Department of War's growing emphasis on resilient energy, electrification, and assured power for distributed and contested operations. As the military deploys increasingly power-intensive capabilities, including autonomous systems, ISR platforms, electronic warfare, counter-UAS technologies, resilient communications, and directed energy systems, the need for safe, high-performance energy storage continues to grow. Advances in separator technology could help extend operational endurance, enhance system performance, improve safety, and reduce logistical burdens across a broad range of current and future defense applications. "Energy resilience and advanced battery technologies will play an increasingly important role in national security, infrastructure modernization, and the future of mobility," said Curt Begle, Chief Executive Officer of Magnera. "This collaboration is an investment in technologies that can enable the next generation of energy storage solutions. By combining the Army Research Laboratory's research capabilities with Magnera's advanced materials expertise, we have the opportunity to accelerate innovations with potential impact across defense, critical infrastructure, and commercial markets." Designed and manufactured in the United States, OmniSep™ reflects Magnera's commitment to strengthening the nation's advanced manufacturing and materials ecosystem. Leveraging domestic production capabilities and U.S.-sourced raw materials, the platform supports secure, resilient supply chains for mission-critical energy storage technologies while reinforcing American industrial competitiveness. 1 Based on internal testing About Magnera Magnera Corporation (NYSE: MAGN) serves 1,000+ customers worldwide, offering a wide range of material solutions, including components for absorbent hygiene products, protective apparel, wipes, specialty building and construction products, and products serving the food and beverage industry. Operating across 44 global production facilities, Magnera is supported by 8,000+ employees. Magnera’s purpose is to better the world with new possibilities made real. artigo.texto: Nightpeak Energy's Bocanova 2 Battery Storage Project Reaches Financial Close and Commercial Operation Nightpeak Energy reported on October 13, 2026, that its Bocanova 2 battery storage facility in Southeast Texas, sized at 150 MW with a two-hour duration, has achieved both financial close and commercial operation. The company stated the project went into commercial service on September 17, lifting the Bocanova site's total capacity to 300 MW and contributing added flexibility to the ERCOT grid amid surging electricity demand from data centers and other large loads. Located in Brazoria County near the Houston metropolitan area, Bocanova 2 represents the second phase of Nightpeak's battery storage buildout there. Bocanova 1, the initial 150 MW phase, entered commercial operation in August 2025. Tesla's Megapack 2 XL battery storage systems equip the project. It runs under a long-term offtake agreement with an investment-grade counterparty, with financing arranged via a tax equity bridge loan and a construction-to-term loan from MUFG Bank, while U.S. Bank supplied traditional tax equity. Paris Hays, Co-founder and CEO/CDO of Nightpeak Energy, noted that large loads are connecting to the grid at a speed and magnitude that is reshaping how the power sector anticipates new demand. Hays remarked that Texas leads this growth, and addressing it will demand substantial new infrastructure along with resources capable of responding swiftly as conditions shift. Hays further stated that with 300 MW now active at Bocanova, the company is deploying that flexibility in one of the nation's most dynamic power markets, and thanked the City of Alvin, Brazoria County, and the local community for their backing. Founded in 2022, Nightpeak has built and purchased a portfolio exceeding 1 GW of operating and de-risked capacity across gas-fired generation, battery storage, and powered land development, while continuing to push forward an additional pipeline of flexible generation and large-load projects to serve rising U.S. demand. Nightpeak Energy develops, owns, and operates flexible power generation and large-load enablement assets aimed at meeting growing electricity and AI demand while fostering a reliable, lower-carbon electric grid. Using a technology-agnostic strategy spanning gas-fired generation, energy storage, renewables, and large-load project types, the company merges generation and load into integrated solutions for its customers. artigo.texto: Abengoa Major historical player, now restructured According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Parabolic Trough Collectors market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global parabolic trough collectors (PTC) market is entering a phase of renewed strategic importance as energy systems prioritize dispatchable renewable capacity. Unlike photovoltaic systems, PTCs integrate cost-effective thermal energy storage, enabling electricity generation or industrial heat supply beyond daylight hours. This report analyzes the market from 2026 to 2035, covering complete collector assemblies, mirrors, receiver tubes, support structures, and tracking systems. The analysis identifies utility-scale CSP plants as the dominant end-use, while industrial process heat, district heating, desalination, and enhanced oil recovery offer diversification pathways. The competitive landscape features established engineering firms and specialized component manufacturers. Regional dynamics are shaped by solar resource quality, policy support, and local manufacturing capabilities. The forecast baseline assumes moderate policy continuity, declining technology costs, and growing recognition of long-duration storage value. Key risks include competition from PV-plus-battery systems, permitting delays, and supply chain concentration. The report provides a data-driven outlook for manufacturers, EPC contractors, investors, and policymakers navigating this evolving market. The baseline scenario for the parabolic trough collectors market from 2026 to 2035 anticipates moderate but steady expansion, with a compound annual growth rate of 4.2% in real terms. This outlook is anchored in the unique value proposition of PTCs: the ability to store thermal energy at scale, providing dispatchable power and heat that complements variable renewable sources. Demand growth will not replicate the subsidy-driven boom of the 2010s; instead, it will be driven by integrated energy projects, hybrid configurations, and industrial decarbonization mandates. Utility-scale CSP plants will remain the largest segment, but their share will gradually erode as industrial process heat and district heating applications gain traction. Technological improvements, including higher-temperature receivers and advanced molten salt systems, will enhance efficiency and lower levelized costs. Supply chain constraints for specialized components, such as evacuated receiver tubes, may temper growth in certain years. Geographically, the Middle East and Africa, along with Asia-Pacific, will account for the majority of new capacity additions, supported by national energy diversification plans. North America and Europe will see selective deployment, often linked to research or hybrid projects. The market index, with 2025 as the base year at 100, is projected to reach 151 by 2035, reflecting cumulative growth. This baseline assumes no major policy reversals and a gradual decline in capital costs, consistent with historical learning curves. Utility-scale CSP plants remain the primary end-use for parabolic trough collectors, leveraging the technology's proven ability to generate dispatchable electricity with integrated thermal energy storage. Currently, new CSP capacity is concentrated in the Middle East, North Africa, and parts of Asia, where strong solar resources and policy support align. Through 2035, demand will be driven by grid operators' need for flexible, firm capacity to balance high shares of photovoltaic and wind generation. The key demand-side indicators include national renewable energy targets, capacity auction schedules, and the levelized cost of storage. While the segment's absolute volume will grow, its share of the overall PTC market will decline as industrial and district heating applications expand. Hybridization with gas or PV will become more common, enhancing dispatchability and reducing risk. Major projects in countries like Morocco, Dubai, and Chile will anchor demand, but growth will be tempered by competition from alternative storage technologies. Current trend: Dominant but gradually declining share as other applications grow. Major trends: Integration of thermal energy storage for extended dispatchability, Hybridization with photovoltaic and gas turbines, Shift towards higher-temperature molten salt systems, Increasing project sizes in sunbelt regions, and Declining levelized cost of electricity. Representative participants: Abengoa, Sener, Acciona, Cobra Energía, and TSK Flagsol. Industrial process heat represents a rapidly emerging application for parabolic trough collectors, as manufacturers in sectors such as food processing, chemicals, and textiles seek to reduce carbon emissions from high-temperature steam generation. Currently, adoption is limited to pilot and demonstration projects, but declining costs and corporate sustainability commitments are accelerating deployment. Through 2035, demand will be driven by carbon pricing mechanisms, renewable heat incentives, and the need for reliable, on-site thermal energy. Key demand-side indicators include industrial energy prices, emissions regulations, and the availability of turnkey PTC solutions. Unlike CSP plants, industrial projects are smaller and modular, enabling faster deployment and lower capital risk. However, integration with existing steam systems and space constraints can pose challenges. The segment's share is expected to rise significantly, supported by growing interest from multinational corporations aiming for net-zero operations. Current trend: Fastest-growing segment, driven by decarbonization mandates. Major trends: Modular PTC systems for on-site steam generation, Corporate net-zero commitments driving adoption, Integration with existing industrial boilers, Government incentives for renewable heat, and Focus on cost reduction through standardized designs. artigo.texto: Proposed 1-year moratorium on data centers, task force fails after Fort Wayne City Council vote FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WPTA) - Proposals for a one-year data center moratorium and a data center task force failed Tuesday, ending a contentious debate between Fort Wayne City Council members. BACKGROUND: Fort Wayne council member proposes one-year data center moratorium Councilwoman Rohli Booker introduced the proposals last month, which would have kept the city council from approving any new data center projects and created a comprehensive data center development standard. It would have stopped short of halting the existing Google data center project underway in southeast Fort Wayne. “If there was ever a perfect time to pause, it’s now,” Booker said ahead of the proposals failing in a 3-to-5 vote for the task force and a 4-to-4 vote for the moratorium. “We know that Fort Wayne has a lot to offer; we have water, we have infrastructure, we have economic development incentives, we have a state that has made it very clear that it wants these types of developments,” she said. “Indiana has practically put up a neon sign saying that ‘We are open for business.’” “I don’t think anyone is confused about that.” Councilman Russ Jehl also voted yes. He said he thinks a big reason why the resolutions weren’t passed is that the Department of Planning Services is now increasing its involvement. “The Department of Planning Services, whose job is to create some guardrails for land use, is finally getting a little bit in motion,” he said. Tonight’s meeting also had a big turnout from a local electrical workers’ union. Recently, members of the union posted on Facebook to express concerns about the moratorium’s potential impact on future jobs. “I think we finally saw some of the stakeholders, like the trades, come and say, ‘Oh, by the way, there are actually some tangible benefits, like my job being produced, and that there are a lot more jobs than the perception is,’” Jehl said. Councilwoman Michelle Chambers was one of the people voting no. She said some definitions in the moratorium were not specific, including the phrase “data centers.” “We cannot have such an open-ended definition,” she said. “We had to be very clear, so that we don’t have other data-driven organizations, corporations, be affected by a moratorium that was attempting to deal with what data centers do.” RELATED: Fort Wayne neighbors say Google data center noise, lights disrupt their lives | Story continues below previous coverage Councilman Nathan Hartman, who has consistently stated his opposition to the proposal, expressed concerns that it would create issues for developments such as schools and hospitals. “I’m still a no on this. I’m not convinced that this is good policy, and I feel like that this sends the wrong message to not just our community, but to our other partners throughout the state,” he said. artigo.texto: Romania’s mergers and acquisitions (M&A) market recorded 212 transactions in the first nine months of 2026, down slightly from 215 deals in the same period last year, according to an analysis by EY. Despite the 1% decline in transaction volume, the estimated value of the market increased by 33% to USD 7.1 billion, from USD 5.4 billion in the first nine months of 2025. The value of disclosed transactions rose by 39% to USD 4.1 billion, driven largely by three major acquisitions announced in the first half of the year. The three largest transactions were Paval Holding’s USD 977 million acquisition of Carrefour Romania, Premier Energy’s USD 824 million acquisition of Evryo Group, and Raiffeisen Bank International’s USD 681 million acquisition of Garanti BBVA Romania. Together, they accounted for approximately 60% of the total disclosed deal value during the period. M&A activity slows in the third quarter Romania’s performance followed a broader international trend of higher transaction values despite declining deal volumes. Across Europe, M&A value increased by 54% in the first nine months of 2026, while global deal value rose by 28%. Meanwhile, transaction volumes fell by 11% in Europe and 8% globally. Following a particularly strong first half, global M&A activity slowed in the third quarter, with total deal value falling below USD 1 trillion for the first time since Q2 2025, according to LSEG. Only ten transactions exceeding USD 10 billion were announced worldwide, the lowest quarterly number of mega-deals since Q4 2024. The slowdown came amid rising energy costs, renewed inflationary pressures, and higher expectations for long-term interest rates. Romania also recorded weaker M&A activity in Q3 2026, with transaction volume down 9% and disclosed deal value falling 15% compared with the same quarter in 2025. No transactions exceeding USD 100 million were announced during the quarter. One notable deal was the acquisition of Pall-Ex Romania by BoldMind Capital Partners and the company’s executive management team through a leveraged buyout valued at approximately USD 29 million. Pall-Ex Romania provides domestic and international palletised freight distribution services as part of a wider European network. Another significant regional development, although outside the scope of EY’s Romanian M&A database, was Canadian group Alimentation Couche-Tard’s announced voluntary tender offer for Żabka Group, Poland’s largest convenience retailer. Żabka operates more than 13,000 stores across Poland and Romania, including the Froo convenience store chain on the Romanian market. The offer implied an equity valuation of approximately USD 8.6 billion. Foreign investors drive deal activity Strategic investors remained the dominant buyers in Romania’s M&A market, accounting for 83% of transaction volume during the first nine months of 2026. Direct acquisitions by financial sponsors declined by 17% year-on-year, with more than one-third involving transactions across multiple countries. However, when acquisitions by private equity-backed companies are also considered, financial sponsor-backed buyers accounted for approximately 28% of total deal volume. Cross-border investment continued to play a significant role. Inbound acquisitions increased by 13% year-on-year to 124 transactions, while domestic deals declined by 10% to 78. Inbound acquisitions also exceeded the 70 transactions involving disposals by foreign-owned businesses, indicating that foreign investors continued to expand their presence in the Romanian market. The United States remained the leading source of foreign investors, with 16 transactions, followed by France and Austria with 11 each. The United Kingdom ranked fourth with seven deals, while Poland followed with six. Real estate and technology lead by deal volume, while energy storage attracts investment Real Estate, Hospitality & Construction remained the most active sector, with 46 transactions during the first nine months of 2026. Technology, Media & Telecommunications (TMT) ranked second with 40 deals, maintaining its position from the corresponding period of 2025. Nearly a quarter of TMT transactions involved technology acquisitions spanning multiple countries, while the telecommunications segment accounted for just one deal. Advanced Manufacturing & Mobility followed with 37 transactions, up 37% year-on-year. The increase was driven entirely by stronger activity in advanced manufacturing, as mobility deal volumes remained unchanged. Foreign buyers accounted for approximately two-thirds of the sector’s transactions. Energy & Utilities ranked fourth with 30 deals, approximately half of which involved foreign acquisitions of battery energy storage system (BESS) projects, reflecting investor interest in Romania’s developing energy storage market. Consumer Products & Retail and Health & Life Sciences each recorded 19 transactions, representing annual declines of 32% and 41%, respectively. The decrease in healthcare-related M&A followed an active period in 2025, when the market recorded a high number of veterinary clinic acquisitions.

artigo.texto: Navitas, NVIDIA collaborate on power delivery board for AI data centers Navitas Semiconductor NVTS announced Monday its latest 24 kW, 800 V-to-12 V DC-DC power delivery board, or PDB. The company highlighted that its power delivery board is powered by GaNFast™ technology and developed in collaboration with NVIDIA NVDA to support the NVIDIA MGX ecosystem and advance 800 VDC power architectures for AI data centers. Shares of NVTS jumped more than 5% in extended trading. This latest 24 kW, 800 V-to-12 V PDB extends Navitas’ portfolio of 800 VDC AI data-center platforms, building on the previously announced 20 kW, 800 V-to-6 V PDB developed in collaboration with NVIDIA, the company noted, adding that "These solutions advance the core strategic focus of the Navitas 2.0 transformation to accelerate the replacement of legacy silicon with next-generation GaN and SiC high-power technologies across AI infrastructure, from Grid-to-xPU." The company highlighted that its power delivery board is designed in NVIDIA’s latest 400 mm × 60 mm form factor and could be integrated onto the compute motherboard as close as possible to the xPUs, minimizing power-delivery losses and supporting high-power demands. “The next era of AI will be defined not only by how much compute we can create but by our ability to deliver the power needed to unleash its full potential,” said Chris Allexandre, President and CEO of Navitas. “Our collaboration with NVIDIA is breaking the AI infrastructure power wall by reimagining power delivery from 800 VDC to the GPU. This next-generation 24 kW solution demonstrates how GaNFast™ technology can eliminate power-conversion stages, increase efficiency and power density, and bring power closer to the GPU.” The company announced that the 800 V-to-12 V PDB is planned to be showcased at the NVIDIA AI Factory MGX Wall partner display area at OCP Global Summit 2026. artigo.texto: Co-locating solar power plants with battery energy storage systems (BESS) can improve the economics and reliability of firm renewable power, but the project design must balance cost, supply reliability and renewable energy curtailment, according to a new study by the Center for Study of Science, Technology and Policy (CSTEP). The study, titled ‘Co-locating solar and battery storage for reliable power supply’, examines how solar and battery capacities should be sized to meet defined power delivery obligations, using a Karnataka case study of a continuous 100-MW power block over durations ranging from two hours to 24 hours. It finds that the optimal combination depends not just on the duration but also the time of power delivery. Obligations extending into non-solar hours require more storage and can raise costs. Across the modelled optimal configurations, the levelised cost of energy ranged from ₹5.73 to ₹6.79 per kWh. For a round-the-clock supply obligation, the model’s preferred configuration comprised 515 MW of solar capacity and 1,300 MWh of battery storage. It covered 76.4 per cent of annual demand at ₹5.73 per kWh. Raising demand coverage to 85.8 per cent would require 768 MW of solar and 3,120 MWh of storage, increasing the cost to ₹8.32 per kWh. CSTEP recommends that renewable-plus-storage tenders explicitly consider curtailment alongside cost and demand fulfilment. It also calls for geographic information system-based site selection and delivery schedules designed around actual power system requirements, rather than standardised supply windows. The study cautions that grid import and export constraints, dependence on imported battery cells and uncertainty over long-term revenue streams remain barriers. It also notes that its analysis did not account for battery degradation over the project lifetime. The central message is that simply adding batteries to solar projects will not guarantee economical, reliable power. Procurement must be designed around factors such as the time of electricity supply and how efficiently the combined system can deliver it. Minister Pralhad Joshi leaves RoW resolution to states New and Renewable Energy Minister Pralhad Joshi has left the ‘right of way’ issues plaguing the wind industry to the State governments, saying the ball is in the states’ courts, because “land is a State subject”. Answering a question at a press conference in Chennai, on the sidelines of the Windergy 2026 event recently, Joshi called upon State governments to solve the RoW issues — after all, it is in their interest to get cheap clean energy, something that will help industries to export. In this context, Joshi referred to the Green Energy Corridor-III scheme, announced recently with an outlay of ₹1.86 lakh crore, including a central government assistance of ₹55,000 crore, for which the State governments would have to compete (”challenge mode”). He said land availability would be an important factor in such a competition. Wind installations in India are growing. After a poor record in the first quarter of the current year (1.35 GW), projects picked up to reach 3.1 GW in the first six months, raising hopes for annual installations of around 7 GW. Yet, the big factor hampering smooth implementation of wind projects is the RoW issue, with most projects suffering delays from filibustering protests in the name of extracting fair compensation for the landowners from the developers. Recently, the Ministry of Power came out with tweaked guidelines for paying compensation, but industry fears that protests may continue regardless. Published on October 12, 2026

artigo.texto: Prime Minister Narendra Modi lays the foundation stone for a 250 MW / 500 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, on October 11, 2026. The project is being developed by NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), a wholly owned subsidiary of NLC India Limited, marking a significant step towards strengthening energy storage infrastructure in the state. The project will be established across three locations in Tamil Nadu: Ottapidaram, Anuppankulam and Kayathar. With a combined capacity of 250 MW and 500 MWh, the battery storage system is designed to support electricity demand during peak hours and improve the flexibility and reliability of the power grid. Battery energy storage systems play an important role in addressing the intermittent nature of renewable energy generation. By storing surplus electricity and releasing it when demand increases or renewable generation declines, these systems can help balance electricity supply and demand. The proposed project is expected to support the integration of renewable energy into the electricity network by providing storage capacity that can improve grid management. It will also contribute to meeting peak-hour power requirements and strengthening the stability of the power system. The initiative comes amid India’s broader efforts to expand renewable energy capacity and develop supporting infrastructure to ensure reliable electricity supply. As solar and wind power installations continue to grow, energy storage is becoming increasingly important for managing variations in generation and maintaining grid stability. Through this project, NIRL and its parent company, NLC India Limited, are contributing to the development of energy storage infrastructure in Tamil Nadu. The project is expected to support the state’s clean energy transition while reinforcing the role of battery storage in building a more flexible and reliable electricity system. artigo.texto: Amwins Global Risks (AGR) is expanding its specialist commercial and industrial (C&I) insurance facility to cover battery energy storage systems (BESS) and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. The facility groups distributed assets under a single program, with deductibles scaled to individual site characteristics rather than to utility-scale norms. The structure is designed for portfolios that sit between the two ends of the existing insurance market: too small for utility-scale terms, too numerous to place site by site. The London-based wholesale broker has previously applied the same portfolio aggregation logic to distributed solar assets, grouping commercial and community-scale projects under a single program structure. The BESS and EV charging expansion applies that same structure to two asset classes where the market gap is arguably sharper. The BESS insurance market has been expanding, but unevenly. A number of insurers have restricted or withdrawn capacity following battery fires in the UK and overseas, a trend documented by market participants including Allianz UK, which expanded its own BESS underwriting capability in July 2026 partly in response to gaps left by capacity withdrawals. That means brokers face a market where appetite and expertise are not evenly distributed. Allianz UK expanded its own BESS underwriting capability in July 2026, with its head of construction, engineering and energy insurance noting that early engagement with experienced underwriters is increasingly valuable given how quickly the risk landscape is developing. For C&I assets specifically, the challenge is structural as much as technical. Individual sites can be relatively small in value, but developers are assembling portfolios of dozens of them across multiple locations. Applying terms designed for a large utility-scale installation to a single C&I site can produce deductibles that are disproportionate to the asset’s value, making the insurance economically unworkable. The Amwins facility is designed to resolve that by underwriting at portfolio level while still assessing accumulated natural catastrophe exposure across individual locations. “Individual sites can be relatively small, but developers are increasingly building portfolios comprising numerous assets across multiple locations," said Tom Harries, director at Amwins Global Risks. "Bringing those assets together allows us to underwrite them efficiently at portfolio scale, while still recognising the individual risk characteristics of each site.” The facility covers both construction and operational phases, including delay in start-up and business interruption cover. The EV charging component is primarily directed at the US market, where commercial charging infrastructure is being deployed at scale. Amwins Global Risks operates from London and places through the London market, giving US-based developers and their brokers access to London capacity for risks that the domestic US market has been slower to accommodate in structured form. Harries said the addition of BESS and EV charging reflects the increasing convergence of distributed energy technologies, and that the facility is designed to adapt as portfolios grow. “It allows us to focus on monitoring how the portfolio’s natural catastrophe exposure changes as new projects are added and gives developers the freedom to concentrate on building out their portfolios, knowing their insurance program can adapt and grow alongside them.” The C&I expansion follows AGR’s renewal and enlargement of a separate natural catastrophe facility for renewable energy projects in July 2026, which increased available capacity to $50 million per placement from $20 million and broadened cover to all major natural catastrophe perils globally. The two moves extend AGR’s distributed and renewable energy proposition across construction, operation and catastrophe layers within a matter of months.

The global Battery Manufacturing Machines Market is a critical capital equipment segment enabling the scale-up of battery production for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. This market encompasses machinery for electrode manufacturing, cell assembly, module and pack assembly, and testing. Demand is structurally driven by the proliferation of gigafactories worldwide, supported by regional localization mandates and subsidies. The transition toward advanced chemistries such as LFP, high-nickel NMC, and solid-state batteries is a primary catalyst for capital expenditure, requiring significant retooling and creating opportunities for technology disruptors. The supply chain faces constraints from long lead times for high-precision components, impacting turnkey line delivery. Competitive advantage is bifurcating between integrated turnkey line exporters and specialized process machine leaders. Factory economics increasingly prioritize throughput, yield, and sustainability, driving adoption of dry electrode coating, solvent-free mixing, and AI-powered inspection. The qualification and integration burden elevates the role of system integrators and EPC specialists. After-sales service and spare parts logistics constitute a high-margin segment. Regulatory evolution around battery passports and carbon footprint tracking is becoming a direct design input for manufacturing equipment. The market is forecast to grow at a robust CAGR through 2035, with Asia-Pacific leading in supply and demand, followed by North America and Europe. The baseline scenario for the Battery Manufacturing Machines Market from 2026 to 2035 anticipates robust growth, driven by the global energy transition and the accelerating adoption of electric vehicles. The market is projected to expand at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9.2%, reaching a market index of 245 by 2035 (2025=100). This growth is underpinned by the continued announcement and construction of gigafactories, particularly in North America, Europe, and Southeast Asia, as governments and automakers invest heavily in localizing battery supply chains. The demand for battery manufacturing machines is not merely about capacity expansion; it is increasingly about manufacturing excellence, cost reduction, and sustainability. The shift toward new chemistries, such as lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and solid-state batteries, necessitates new equipment and retooling, creating fresh capital expenditure cycles. The supply side is characterized by long lead times for critical components, such as high-precision lasers and vacuum systems, which can constrain delivery schedules. Competitive dynamics are evolving, with turnkey line providers competing on scale and project delivery, while specialized machine makers focus on technological differentiation. The aftermarket for service, upgrades, and spare parts is expected to grow in importance, offering high-margin opportunities. Regionally, Asia-Pacific will maintain its dominance in both production and consumption, but North America and Europe are expected to gain share as localization efforts intensify. Risks to the outlook include potential delays in gigafactory projects, raw material price volatility, and geopolitical tensions affecting supply chains. However, the long-term trajectory remains positive, supported by decarbonization goals and technological advancements. The electric vehicle (EV) battery manufacturing segment is the largest end-use sector for battery manufacturing machines, accounting for over half of global demand. This segment is driven by the rapid expansion of EV production capacity worldwide, as automakers race to electrify their fleets. Battery manufacturing machines are essential for producing lithium-ion cells and packs at scale, with processes including electrode coating, cell assembly, and module/pack assembly. The demand is characterized by high-volume, high-precision requirements, as EV batteries must meet stringent safety, performance, and cost targets. Through 2035, this segment will continue to grow, albeit with shifting dynamics. The transition from NMC to LFP chemistries for entry-level EVs will require different equipment, while solid-state batteries may disrupt the market later in the forecast period. Demand-side indicators include EV sales penetration rates, battery pack prices, and government EV mandates. The segment is dominated by major battery manufacturers such as CATL, LG Energy Solution, and Tesla, who are also key customers for machine suppliers. The trend toward vertical integration among automakers and battery makers is expected to influence equipment procurement strategies, with a growing emphasis on turnkey lines and local sourcing. artigo.texto: Land & Expand: North America's Data Center Pipeline Expands Under Pressure Key Highlights - Large-scale projects like Fluidstack's 1.5 GW AI data center in Texas exemplify the industry's move toward industrial-scale infrastructure supporting advanced computing needs. - Community opposition and regulatory scrutiny are increasingly influencing project approvals, as seen in Mahomet, Illinois, where public opposition halted negotiations. - Developers are securing land, power, and water infrastructure while addressing local concerns about environmental impact, noise, and costs, reflecting a more complex development environment. - Major tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and AWS are expanding their regional footprints with multi-phase campuses, often integrating renewable energy and onsite generation. - The data center pipeline remains robust, with projects at various stages—from land acquisition to construction—highlighting ongoing industry growth despite rising development challenges. Land & Expand is Data Center Frontier's periodic look at the latest data center development news, including new sites, land acquisitions and campus expansions across North America. This latest installment finds the development pipeline continuing to expand, even as the requirements for bringing large-scale projects online grow more complicated. Developers are securing land, planning new power infrastructure and advancing campuses measured in hundreds of megawatts or more. At the same time, local governments and residents are demanding greater clarity on electricity costs, water consumption, noise, tax incentives and the long-term effects of industrial-scale computing facilities. A succession of development disclosures and project milestones through September and early October 2026 illustrates both the geographical reach of North America's expanding data center pipeline and the growing difficulty of measuring how much proposed capacity will ultimately be delivered. The projects range from preliminary discussions and newly secured development sites to campuses already under construction. Some are advancing through formal permitting and power studies; others remain contingent on customers, financing or local approvals. Together, they reveal an industry still expanding aggressively, but operating under increasingly complex development conditions. Fluidstack: Cameron County, Texas — Up to 1.5 GW One of the largest newly disclosed projects is Fluidstack's AI data center development in Cameron County in the Rio Grande Valley. The project surfaced publicly September 10 when Cameron County announced that it had issued Fluidstack a worksite permit for property near Harlingen. The permit authorizes preliminary site work, including grading, utilities and related infrastructure, rather than construction of the data center buildings themselves. Fluidstack subsequently disclosed considerably more detail on September 21, saying construction had begun on a $4 billion first phase capable of supporting as much as 1.5 GW. Fluidstack expects the project to generate more than 2,500 construction jobs and several hundred permanent positions. The company has placed unusual emphasis on the project's local infrastructure impact. It says it requested no local property-tax abatements and intends to pay for the energy, water and infrastructure necessary to serve the campus. Cooling will use a recirculating closed-loop system. At up to 1.5 GW in its announced first phase, Cameron County represents a major addition to the Texas AI development pipeline, reflecting the increasingly industrial scale of projects designed to support advanced computing. Microsoft ATL50: Union City, Georgia A new filing for Microsoft's ATL50 campus entered Georgia's Development of Regional Impact review process on September 15. Microsoft filed plans for ATL50, a new data center campus at 5235 Stonewall Tell Road in Union City, southwest of Atlanta. Plans call for two three-story data center buildings totaling approximately 910,000 square feet on 88 acres. The filing projects completion in 2032. Microsoft already has a substantial Georgia footprint, with development activity in Fairburn, Douglasville, Palmetto, Rome, East Point and other communities. ATL50 represents another proposed campus in the greater Atlanta market rather than entry into a new region. No electrical capacity has been disclosed. Project Gravel: Pima County, Arizona Another proposed development emerged through public-records reporting rather than a corporate announcement. Documents obtained in September disclosed Project Gravel, an eight-building data center campus being evaluated on approximately 160 acres of vacant land in unincorporated Pima County west of Sahuarita, Arizona. Plans show eight buildings of roughly 203,000 square feet each, producing a potential campus of approximately 1.6 million square feet, along with a dedicated electrical substation, roads and parking infrastructure. Project documents contemplate full buildout by 2029, contingent on the development advancing through the necessary approvals. County staff had reportedly been evaluating the proposal for months before details became public. Neither the developer nor a prospective tenant has been publicly identified, and the planned electrical load remains undisclosed. The disclosure has already generated local concern: Residents gathered September 29 to discuss the project's potential effects on water, energy use and the surrounding environment. Sahuarita officials subsequently clarified that the proposed site lies outside town boundaries, under Pima County jurisdiction. Project Gravel also illustrates the difficulty in determining the true size of the U.S. development pipeline. Large sites can remain in engineering, environmental and land-use review for months before appearing in conventional industry announcements. Apostas em produção local e gestão de energia, são prioridades. - Cinco anos após iniciar operações em Portugal, a empresa foca em soluções de energia descentralizada, integrando armazenamento e inteligência artificial para otimização. - A Youdera pretende instalar 500 megawatts até 2030, especialmente no setor empresarial, através do modelo Energy-as-a-Service, sem investimento inicial dos clientes. Conteúdo Este resumo foi criado com recurso a inteligência artificial. Embora esta tecnologia tenha sido concebida para ser útil e precisa, pode conter erros ou não captar todas as nuances importantes do artigo. Feedback Se consideras que o resumo não está claro ou não reflete bem o conteúdo, envia o teu feedback. A tua opinião é importante para ajudar a melhorar esta funcionalidade! Partilhar Empresa, que opera em Portugal, Espanha e Suíça, pretende atingir 500 MW de potência instalada nos três mercados até 2030. A Youdera assinala 11 anos de atividade com mais de 2.500 projetos de energia solar realizados em Portugal, Espanha e Suíça e pretende reforçar a aposta em sistemas locais que combinam produção fotovoltaica, armazenamento em baterias e gestão de energia, foi divulgado em comunicado. Segundo a mesma fonte, cinco anos depois de iniciar operações em Portugal, a empresa está a direcionar a sua atividade para soluções de energia descentralizada instaladas nas próprias instalações dos clientes, do lado do consumo, o chamado modelo behind the meter. A estratégia passa por combinar a produção solar com baterias e ferramentas digitais de gestão de energia. Segundo a empresa, a plataforma tecnológica, que recorre a inteligência artificial, permite otimizar a utilização da energia produzida localmente e a eletricidade adquirida à rede. A evolução do modelo de negócio acompanha também um reforço da capacidade de investimento. No início de 2026, a Youdera fechou uma ronda estratégica com a Amundi Energy Transition, associada a um plano de implementação de 150 milhões de euros para infraestruturas de energia distribuída. O financiamento deverá ser aplicado na instalação de novos sistemas, na incorporação de armazenamento em ativos existentes e na aquisição de projetos e portefólios já em operação nos três mercados onde a empresa está presente. “O quinto aniversário de operação da Youdera em Portugal é uma ocasião especial. Temos muito orgulho no trabalho que temos feito no país até aqui”, afirma Pedro Miranda, cofundador e CEO da Youdera. A empresa, acrescenta, começou por financiar projetos solares e evoluiu para um modelo em que constrói e opera sistemas locais de energia nas instalações dos clientes, combinando produção, armazenamento e gestão. A Youdera estabeleceu como objetivo alcançar 500 megawatts (MW) de potência instalada em Portugal, Espanha e Suíça até 2030, através da construção de novos sistemas de geração e armazenamento e da aquisição de projetos e portefólios em funcionamento. Em Portugal, a empresa mantém o foco no desenvolvimento de sistemas locais de energia destinados sobretudo ao setor empresarial, num contexto de procura por soluções que permitam reduzir custos energéticos e aumentar a previsibilidade do consumo. O modelo Energy-as-a-Service adotado pela empresa prevê que os clientes não tenham de realizar o investimento inicial nos equipamentos, ficando a Youdera responsável pelo financiamento, instalação e operação dos sistemas.

artigo.texto: Phoenix is stationing inspectors at Menlo Digital’s Ahwatukee data center construction site in the early morning and has secured a series of commitments from the contractor to reduce noise and other disturbances following complaints from nearby residents. The measures include moving construction traffic farther from homes, restricting early-morning deliveries, relocating employee parking and monitoring noise levels around the property. In an Oct. 9 email to residents, Mike Baxley, assistant director of the city's Planning and Development Department, said the city met with the construction management team and a representative of the project's ownership to address neighborhood concerns. “As with all construction projects, there is a certain amount of noise that the activity of construction will create,” he wrote. “The contractor has committed to taking steps to minimize these aspects of those types of issues.” Baxley’s email was the city’s latest reaction to months of complaints by residents about construction noise, bright lighting and work they contend was occurring outside legally permitted hours at the million-square-foot Menlo Digital data center campus near 48th Street and Thistle Landing Drive. "Earlier today we were able to have a meeting with the onsite management team and a representative of ownership for the Thistle Landing project to identify ways to soften the challenges that neighbors are facing with this project," Baxley wrote. His email also came days before two developments are set this week, one involving the Menlo project and the other data centers generally. On Friday, Oct. 16, construction hours return to a wintertime schedule, with crews permitted to work outside only between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. Monday to Friday unless they secure a special permit from the city Planning and Development Department City Planning Director Joshua Bednarik several weeks ago told residents in an email his department will not give the Menlo Digital data campus company such a permit. From 5-6:30 p.m. today, Oct. 14, Attorney General Kris Mayes will hold a town hall on data centers at The Eagles Community Center, 828 E. Broadway Road, Mesa. “The AG is not investigating the Ahwatukee data center approval,” said Richie Taylor, the attorney general’s communications director. “She is holding a townhall to hear directly from residents about their concerns after receiving multiple complaints from the community.” Mayes subsequently broadened the the town hall's scope to data centers generally. The most significant immediate change outlined by Baxley involves city inspectors. "Starting today, I have asked our Inspections team to have after hours inspectors onsite, in the morning, each work day to ensure that no activity takes place prior to legal start times through the end of the state mandated early construction" period, he wrote. "My hope is that this will ensure compliance and allow the neighbors not to have to worry about having to call in a complaint as we will already have an inspector there to handle any infraction of the mandated start times." The decision represents a more direct approach to monitoring construction activity than relying solely on complaints from neighbors. However, Baxley's email does not indicate that the city has determined any violations occurred. He said his staff is investigating complaints filed Sept. 12, 24, 25, 26 and Oct. 2 to establish what happened and whether enforcement action was warranted. "We use a call service that logs the complaints and notifies the on-call inspector that day," Baxley wrote. "Once I get more information on the complaints for these dates I can respond further as to what the determination of the complaints were and if any action was necessary." The latest development comes as the controversial data center project continues to face opposition from nearby residents, who have raised concerns about its potential effects on their neighborhood. Much of the broader dispute has centered on the facility's anticipated operations, including questions about noise, electricity consumption and other environmental and health impacts. Construction itself quickly evolved as a separate source of friction, particularly for residents living closest to the site. Craig Evans, president of the Ahwatukee Community Alliance, a nonprofit opponents formed to fight the facility, was not impressed by Baxley's message. "It didn’t seem to mean much," he said. "As far as the City of Phoenix seems concerned, the citizens that do most of the living, working and dying in Ahwatukee...aren't all that important to the permitting process. "Disruption to the peace and tranquility of our homes seems an acceptable sacrifice to the City of Phoenix once a permit is issued." "Quite frankly Mr. Baxley should be standing in our neighborhood in the small hours making his own recordings and protecting our interests, rather we suspect his are just the latest effort to discount and dismiss the concerns and suffering the City’s decisions have already inflicted on Ahwatukee." Evans then lashed out at the city process that got the neighbors in the position they're now in. Baxley's email outlines several changes the contractor has agreed to make. Through Oct. 15, when early construction hours are scheduled to end, the contractor has committed not to open the project's gates or turn on construction lighting before the legally permitted start time. Ninguém ficou ferido no ataque, mas alguns serviços da Yandex estão indisponíveis para os usuários desde domingo, informou a empresa. Em nota, a companhia disse estar restabelecendo gradualmente a prestação de serviços. Este é o terceiro grande data center a ser tirado de operação nos últimos dias. Na sexta-feira, a Yandex, que tem forte atuação no desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial na Rússia e às vezes é chamada de "Google russo", informou que seu data center na região de Kaluga, a sudoeste de Moscou, havia sido atingido por drones ucranianos e ficado parcialmente fora de operação. Um dia antes, um ataque ucraniano havia provocado a paralisação do data center da Yandex em Sasovo, a sudeste de Moscou, onde estão instalados dois dos três supercomputadores utilizados para desenvolver o modelo de inteligência artificial da empresa.

artigo.texto: Marrakech – Gotion Power Morocco (GPM) will begin commissioning and starting up the production equipment at its battery gigafactory in Kenitra during the week of October 20. The subsidiary of Chinese group Gotion High-Tech announced the schedule in a statement, describing the plant as the first of its kind in Africa and the Middle East. The startup opens the way to industrial production of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, built from lithium, iron, and phosphate, within a first phase of 20 GWh. GPM president Khalid Qalam had earlier revealed that the first cell line would begin in October, with a second line following in November. He also pointed to a start of sales for assembled batteries by the end of the year. The site sits inside the Atlantic Free Zone of Kenitra and drew MAD 13 billion ($1.3 billion) in investment for its first phase. It will produce cells and batteries for the automotive and energy storage sectors, serving the Moroccan market and the African continent, along with Europe, the Middle East, and the United States. Construction began in September 2025 after earthworks, and the buildings and infrastructure of the cell plant were completed in 13 months. According to GPM, that timeline ranks the project among the fastest industrial builds of its kind internationally. The work relied on a logistics operation of a scale new to Moroccan industry, with several thousand containers shipped from China to move production lines and high-technology equipment to Kenitra, backed by port and customs authorities. “The startup of the equipment on October 20 is only a first step in the rollout of a unique and promising project, meant to durably structure Morocco’s battery industrial ecosystem,” Qalam noted. He tied the plant to “the kingdom’s sovereignty in the field of green energy.” GPM has so far recruited more than 400 Moroccan employees, among them engineers, technicians, operators, and support staff. Most trained in China at Gotion High-Tech production sites, then worked alongside group experts in Kenitra. At full development, the gigafactory will create more than 2,300 direct jobs. The first phase targets 20 GWh of cells, battery packs, and energy storage systems, plus 100,000 tons of cathode materials. The project advanced further on September 28, when Volkswagen, a Gotion High-Tech shareholder, joined the Chinese group in announcing a Kenitra joint venture for cathode materials. That venture forms part of a broader Gotion-Volkswagen plan to invest about €3.22 billion ($3.67 billion) across battery and materials projects in Europe and North Africa, split between roughly €1.6 billion from Gotion and €1.62 billion from PowerCo, Volkswagen’s battery unit. The companies plan joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia, and Morocco, with the Kenitra cathode project set at about €480 million and 100,000 metric tons a year, prioritizing supplies to the two European battery plants. Gotion will control the Moroccan venture with a 51% stake, and PowerCo will hold 49%. Financing arrived earlier in the year. On July 24, the African Development Bank (AfDB) approved a €100 million loan to GPM for the integrated LFP gigafactory, with plans to mobilize up to €141 million more from partners. The bank described a first phase of 10 GWh scaling toward 100 GWh, and projected more than 600 direct jobs and a 70% local industrial integration rate. Gotion ranked fifth among global EV battery makers over the first seven months of 2026, with installations of 34.0 GWh, up 44.2% from a year earlier.

Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h do dia do concurso, em lotéricas credenciadas, na internet ou no app
Por O Globo — Rio de Janeiro
Atualizado
A Caixa Econômica Federal não realizará o sorteio da Mega-Sena nesta terça-feira (13), como de costume. O sorteio do concurso 3.070 da Mega-Sena, com um prêmio estimado em R$ 150 milhões, será então realizado na quarta-feira (14). Os sorteios da loteria ocorrem às 21h, no Espaço da Sorte, em São Paulo (SP), e contam com transmissão ao vivo pelas redes sociais da instituição e do g1.

Na próxima quinta-feira (15), também não haverá sorteio. O concurso 3.071 está marcado para o domingo, dia 18.
Como apostar na Mega-Sena
O palpite mínimo para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6,00. Além desse modelo de aposta, com seis números selecionados, que paga o prêmio principal, ainda é possível ganhar prêmios ao acertar quatro ou cinco dezenas.

artigo.texto: O exército russo bombardeou dois prédios em Sloviansk e armazéns em Kiev: quatro feridos e desaparecidos sob escombros. Drones ucranianos atingem centro de dados da Yandex em Vladímir, provocando falhas, sem vítimas. Na manhã deste domingo, o exército russo atacou dois blocos de apartamentos em Sloviansk, na região de Donetsk. “Neste momento há registo de quatro feridos”, declarou o presidente da câmara da cidade, Vadym Liakh. “Todos estão a receber assistência médica”. Debaixo dos escombros poderão ainda estar pessoas, afirmou por seu lado o presidente Volodymyr Zelensky. Em Bucha, nos arredores de Kiev, um ataque russo durante a noite deixou um conjunto de armazéns de uma empresa industrial a arder. Na tarde de domingo, as equipas de bombeiros continuavam a combater o incêndio. Um paramédico e um condutor ficaram feridos depois de um drone russo atingir uma ambulância na região de Sumy. Segundo o chefe da administração militar regional, Oleg Hryhorov, os profissionais de saúde conseguiram sair sozinhos do veículo danificado. Em várias regiões da Ucrânia, devido à situação difícil no setor energético causada pelos bombardeamentos russos, foram introduzidos no domingo cortes de emergência de eletricidade, informou o serviço de imprensa da NEC “Ukrenergo”. Os horários anteriormente divulgados para cortes de eletricidade por horas estão atualmente suspensos. Os cortes de emergência serão levantados depois de estabilizada a situação no sistema energético. Drones atacam terceiro centro de dados da Yandex em Vladímir, na Rússia Drones ucranianos atacaram na noite de sábado para domingo o centro de dados da Yandex em Vladímir. A empresa informou que a infraestrutura do centro foi danificada e que a sua atividade está totalmente interrompida. Até ao momento não há registo de feridos na sequência do ataque. A Yandex acrescentou que continua a avaliar o estado da infraestrutura e que, para já, não pode indicar prazos para a reposição dos equipamentos. Este é já o terceiro centro de dados da empresa atacado em outubro. O governador Aleksandr Avdeev confirmou o ataque de drones em Vladímir e o incêndio que se seguiu. Segundo o responsável, foi possível evitar danos na zona residencial. Os moradores foram retirados das casas mais próximas do local do ataque. Em Vladímir foram desligadas duas subestações que fornecem eletricidade a 5000 residentes. Uma hora depois, o governador informou que o fornecimento de eletricidade estava restabelecido em 80% e o de aquecimento e água em 100%. Segundo dados preliminares, foi atingido um supercomputador localizado no centro de dados de Vladímir. Um equipamento idêntico está instalado no centro de dados da Yandex em Riazan, que também foi alvo de ataque. Na sequência do ataque, os utilizadores enfrentaram falhas generalizadas nos serviços da empresa. Em Moscovo, São Petersburgo, Perm, Krasnoiarsk, Vladivostoque, Ulan-Ude, Ecaterimburgo e outras cidades russas não é possível chamar táxi através da aplicação. Problemas semelhantes foram registados na Sérbia, Cazaquistão, Bielorrússia e Arménia. Motoristas referem que não conseguem entrar na aplicação ou se deparam com falhas na navegação, enquanto o serviço indica aos passageiros que não há viaturas disponíveis. Há também registo de perturbações em muitos outros serviços da empresa. A 9 de outubro, drones atacaram o centro de dados da Yandex em Kaluga. Na manhã de 8 de outubro, as Forças Armadas da Ucrânia atingiram um centro de dados da Yandex perto de Riazan. Após esses ataques, começaram falhas nos sistemas internos de grandes empresas russas. Os sites de vários grandes meios de comunicação russos também deixaram de carregar. Canais ucranianos de monitorização relatam ataques, no domingo, contra uma ponte ferroviária basculante em Rostov-do-Don. As autoridades regionais ainda não comentaram o incidente. No início de outubro, a Rússia lançou repetidos ataques contra pontes estratégicas em Kiev. Segundo revelava o jornal The Telegraph, perante reveses militares, Vladimir Putin decidiu passar a atacar infraestruturas críticas da Ucrânia e pontes em Kiev. O centro operacional da região de Krasnodar informou que “fragmentos de drones” caíram na área do aeroporto de Sochi. Um dos edifícios administrativos foi atingido por um incêndio, sem registo de feridos. Destroços caíram também em zonas residenciais. O Ministério russo da Defesa afirmou que, durante a noite, as forças de defesa antiaérea abateram 479 drones ucranianos sobre 17 regiões da Rússia e a Crimeia anexada.

artigo.texto: BOSTON, Sept. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Factorial Energy Inc. (“Factorial”) (Nasdaq: FAC), a global leader in solid-state battery technology, today announced a strategic partnership with Mitsui Kinzoku Company, Limited to support the industrialization of its Solstice™ all-solid-state battery platform. Mitsui Kinzoku is a leading producer of sulfide-based solid electrolytes for all-solid-state batteries, one of few companies worldwide with foundational technology in this space, and already the global leader in ultra-thin copper foil, with an estimated 90% share of the semiconductor market for that foil. That materials science expertise underpins its A-SOLiD™ sulfide solid electrolyte, unveiled in 2016 and advancing toward mass production at a dedicated plant in Saitama, Japan. "I am very pleased that we have been able to enter into this joint development agreement with Factorial," said Dr. Kiyotaka Yasuda, Senior Executive Officer, General Manager, Business Creation Division of Mitsui Kinzoku Company, Limited. "Batteries are a key technology for realizing an electrified society, but significant technical challenges still remain. That is precisely why we believe it is necessary to go beyond the extension of existing technologies and take on the challenge of creating new value. By leveraging Mitsui Kinzoku's long-established expertise in materials and manufacturing technologies and combining it with Factorial's advanced technological capabilities, we aim to accelerate the realization of next-generation batteries." Factorial remains the fabless innovator across the platform, leading cell design, process development, supply chain qualification, line integration, and manufacturing validation. “Battery innovation can't be done by one single company," said Siyu Huang, CEO of Factorial. "It's driven by the entire supply chain and, increasingly, by an entire industry coalition. Mitsui Kinzoku's foundational electrolyte technology brings critical materials expertise to our work to move Solstice™ toward commercial deployment. We're not just building a battery. We're building the connective thread that helps the whole industry move forward together.” As robotics, aerospace systems, and AI-enabled infrastructure ask more of the physical world, energy is fast becoming the defining constraint on what's possible. Factorial calls this the emergence of the energy layer - the battery infrastructure needed to power the next era of mobility, aerospace and physical intelligence. Built for that layer, Solstice™, Factorial's sulfide-based all-solid-state battery platform, delivers high energy density and improved thermal stability, with proprietary dry-cathode processing enabling more cost-effective manufacturing. This collaboration builds on Factorial's recent momentum, including strategic investments from IQT and POSCO Future M; its first commercial orders for passenger vehicles in January and for aerospace in July; expanded automotive and industrialization partnership programs; and its June 2026 Nasdaq listing under the ticker symbol FAC. Factorial Energy (Nasdaq: FAC) is a leading American solid-state battery innovator backed by IQT – the not-for-profit strategic investor for the U.S. national security community and America’s allies – and Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, Hyundai, and Kia. Through its proprietary FEST® and Solstice™ platforms, engineered for scalable manufacturing, Factorial delivers industry-leading performance across aerospace, energy storage and mobility applications. In 2026, Factorial's initial drone flight test achieved 30% longer range, and the company secured its first commercial orders in both aerospace and passenger vehicle applications. In automotive, Mercedes-Benz’ real-world road testing in a lightly modified test vehicle achieved over 1,200 km of range on a single charge, with the technology also successfully integrated into a fully built Dodge Charger Daytona demonstration vehicle in partnership with Stellantis.. For more information, visit www.factorialenergy.com. Mitsui Kinzoku is a Japan-based global materials company and a leading manufacturer of non-ferrous metals and advanced materials, providing innovative solutions primarily for the automotive and electronics industries. Leveraging its core strengths in non-ferrous metals, functional materials, and recycling technologies, the company develops and manufactures a wide range of high-performance products, including automotive components, semiconductor materials, battery materials, and engineered materials. With a strong focus on innovation, environmental responsibility, and resource circulation, Mitsui Kinzoku collaborates with partners around the world to create new value and will continue to contribute to the realization of a sustainable society.
